Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 21, verse 1–2:

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿The reckoning of the people has drawn near to them, while they are heedless, turning away (1)﴾

Its meaning, He, the Exalted, says: The reckoning of people for their deeds that they did in their worldly life has drawn near, and for the blessings He bestowed upon them therein, in their bodies, their physical forms, their foods, their drinks, their clothing, and other of His blessings upon them, and His questioning them about what they did with them: whether they obeyed Him in them, complying with His command and prohibition regarding all of them, or disobeyed Him by opposing His command regarding them. ﴿And they are heedless, turning away﴾ means: while they are in the world, unaware of what Allah will do to them on the Day of Resurrection, and of the nearness of His reckoning them, and His drawing near to them, in forgetfulness and heedlessness, and they have turned away from that, neglecting to reflect upon it, to prepare for it, and to make ready for it, out of ignorance of what they will face at that time of great trial and severe terrors.

In accordance with what we have said regarding the interpretation of His saying ﴿while they are heedless, turning away﴾, the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have spoken, and a report has come from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

Mention of those who said that:

* Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, he said: Abu al-Walid narrated to us, he said: Abu Mu'awiya narrated to me, he said: al-A'mash informed us, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayra, from the Prophet (ﷺ) regarding ﴿while they are heedless, turning away﴾, he said: "In the world."

* *

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿No reminder comes to them from their Lord, newly revealed, but they listen to it while playing (2)﴾

Its meaning, He, the Exalted, says: Whatever new reminder of this Qur'an Allah sends down to the people, admonishing and advising them with it, they only listen to it while they are playing, their hearts being distracted.

In accordance with what we have said regarding the interpretation of that, the people of interpretation have spoken.

Mention of those who said that:

* Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada regarding His saying ﴿No reminder comes to them from their Lord, newly revealed﴾ ... the verse, he said: No part of the Qur'an is sent down to them except that they listen to it while playing.

The commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 21, verse 3:

The explanation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿Their hearts are heedless﴾ [distracted, inattentive]. He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: ﴿Their hearts are heedless﴾ means unmindful. That is, these people, whose description has been given, listen to this Qur'an only while playing, their hearts heedless of it. They do not ponder its judgments or reflect on the proofs God has placed in it against them.

As follows:

⁕ Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, concerning His words ﴿Their hearts are heedless﴾, he said: their hearts are unmindful.

* *

As for His words ﴿And they conceal their private consultation, those who did wrong﴾:

That is, these people, of whom the Reckoning has drawn near while they are heedless and turning away, with hearts distracted, conceal their private consultation among themselves. That is, they openly made their secret counsel among themselves, saying: "Is this one, who claims to be a messenger sent to you by God, anything but a human being like you?" They say: "He is merely a man like you in form and creation." By this they mean Muhammad (ﷺ). And "those who did wrong" describes them as wrongdoers, by their deeds and their words which He reports about them in these verses, which are their conduct and speech in turning away from the remembrance of God and denying His Messenger.

Regarding the i'rab (grammatical analysis) of His words ﴿those who did wrong﴾, there are two possibilities. The first is the genitive (khafd), as a qualifier following "the people" in His words "The Reckoning of mankind has drawn near" (iqtaraba lil-nasi hisabuhum). The second is the nominative (raf'), by way of referring back to the subject of the verb in His words "they conceal" (wa asarru), which is the pronoun referring to "the people," as is said in ﴿Then they became blind and deaf, many of them﴾. It may also be nominative as a beginning (mubtada'), meaning: "And they conceal the private consultation," and then He says: "They are those who did wrong."

* *

As for His words ﴿Will you then approach magic while you see?﴾:

That is, they made this statement openly among themselves, and it was the private consultation they had concealed among themselves. Some of them said to others: "Will you accept magic and believe in it, while you know that it is magic?" By this they mean the Qur'an.

As follows:

⁕ Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His words ﴿Will you then approach magic while you see?﴾, he said: The people of disbelief said to their Prophet, concerning what he had brought from God, they claimed that he was a sorcerer and that what he brought was magic. They said: "Will you approach magic while you see?"

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 21, verse 4–5:

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿He said, "My Lord knows every word in the heavens and the earth, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing."﴾ (4)

The reciters differed over the reading of His words ﴿Qul rabbi﴾. The majority of the reciters of Madinah and Basrah, and some of the Kufans, read ﴿Qul rabbi﴾ in the imperative mood ("Say, my Lord..."), while some of the reciters of Makkah and the majority of the reciters of Kufah read ﴿Qala rabbi﴾ in the indicative mood ("He said, my Lord...").

It appears that those who read it in the imperative mood intended by its interpretation: Say, O Muhammad, to those who say ﴿Do you then approach magic while you see?﴾: "My Lord knows the speech of every speaker in the heavens and the earth; nothing of it is hidden from Him, and He is the All-Hearing of all of it, and of what they say of falsehood, the All-Knowing of my truthfulness and the reality of what I call you to, and the falsity of what you say, and other than that of all things." And it appears that those who read it in the indicative mood intended: Muhammad said, "My Lord knows the speech," as a report from God about the answer of His Prophet to them.

The view on this is that both are well-known readings among the regional reading traditions, each of them was recited by scholars of the reciters, and both are found in the codices of the Muslims with the same meaning. This is because when God commands Muhammad to say that, he says it, and when he says it, he says it by the command of God. So whichever of the two readings the reader recites, he is correct in his recitation.

* *

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿Nay, they say, "Confused dreams! Nay, he has invented it! Nay, he is a poet! Let him then bring us a sign, as the earlier messengers were sent."﴾ (5)

He, the Exalted, says: They did not affirm the wisdom of this Qur'an, nor that it is from God, nor did they acknowledge that it is a revelation which God revealed to Muhammad ﷺ. Rather, some of them said: it is the confused images of a dream he saw in sleep. Some of them said: it is a fabrication and invention which he invented from himself. Some of them said: rather, Muhammad is a poet, and what he has brought you is poetry. ﴿Let him then bring us﴾ means: they said, let Muhammad bring us, if he is truthful in his saying, that God has sent him as a messenger to us, and that what he recites to us is a revelation from God revealed to us. ﴿A sign﴾ means: a proof and evidence of the truth of what he says and claims. ﴿As the earlier messengers were sent﴾ means: as the earlier messengers before him brought, such as raising the dead, healing the blind and the leper, the she-camel of Salih, and what is similar to that of the miracles which none can do except God and which none brings except the prophets and messengers.

The people of interpretation said things similar to what we have said.

Mention of those who said that:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words ﴿confused dreams﴾: that is, the deed of a dreamer; it is only a dream he saw. ﴿Nay, he has invented it! Nay, he is a poet!﴾ All of this had been said by them.

* *

And His words ﴿Let him then bring us a sign, as the earlier messengers were sent﴾:

He says: as Jesus brought clear signs, and Moses brought clear signs, and the messengers.

Ali narrated to me, saying: Abdullah narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words ﴿confused dreams﴾, he said: "mushtabihah" (confused, intermingled).

Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us, and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa narrated to us, all of them, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿confused dreams﴾, he said: its confusions (ahawil).

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij, from Mujahid, the same.

And He, the Exalted, said: "Bal qalu" (Nay, they said). There is no explicit denial in the speech which would be confirmed by "bal," because the report concerns people of denial and rejection; the hearers' knowledge of what His words indicate, through mention of the report about them, suffices, as we have explained.

The Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 21, verse 6:

On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿No town before them that We destroyed believed. Will they then believe?﴾

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: No one from among the polytheists of his people who said, "Let Muhammad bring us a sign just as the messengers before him brought," believed before these deniers, from the people of a town that We punished with destruction in this world when Our messenger came to them with a miraculous sign. ﴿Will they then believe?﴾ meaning: Will these deniers who call Muhammad a liar and ask him for a sign believe if a sign comes to them, when their predecessors from the bygone nations, whom We destroyed through their messengers despite the coming of the signs, did not believe before them?

And in accordance with what we have said on this, the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said.

Those who said that:

Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿We destroyed; will they then believe?﴾: "They will believe in that," meaning they will affirm it.

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, the like of it.

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding His words ﴿No town before them that We destroyed believed. Will they then believe?﴾: That is, the messengers, when they came to their peoples with clear proofs and they did not believe, were not given respite (lam yunadharu).

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 21, verse 7:

The interpretation of His saying, ﴿And We sent not before you except men to whom We revealed; so ask the people of the Reminder if you do not know﴾ [21:7].

He, may He be exalted, says to His Prophet: "And We did not send before you, O Muhammad, any messenger to a nation of the nations that passed before your nation, except men like them to whom We revealed what We wished to reveal to them of Our command and Our prohibition, not angels. So what do they deny of Our sending you to them, when you are a man like the other messengers before you who were sent to their peoples?"

* *

And His saying, ﴿so ask the people of the Reminder if you do not know﴾.

He says to those who said to Muhammad ﷺ in their secret conferences among themselves: "Is this anything but a human like you? So if you deny and are ignorant of the matter of the messengers who came before Muhammad, and you do not know, O people, whether they were humans or angels, then ask the people of the Books, of the Torah and the Gospel, what they used to tell you about them."

As related:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿so ask the people of the Reminder if you do not know﴾, he said: "Ask the people of the Torah and the Gospel." Abu Ja'far said: "I think that he [Qatadah] said: 'They will tell you that the messengers were men who ate food and walked in the markets.'" It was also said: "The people of the Reminder are the people of the Qur'an."

Mention of those who said that:

Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Tusi narrated to me, saying: Abd al-Rahman ibn Salih narrated to me, saying: Musa ibn Uthman narrated to me, from Jabir al-Ju'fi, who said: "When ﴿so ask the people of the Reminder if you do not know﴾ was revealed, Ali said: 'We are the people of the Reminder.'"

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿so ask the people of the Reminder if you do not know﴾: "They are the people of the Qur'an, and the Reminder is the Qur'an." And he recited: ﴿Indeed, We have sent down the Reminder, and indeed We will be its guardian﴾ [15:9].

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 21, verse 8:

The interpretation of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And We did not make them bodies that do not eat food, nor were they immortal﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: And We did not make the messengers whom We sent before you, O Muhammad, to the earlier nations before your community, ﴿bodies that do not eat food﴾. That is, We did not make them angels who do not eat food; rather, We made them bodies like you who eat food.

As related:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿And We did not make them bodies that do not eat food﴾: that is, We did not make them bodies except that they would eat food.

I was told on the authority of al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His saying ﴿And We did not make them bodies that do not eat food﴾: that is, We did not make them bodies without spirits that do not eat food; rather, We made them bodies in which there are spirits that eat food.

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: He said ﴿bodies﴾ in the singular, and made it a singular noun, although it describes a group. This is permissible because "jasad" (body) here carries the sense of a verbal noun, as one says in speech: "And We did not make them a creation (khalq) that does not eat."

* *

As for His saying ﴿and they were not immortal﴾:

That is: nor were they lords who do not die and do not perish; rather, they were humans, bodies, and they died. This is because they said to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, as Allah has reported of them: ﴿We will not believe you until you cause a spring to gush forth for us from the earth...﴾ up to His saying ﴿or you bring Allah and the angels before us as a guarantee﴾. Allah, blessed and exalted, said to them: We did not do that to anyone before you, so that We would do it to you; rather, We used to send to them men to whom We revealed, just as We sent to you a Messenger to whom We revealed Our command and Our prohibition.

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) said things similar to what we have said on this matter.

Those who said this:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿and they were not immortal﴾: that is, there is no escape for them from death; they must die.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 21, verse 9:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Then We fulfilled the promise to them, and We saved them and whom We willed, and We destroyed the transgressors﴾ (21:9).

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: Then We made true Our promise to Our messengers whom their peoples denied and whom they asked for signs. So We gave them what they asked for, then they persisted in their denial of it and insisted on rejecting its prophethood after the signs of their Lord had come to them. We fulfilled what We had promised them of destruction for their persistence in disbelief in their Lord after the sign they had asked for had come. This is like His saying, majestic is His praise: ﴿Whoever among you disbelieves after that, I will surely punish him with a punishment I will not inflict upon anyone among the worlds﴾ (5:115), and like His saying: ﴿And do not touch them with harm, lest there seize you the punishment of a near day﴾ (11:64), and similar to that of the threats which He made to the nations along with the coming of the signs. As for His saying, ﴿So We saved them﴾, He, exalted is His remembrance, says: We saved the messengers when their peoples persisted in denying them after the signs. ﴿And whom We willed﴾, namely their followers who believed them and affirmed them. As for His saying, ﴿And We destroyed the transgressors﴾, He, exalted is His remembrance, says: And We destroyed those who transgressed against themselves by their disbelief in their Lord.

As related:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿and We destroyed the transgressors﴾: the transgressors are the polytheists.

Commentary on the interpretation of His words, the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, We have sent down to you a Book in which is your reminder. Will you not then use reason?﴾ (21:10)

Interpreters of the Qur'an (ahl al-ta'wil) differed regarding the meaning of this. Some of them said: its meaning is, "Indeed, We have sent down to you a Book in which is your reminder," meaning in it is your report (hadith), your news.

Those who said this:

- Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿in it is your reminder﴾, he said: "Your report (hadith)."

- al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, ﴿Indeed, We have sent down to you a Book in which is your reminder﴾, he said: "Your report (hadith)." ﴿Will you not then use reason?﴾, he said: "In [the verse] 'Qad aflaha' (surely he has succeeded)." ﴿But We have brought them their reminder, yet they, from their reminder, are turning away﴾.

- al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Sufyan said: "The Qur'an was sent down with noble character. Have you not heard Him say: ﴿Indeed, We have sent down to you a Book in which is your reminder. Will you not then use reason?﴾"

Others said: rather, by "reminder" in this place is meant honour (sharaf), and they said: the meaning of the speech is, "Indeed, We have sent down to you a Book in which is your honour."

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: This second view is closer to the meaning of the word, and it is similar to what Sufyan said which we have related from him; for it is an honour for whoever follows it and acts by what is in it.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 21, verses 11–12:

The interpretation of His saying, ﴿And how many a town did We shatter, which had been wrongdoing, and raised up after it another people﴾ (11) ﴿So when they perceived Our might, behold, they were fleeing from it﴾ (12).

His saying, may His remembrance be exalted: "And how many a town did We shatter" — al-qasm (shattering) is originally breaking. It is said of it: "I shattered the back of so-and-so" when you broke it, and "his tooth was shattered" when it broke. Here it means "We destroyed," and the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) explained it in this way.

Those who said so:

⁕ Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim told us, saying: Isa told us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan told us, saying: Warqa' told us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying, ﴿And how many did We shatter﴾, he said: "We destroyed."

⁕ al-Qasim told us, saying: al-Husayn told us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, regarding His saying, ﴿And how many a town did We shatter﴾, he said: "We destroyed it." Ibn Jurayj said: "We shattered a town" — he said: "In Yemen We shattered; by the sword they were destroyed."

⁕ Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding the saying of Allah, ﴿We shattered a town﴾: "Shattering it means destroying it."

* *

As for His saying, ﴿a town which had been wrongdoing﴾:

The discourse is addressed to the town, while what is meant is its people, since the listeners know its meaning. It seems that its wrongdoing was its disbelief in Allah and its denial of His messengers. As for His saying, ﴿and raised up after it another people﴾, He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: We brought into being, after We destroyed these wrongdoers of this town which We shattered for its wrongdoing, another people other than them.

* *

As for His saying, ﴿So when they perceived Our might﴾:

It means: when they witnessed Our punishment having descended upon them, and saw it, and felt its touch. It is said of it: "I perceived weakness in so-and-so" and "I perceived it from him." ﴿Behold, they were fleeing from it﴾ means: when they perceived Our punishment descending upon them, they fled swiftly and hastily, running away in defeat. It is said of it: "So-and-so spurred his horse" when he drove it hard in its pace (al-rakd: to drive a horse at speed).

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 21, verses 11–12:

The interpretation of His saying, ﴿And how many a town did We shatter, which had been wrongdoing, and raised up after it another people﴾ (11) ﴿So when they perceived Our might, behold, they were fleeing from it﴾ (12).

His saying, may His remembrance be exalted: "And how many a town did We shatter" — al-qasm (shattering) is originally breaking. It is said of it: "I shattered the back of so-and-so" when you broke it, and "his tooth was shattered" when it broke. Here it means "We destroyed," and the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) explained it in this way.

Those who said so:

⁕ Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim told us, saying: Isa told us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan told us, saying: Warqa' told us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying, ﴿And how many did We shatter﴾, he said: "We destroyed."

⁕ al-Qasim told us, saying: al-Husayn told us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, regarding His saying, ﴿And how many a town did We shatter﴾, he said: "We destroyed it." Ibn Jurayj said: "We shattered a town" — he said: "In Yemen We shattered; by the sword they were destroyed."

⁕ Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding the saying of Allah, ﴿We shattered a town﴾: "Shattering it means destroying it."

* *

As for His saying, ﴿a town which had been wrongdoing﴾:

The discourse is addressed to the town, while what is meant is its people, since the listeners know its meaning. It seems that its wrongdoing was its disbelief in Allah and its denial of His messengers. As for His saying, ﴿and raised up after it another people﴾, He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: We brought into being, after We destroyed these wrongdoers of this town which We shattered for its wrongdoing, another people other than them.

* *

As for His saying, ﴿So when they perceived Our might﴾:

It means: when they witnessed Our punishment having descended upon them, and saw it, and felt its touch. It is said of it: "I perceived weakness in so-and-so" and "I perceived it from him." ﴿Behold, they were fleeing from it﴾ means: when they perceived Our punishment descending upon them, they fled swiftly and hastily, running away in defeat. It is said of it: "So-and-so spurred his horse" when he drove it hard in its pace (al-rakd: to drive a horse at speed).

The interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿Do not flee, and return to that in which you were made affluent, and to your dwellings, that you may be questioned.﴾

His saying, may His remembrance be exalted: "Do not flee, and return to that in which you were made affluent" means: return to the comforts in which you were given ease of living, and to your dwellings.

As related:

⁕ Muhammad ibn Sa'd told me, he said: my father told me, he said: my paternal uncle told me, he said: my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words ﴿Do not flee, and return to that in which you were made affluent and to your dwellings, that you may be questioned﴾: he meant those upon whom the punishment descended in this world from among the nations who disobeyed God.

⁕ Muhammad ibn 'Amr told me, he said: Abu 'Asim told us, he said: 'Isa told us, and al-Harith told me, he said: al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa' told us, all of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Najih, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿Do not flee﴾: "Do not run away."

⁕ al-Qasim told us, he said: al-Husayn told us, he said: Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, the like of it.

⁕ Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Sa'id told us, on the authority of Qatadah regarding ﴿and return to that in which you were made affluent﴾: he said, "Return to your worldly life in which you were made affluent."

⁕ Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la told us, he said: Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Ma'mar, on the authority of Qatadah regarding ﴿and return to that in which you were made affluent﴾: he said, "To that in which you were made affluent of your worldly life."

The scholars of interpretation (ta'wil) differed regarding the meaning of His words ﴿that you may be questioned﴾. Some of them said: its meaning is: "that you may understand and comprehend through questioning."

Mention of those who said that:

⁕ Muhammad ibn 'Amr told me, he said: Abu 'Asim told us, he said: 'Isa told us, and al-Harith told me, he said: al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa' told us, all of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Najih, on the authority of Mujahid regarding His words ﴿that you may be questioned﴾: he said, "That you may gain understanding."

⁕ al-Qasim told us, he said: al-Husayn told us, he said: Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid ﴿that you may be questioned﴾: he said, "That you may gain understanding."

Others said: rather, its meaning is: "that you may be asked something of your worldly life, in a manner of mockery and derision."

Mention of those who said that:

⁕ Bishr told me, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Sa'id told us, on the authority of Qatadah ﴿that you may be questioned﴾: "In mockery of them."

⁕ Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la told me, he said: Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Ma'mar, on the authority of Qatadah ﴿that you may be questioned﴾: "About something of your worldly life, in mockery of them."

**The discourse on the interpretation (ta'wil) of the words of God, the Exalted:** ﴿They said, "Woe to us! Indeed, we were wrongdoers." So that remained their cry until We made them like harvested stalks, extinguished.﴾ (21:14–15)

God, may His remembrance be exalted, says: those whom God visited with His punishment because of their wrongdoing said, when God's punishment came down upon them, "Woe to us! Indeed, we were wrongdoers," meaning: by our disbelief in our Lord. "So that remained their cry," meaning: their cry did not cease, when God's punishment came to them because they had wronged themselves, "Woe to us! Indeed, we were wrongdoers," until God destroyed them, mowing them down with the sword as crops are mowed and cut off by sickles. As for His words ﴿extinguished﴾, He means: destroyed, their sparks put out and their movement stilled, so that they became ashes, as a fire dies down and is quenched.

What we have said on this matter is also what the people of ta'wil have said.

Those who said this:

• Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada, regarding His words ﴿So that remained their cry...﴾ to the end of the verse: When they saw the punishment and witnessed it, their only hijjira (constant refrain) was their saying ﴿Woe to us! Indeed, we were wrongdoers,﴾ until God destroyed them and annihilated them.

• Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada, regarding ﴿They said, "Woe to us! Indeed, we were wrongdoers. So that remained their cry until We made them like harvested stalks, extinguished."﴾ He means: until they perished.

Also:

• al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Juraij, who said: Ibn 'Abbas (said regarding) ﴿harvested stalks﴾: the harvest; ﴿extinguished﴾: the extinguishing of a fire when it is put out.

• Sa'id ibn al-Rabi' related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, who said: They were people of fortresses, and God sent Bukhtnasar (Nebuchadnezzar) against them. He sent to them an army, which killed them with the sword, and they had killed a prophet of theirs, so they were mowed down by the sword. This is His words ﴿So that remained their cry until We made them like harvested stalks, extinguished,﴾ by the sword.

**The discourse on the interpretation (ta'wil) of the words of God, the Exalted:** ﴿They said, "Woe to us! Indeed, we were wrongdoers." So that remained their cry until We made them like harvested stalks, extinguished.﴾ (21:14–15)

Indeed, we were wrongdoers," meaning: by our disbelief in our Lord. Indeed, we were wrongdoers," until God destroyed them, mowing them down with the sword as crops are mowed and cut off by sickles. Those who said this:

Indeed, we were wrongdoers,﴾ until God destroyed them and annihilated them.

Also:

• al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Juraij, who said: Ibn 'Abbas (said regarding) ﴿harvested stalks﴾: the harvest; ﴿extinguished﴾: the extinguishing of a fire when it is put out.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 21, verse 16:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We did not create the heavens and the earth and what is between them in play.﴾ (16)

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: ﴿And We did not create the heavens and the earth and what is between them﴾ except as a proof for you, O people, and so that you may take warning from all of that, and know that the One who arranged and created them has nothing like Him, that divinity belongs to Him alone, that worship is fitting for nothing other than Him, and that He did not create that in vain or as a game.

As narrated:

⁕ Bishr told us, saying: Yazid told us, saying: Sa'id told us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿And We did not create the heavens and the earth and what is between them in play﴾: He says, "We did not create them in vain or without purpose."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 21, verse 17:

The interpretation of His saying, ﴿Had We wished to take a pastime, We would have taken it from Ourselves, if We were to do [it]﴾

His saying, may He be remembered, means: Had We wished to take a wife and a son, We would have taken that from Ourselves. But We do not do that, and it is not fitting for Us or proper for Us to do it, because it is not proper for God to have a son or a consort.

Those who interpret the Qur'an have said something similar to what we have said on this.

Mention of those who said that:

Muhammad ibn Sulayman ibn Ubayd Allah al-Ghaydani narrated to me, saying: Abu Qutaybah narrated to us, saying: Salam ibn Miskin narrated to us, saying: Uqbah ibn Abi Hamzah narrated to us, saying: I witnessed al-Hasan in Mecca. Tawus, ʿAta' and Mujahid came to him and asked him about the saying of God, blessed and exalted, ﴿Had We wished to take a pastime, We would have taken﴾. Al-Hasan said: The pastime is the woman.

Sa'id ibn Amr al-Sukuni narrated to me, saying: Baqiyyah ibn al-Walid narrated to us, from Ali ibn Harun, from Muhammad, from Layth, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿Had We wished to take a pastime﴾: He said: A wife.

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿Had We wished to take a pastime﴾ ... the verse: that is, that this would not occur and is not fitting. And "al-lahw" in the dialect of the people of Yemen means: the woman.

Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah: ﴿Had We wished to take a pastime﴾ He said: "al-lahw" in some dialect of the people of Yemen means: the woman. ﴿We would have taken it from Ourselves﴾.

And His saying ﴿if We were to do [it]﴾

Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿if We were to do [it]﴾: he says: "What We were doing."

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij, who said: They said Mary is His consort and Jesus is His son. So He, blessed and exalted, said ﴿Had We wished to take a pastime﴾: women and a son, ﴿We would have taken it from Ourselves, if We were to do [it]﴾. He said: From Ourselves, and We did not create Paradise or Fire, nor death or resurrection or reckoning.

Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿We would have taken it from Ourselves﴾: from Ourselves, and We did not create Paradise or Fire, nor death or resurrection.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 21, verse 18:

The interpretation of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Nay, We hurl the truth against falsehood, and it crushes it, and behold, it vanishes. And woe to you for what you ascribe (to Him).﴾ (21:18)

His saying, may His remembrance be exalted: "But We send down the truth from Our presence, which is the Book of Allah and His revelation, against disbelief and its people, so that it crushes it," meaning: so that it destroys it, just as a man crushes another man by striking him on the head with a blow that reaches the brain. When a blow reaches the brain of the one struck, he has no life after it.

* *

As for His saying ﴿and behold, it vanishes﴾

He means: then it is destroyed and annihilated.

As related:

* Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, he said: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿and behold, it vanishes﴾, he said: "Destroyed."

* Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿and behold, it vanishes﴾, he said: "Gone."

The people of interpretation have said something similar to what we have said on this.

Those who said so:

* Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿Nay, We hurl the truth against falsehood, and it crushes it, and behold, it vanishes﴾: "The truth is the Book of Allah, the Qur'an, and falsehood is Iblis. It crushes him, and behold, he vanishes," i.e., he is gone.

* *

As for His saying ﴿And woe to you for what you ascribe﴾

He means: woe to you for describing your Lord with other than His attributes, and for your claim that He has taken a wife and a son, and for your slander against Him.

The people of interpretation have said something similar to what we have said on this, except that some of them said the meaning of "you ascribe" is "you lie."

Others said: the meaning of that is "you associate partners (with Him)." Although the wording differs, the meanings converge, because whoever ascribes to Allah a consort has lied in describing Him thus, and has associated partners with Him, and has described Him with other than His attributes. However, the most preferable expression by which the meanings of the Qur'an are conveyed is the one closest to the understanding of its hearers.

Those who said what we have said on this: Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿And woe to you for what you ascribe﴾, i.e., "you lie."

* al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij, regarding ﴿And woe to you for what you ascribe﴾, he said: "You associate partners." And regarding His saying ﴿what they ascribe﴾, he said: "They associate partners." He said: Mujahid said regarding ﴿He will requite them for their describing﴾, he said: "Their speech, which is falsehood in this matter."

The interpretation of His saying, ﴿And to Him belongs whoever is in the heavens and the earth. And those near Him are not too proud to worship Him, nor do they tire﴾.

Exalted is He, says God. How could it be permissible for God to take a plaything, when to Him belongs the dominion of all who are in the heavens and the earth, and those near Him among His creation are not too proud to worship Him nor weary of long service to Him? You know that no father enslaves his own child, nor his spouse, while everyone in the heavens and the earth is His servant. So how could He have a spouse or a child? That is, will you not reflect on the lies you invent against your Lord?

In line with what we have said on this matter, the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said.

Those who said this:

Ali narrated to us, saying: Abdullah narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿nor do they tire﴾: they do not return.

Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us, and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa narrated to us, all of them, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿nor do they tire﴾: they do not become exhausted.

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, the like of it.

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding His saying ﴿nor do they tire﴾: he said: they do not grow weary.

Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatada, regarding His saying: ﴿nor do they tire﴾: he said: they do not grow weary.

Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada, the like of it.

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿They are not too proud to worship Him, nor do they tire﴾: he said: "They do not tire, they are not wearied of that exhaustion," and he said: "nor do they grow slack, nor become bored." All of this has one meaning, though the wording differs, and it derives from their saying: a camel is ḥasīr when it becomes exhausted and stops; and from the verse of 'Alqama ibn 'Abda:

Among them are the carcasses of the exhausted (al-ḥasrā), their bones are white, and their hides are hard (ṣalīb).

[[The verse is by 'Alqama ibn 'Abda al-Tamimi, from a poem in which he praises al-Harith ibn Abi al-Harith ibn Abi Shamir al-Ghassani (Mukhtar al-Shi'r al-Jahili, with the commentary of Mustafa al-Saqqa, Mustafa al-Babi al-Halabi edition, p. 421; it is the twentieth verse of the poem). Al-ḥasrā: the plural of ḥasīr among beasts, meaning one that is worn out from travel and dies of exhaustion. Ṣalīb: dry, not tanned. The pronoun in "bihā" refers to the cave he entered, where he found remains of the beasts that had passed through it earlier, including bones and hides.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 21, verses 20–21:

The interpretation of His saying, ﴿They glorify Him night and day; they never tire﴾ (21:20) ﴿Or have they taken gods from the earth who raise the dead?﴾ (21:21)

He, may He be exalted and remembered, says: These who are with Him, the angels of their Lord, glorify Him night and day, never tiring of glorifying Him.

As reported:

* Ya'qub related to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah related to us, saying: Humayd informed us, from Ishaq ibn 'Abd Allah ibn al-Harith, from his father, that Ibn 'Abbas asked Ka'b about His saying: ﴿They glorify Him night and day; they never tire﴾ and ﴿They glorify Him night and day; they never grow weary﴾ [[The recitation "yusabbihuna lahu bi-al-layli wa-al-nahari wa-hum" ... etc.]] He said: Does your gaze grow weary? Does your breath grow weary? He said: No. He said: Then they have been inspired to glorify Him just as you have been inspired with the gaze and the breath.

* Al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Abu Mu'awiyah related to me, from Abu Ishaq al-Shaybani, from Hassan ibn Mukhariq, from 'Abd Allah ibn al-Harith, who said: I said to Ka'b al-Ahbar: ﴿They glorify Him night and day; they never tire﴾ Does not some mission or work occupy them? He said: O nephew, they have been given glorification just as you have been given breath. Do you not eat, drink, stand, sit, come and go while you breathe? I said: Yes. He said: Likewise, glorification has been given to them.

* Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman and Abu Dawud related to us, both saying: Imran al-Qattan related to us, from Qatadah, from Salim ibn Abi al-Ja'd, from Ma'dan ibn Abi Talhah, from 'Amr al-Bakali, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar, who said: Allah created ten parts. He made nine parts for the angels and one part for the rest of creation. Then He divided the angels into ten parts: nine parts glorify Him night and day, never tiring, and one part is for His messenger. He divided creation into ten parts: nine parts for the jinn and one part for the rest of the children of Adam. Then He divided the children of Adam into ten parts, and Ya'juj and Ma'juj were assigned nine parts and one part for the rest of the children of Adam.

* Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿They glorify Him night and day; they never tire﴾, he said: The angels who are with the Most Merciful do not disdain to worship Him, nor do they grow weary of it.

It has been mentioned to us that the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ), while sitting with his companions, said: "Do you hear what I hear?" They said: "We hear nothing, O Prophet of Allah." He said: "I hear the creaking of the heaven, and it has a right to creak. There is no spot of space in it the size of a palm but there is an angel in prostration or standing upon it."

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Or have they taken gods from the earth who raise the dead?﴾

He, may He be exalted and remembered, says: Have these polytheists taken gods from the earth who raise the dead? By His saying "they" he means the gods: these gods they have taken raise the dead, that is, they give life to the dead and raise up creation. But Allah is the One who gives life and causes death.

As reported:

* Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, saying: Isa related to me, [transmission marker "ḥ"] and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa' related to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿yunshirun﴾, he said: it means "yuhyun" (they give life).

* Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying: ﴿Or have they taken gods from the earth who raise the dead?﴾, he said: Is there among their gods anyone who gives life so that they raise the dead? And he recited the saying of Allah: ﴿Say: Who provides for you from the heaven and the earth?﴾ ... up to His saying ﴿What is the matter with you? How do you judge?﴾.

He divided creation into ten parts: nine parts for the jinn and one part for the rest of the children of Adam. Then He divided the children of Adam into ten parts, and Ya'juj and Ma'juj were assigned nine parts and one part for the rest of the children of Adam.

* Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿They glorify Him night and day; they never tire﴾, he said: The angels who are with the Most Merciful do not disdain to worship Him, nor do they grow weary of it.

It has been mentioned to us that the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ), while sitting with his companions, said: "Do you hear what I hear?" They said: "We hear nothing, O Prophet of Allah." He said: "I hear the creaking of the heaven, and it has a right to creak. There is no spot of space in it the size of a palm but there is an angel in prostration or standing upon it."

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Or have they taken gods from the earth who raise the dead?﴾

He, may He be exalted and remembered, says: Have these polytheists taken gods from the earth who raise the dead? By His saying "they" he means the gods: these gods they have taken raise the dead, that is, they give life to the dead and raise up creation. But Allah is the One who gives life and causes death.

As reported:

* Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, saying: Isa related to me, [transmission marker "ḥ"] and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa' related to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿yunshirun﴾, he said: it means "yuhyun" (they give life).

* Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying: ﴿Or have they taken gods from the earth who raise the dead?﴾, he said: Is there among their gods anyone who gives life so that they raise the dead? And he recited the saying of Allah: ﴿Say: Who provides for you from the heaven and the earth?﴾ ... up to His saying ﴿What is the matter with you? How do you judge?﴾.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 21, verses 22–23:

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿Had there been in them gods other than Allah, they would have been corrupted. Exalted is Allah, Lord of the Throne, above what they describe﴾ (21:22)

He, the Exalted, says: Had there been in the heavens and the earth gods fit to be worshipped besides Allah, who is the Creator of things, and to whom alone worship and divinity belong, which are fit for none but Him, ﴿they would have been corrupted﴾, meaning: the people of the heavens and the earth would have been corrupted. ﴿Exalted is Allah above what they describe﴾, meaning: His, the Majestic and Praised One's, is the glorification and the clearing of Him from the falsehood that these polytheists attribute to Him by ascribing partners to Him.

As related:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words ﴿Had there been in them gods other than Allah, they would have been corrupted. Exalted is Allah, Lord of the Throne, above what they describe﴾: He glorifies Himself when slander is spoken against Him.

* *

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿He is not questioned about what He does, but they will be questioned﴾ (21:23)

He, the Exalted, says: No questioner asks the Lord of the Throne about what He does with His creation, of their being turned over in life and death, honor and humiliation, and other of His judgments concerning them; because they are His creation and His servants, and all of them are under His dominion and authority, and the judgment is His, and the decree is His, and there is nothing above Him to question Him about what He does, so as to say to Him: Why did You do this? Why did You not do that? ﴿But they will be questioned﴾, meaning: His, the Majestic and Praised One's, is that all who are in the heavens and the earth among His servants will be questioned about their actions and held accountable for their deeds, and it is He who will question them about that and hold them accountable for it, for He is above them and their Owner, and they are under His authority.

Those of the interpreters said the same as what we have said concerning that.

Mention of those who said that:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words ﴿He is not questioned about what He does, but they will be questioned﴾: He is not questioned about what He does to His servants, and they are questioned about their deeds.

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij, who said, regarding His words ﴿He is not questioned about what He does, but they will be questioned﴾: The Creator is not questioned about His decree concerning His creation, while He questions the creation about their deeds.

It was related from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His words ﴿He is not questioned about what He does, but they will be questioned﴾: The Creator is not questioned about what He decrees concerning His creation, and the creatures are questioned about their deeds.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 21, verse 24:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Or have they taken gods besides Him? Say, "Bring your proof. This is the reminder of those with me and the reminder of those before me." But most of them do not know the truth, so they turn away.﴾ (21:24)

God, mighty and majestic is He, says: Have these polytheists taken gods besides God that benefit and harm, that create and give life and cause death? Say, O Muhammad, to them: "Bring your proof," meaning your argument. He means: Bring it, if you claim that you are right in your saying, a proof and evidence of your truthfulness.

As related:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿Say, "Bring your proof"﴾: he said: Bring your evidence for what you say.

* *

As for His saying ﴿This is the reminder of those with me﴾

He says: This which I have brought you from God, of the Qur'an and the revelation, ﴿is the reminder of those with me﴾, meaning: the news of those with me, of what they have of God's reward for their faith in Him and their obedience to Him, and what is upon them of God's punishment for their disobedience to Him and their disbelief in Him. ﴿And the reminder of those before me﴾ means: the news of those before me among the nations that passed before me, and what God did to them in this world, and what He will do to them in the Hereafter.

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said what is similar to what we have said regarding this.

Mention of those who said that:

Bishr narrated to me, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿This is the reminder of those with me﴾: he said: This Qur'an contains the mention of what is lawful and unlawful. ﴿And the reminder of those before me﴾: he said: the mention of the deeds of the past nations and what God did to them until they reached their state.

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, regarding ﴿This is the reminder of those with me﴾: he said: the account of those with me, and the account of those before me.

* *

As for His saying ﴿But most of them do not know the truth﴾

He says: But most of these polytheists do not know the right course in what they say or in what they do and abandon, so they turn away from the truth out of ignorance of it and lack of understanding.

Qatadah used to say about this what follows:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿But most of them do not know the truth, so they turn away﴾: from the Book of God.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 21, verse 25–27:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We did not send before you any messenger except that We revealed to him that there is no deity except Me, so worship Me﴾ (25)

His saying, exalted is His remembrance: And We did not send, O Muhammad, before you any messenger to any nation of the nations except that We revealed to him that there is no one worthy of worship in the heavens and the earth besides Me, so worship Me, meaning: devote worship sincerely to Me, and single out divinity for Me.

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said what is similar to what we have said regarding this.

Mention of those who said this:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying, ﴿And We did not send before you any messenger except that We revealed to him that there is no deity except Me, so worship Me﴾, he said: The messengers were sent with sincerity and monotheism. Nothing from them is accepted without the deed until they say it and affirm it, and the sharia'ahs differ: in the Torah there is a sharia, in the Gospel there is a sharia, and in the Qur'an there is a sharia, lawful and unlawful; but all of this concerns sincerity to Allah and His monotheism. Abu Ja'far said: I think he said "I suppose".

* *

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And they say, "The Most Merciful has taken a son." Glory be to Him! Rather, they are honoured servants. They do not precede Him in speech, and they act by His command﴾ (26–27)

His saying, exalted is His remembrance: And these disbelievers in their Lord said: "The Most Merciful has taken a son from His angels." So He, majestic is His praise, said, declaring it monstrous of what they said and disassociating Himself from what they attributed to Him, glory be to Him, meaning: exalting Himself above that, such is not among His attributes: ﴿Rather, they are honoured servants﴾, meaning: the angels are not as these disbelievers from the children of Adam have described them, but they are honoured servants, meaning: Allah has honoured them.

As:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying, ﴿And they say, "The Most Merciful has taken a son." Glory be to Him! Rather, they are honoured servants﴾, he said: The Jews said: Allah, blessed and exalted, has intermarried with the jinn, and from them came the angels. Allah, blessed and exalted, said, denying them and refuting them: ﴿Rather, they are honoured servants﴾, and the angels are not as they claimed; they are only servants whom Allah has honoured with His worship.

Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah; and al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah: ﴿And they say, "The Most Merciful has taken a son"﴾, the Jews and groups of people said: Allah, blessed and exalted, is related by marriage to the jinn, and the angels are from the jinn. Allah, blessed and exalted, said: ﴿Glory be to Him! Rather, they are honoured servants﴾. And His saying: ﴿They do not precede Him in speech﴾, meaning, He, majestic is His praise: they do not speak except what their Lord commands them, and they do no deed except by Him.

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, who said: Allah said: ﴿They do not precede Him in speech﴾, He praises them, ﴿and they act by His command﴾.
