**The interpretation of His words, Exalted is He: ﴿He knows what is before them and what is behind them, and they do not intercede except for one whom He approves, and they are, out of fear of Him, apprehensive.﴾ (21:28)**

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: He knows what is before His angels, meaning what they have not yet reached, what they will say and do, and what is behind them, meaning what has passed before today of the times and ages that they left behind, and what they did in it. All of that is recorded for them and against them, and nothing of it is hidden from Him.

What we have said on this matter is also the view of the people of ta'wil (interpretation of the Qur'an).

Mention of those who said this:

Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my paternal uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, concerning His words ﴿He knows what is before them and what is behind them﴾: he means He knows what they have advanced and what they have neglected of their deeds. ﴿And they do not intercede except for one whom He approves﴾: he means the angels do not intercede except for one with whom Allah is pleased.

What we have said on this matter is also the view of the people of ta'wil.

Mention of those who said this:

Ali related to me, saying: Abu Salih related to us, saying: Mu'awiya related to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, concerning His words ﴿and they do not intercede except for one whom He approves﴾: he means those for whom He approves the testimony that there is no god but Allah.

Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, saying: Abu Asim related to us, saying: Isa related to us, and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa related to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning His words ﴿except for one whom He approves﴾: he said: for one with whom He is pleased.

Al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, the same.

Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada, concerning His words ﴿and they do not intercede except for one whom He approves﴾: on the Day of Resurrection, ﴿and they are, out of fear of Him, apprehensive﴾.

Al-Hasan related to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatada, who said: they do not intercede on the Day of Resurrection.

Ibn Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada, the same. As for His words ﴿and they are, out of fear of Him, apprehensive﴾, he said: they are apprehensive out of fear of Allah and dread of His punishment descending upon them; he means they are wary lest they disobey Him and oppose His command and prohibition.

The explanation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And whoever among them should say, "Indeed, I am a deity besides Him," - then We would recompense him with Hell. Thus do We recompense the wrongdoers.﴾ (21:29)

Says He, exalted is His mention: And whoever among the angels should say, "Indeed, I am a deity besides Allah" - ﴿then that one who says that among them﴾ - ﴿We would recompense him with Hell﴾, meaning: We would reward him for his saying that with Hell. ﴿Thus do We recompense the wrongdoers﴾, meaning: Just as We recompense whoever among the angels says, "Indeed, I am a deity besides Allah," with Hell, so too do We recompense every one who wrongs himself, disbelieving in Allah and worshipping other than Him. It has also been said that this verse refers to Iblis, and those who say this argue: "We say that only because no one among the angels said, 'Indeed, I am a deity besides Allah,' other than him."

Mention of those who said that:

- Al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, regarding ﴿And whoever among them﴾: Ibn Jurayj said: "Whoever among the angels says, 'Indeed, I am a deity besides Him' - none said that except Iblis, who called to the worship of himself, so this verse was revealed concerning Iblis."

- Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿And whoever among them should say, "Indeed, I am a deity besides Him," - then We would recompense him with Hell. Thus do We recompense the wrongdoers﴾: "This verse was specific to the enemy of Allah, Iblis, when he said what he said, may Allah curse him and make him a repelled one (rajim), so He said, ﴿then We would recompense him with Hell. Thus do We recompense the wrongdoers﴾."

- Ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, he said: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿And whoever among them should say, "Indeed, I am a deity besides Him," - then We would recompense him with Hell﴾, he said: "It is specific to Iblis."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 21, verse 30:

The interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿Have not those who disbelieve seen that the heavens and the earth were a joined mass, and We parted them and made from water every living thing? Will they not then believe?﴾ (21:30)

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: Have not these who disbelieve in God looked with the sight of their hearts, so that they would see with it and know that the heavens and the earth were a joined mass? That is: there was no opening in them; rather, they were stuck together. It is said of this: "raqa Fulan al-fatq" (he sewed up the tear) when he tightened it, so he sews it up (yarququhu) with a sewing (raqqan) and stitching (ruqsan). From this comes the saying about a woman whose vagina is closed: raqqa'. The word "raq" (joined mass) is in the singular, although it describes the heavens and the earth, and it came after His words "kanata" (were) because it is a verbal noun (masdar), like "qawl al-zawr" (false speech), "al-sawm" (fasting) and "al-fitr" (breaking the fast).

* *

As for His words: ﴿fataqnahuma﴾

He says: We split them and opened them up.

Then the people of interpretation differed concerning the meaning of God's description of the heavens and the earth as joined, how the joining was, and in what sense the parting occurred. Some of them said: He meant by this that the heavens and the earth were stuck together, and God separated them with air.

Those who said this:

- Ali narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, concerning His words ﴿Have not those who disbelieve seen that the heavens and the earth were a joined mass﴾: he says: they were stuck together.

- Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, concerning His words ﴿Have not those who disbelieve seen that the heavens and the earth were a joined mass, and We parted them﴾ ... the verse: he says: they were stuck together, so He raised the sky and set down the earth.

- I was told on the authority of al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd ibn Sulayman informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say, concerning His words ﴿that the heavens and the earth were a joined mass, and We parted them﴾: Ibn Abbas used to say: they were stuck together, and God parted them.

- Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, ﴿that the heavens and the earth were a joined mass, and We parted them﴾: He said: al-Hasan and Qatada used to say: they were together, and God separated them with this air.

Others said: Rather, the meaning is that the heavens were a layered joined mass, and God parted them and made them seven heavens; likewise the earth was a joined mass and He parted it and made it seven earths.

Those who said this:

- Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning the saying of God, blessed and exalted: ﴿a joined mass, and We parted them﴾: from the earth six earths together with it, so that is seven earths together with it, and from the sky six heavens together with it, so that is seven heavens together with it. He said: the earth and the sky were not touching each other.

- Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, ﴿a joined mass, and We parted them﴾: he said: He parted them into seven heavens, some above others, and seven earths, some beneath others.

- al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij, from Mujahid, similar to the report of Muhammad ibn Amr from Abu Asim.

- Abd al-Hamid ibn Bayan narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Yazid informed us, from Isma'il, who said: I asked Abu Salih about His words ﴿were a joined mass, and We parted them﴾, and he said: the earth was joined and the heavens were joined, and from the sky He parted seven heavens, and from the earth seven earths.

- Musa narrated to us, saying: Amr narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, who said: It was one sky, then He parted it and made it seven heavens in two days, on Thursday and Friday, and Friday was so named because on it the creation of the heavens and the earth was gathered (jumma'a). That is the time of His saying ﴿He created the heavens and the earth in six days﴾, and His saying ﴿were a joined mass, and We parted them﴾.

Others said: Rather, He meant by this that the heavens were a joined mass, not raining, and the earth likewise was a joined mass, not growing plants; so He parted the sky with rain and the earth with plants.

Those who said this:

- Hannad narrated to us, saying: Abu al-Ahwas narrated to us, from Simak, from Ikrima, concerning ﴿Have not those who disbelieve seen that the heavens and the earth were a joined mass, and We parted them﴾: he said: they were a joined mass from which nothing came out, so He parted the sky with rain and parted the earth with plants. He said: this is His saying ﴿By the sky of the returning rain and the earth of the splitting open﴾ (86:11-12).

- al-Husayn ibn Ali al-Sada'i narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to us, from al-Fudayl ibn Marzuq, from Atiyya, concerning His words ﴿Have not those who disbelieve seen that the heavens and the earth were a joined mass, and We parted them﴾: he said: the sky was a joined mass that did not rain, and the earth was a joined mass that did not grow; He parted the sky with rain and parted the earth with plants, and made from water every living thing. Will they not then believe?

- Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His words ﴿Have not those who disbelieve seen that the heavens and the earth were a joined mass, and We parted them﴾: he said: the heavens were a joined mass from which no rain descended, and the earth was a joined mass from which no plant came out; God parted them, sent down the rain of the sky, split the earth and brought forth its plants, and he recited ﴿and We parted them, and made from water every living thing. Will they not then believe?﴾.

Others said: "fatiqnahuma" was said only because the night was before the day, and He parted off the day.

Those who said this:

- al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: al-Thawri informed us, from his father, from Ikrima, from Ibn Abbas, who said: the night was created before the day, then He said: they were a joined mass, and We parted them.

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: The most correct of these sayings is the saying of the one who said: the meaning is: Have not those who disbelieve seen that the heavens and the earth were a joined mass of rain and plants, and We parted the sky with rain and the earth with plants.

We say this is more correct because of the indication in His words ﴿and made from water every living thing﴾, and because He, exalted is His praise, did not follow that with describing the water in this way unless the preceding mention concerned its causes.

If someone says: If that is so, how is it said: "Have not those who disbelieve seen that the heavens and the earth were a joined mass," while rain only descends from the lowest heaven? It is answered: this is disputed; some have said it descends from the seventh heaven, and others from the fourth heaven. Even if it descends from the lowest heaven as you say, there is no evidence in His words ﴿that the heavens and the earth﴾ against what we have said, since it is not impossible to say "the heavens" meaning one of them, in the plural, because each piece of it is a sky, as one says "a worn cloak" (thawb akhlaq) and "a rag shirt" (qamis asmal).

If someone says: How is it said "the heavens and the earth were" (kanata), when "the heavens" is plural, and the rule for feminine plurals is to say "kunna" for few and "kanat" for many? It is answered: it is said this way because they are two kinds: the heavens are one type and the earth is another, and this is like the verse of al-Aswad ibn Ya'fur:

"Indeed death (al-maniyya) and calamities (al-hutuf), both of them ... cut off the passes (al-makharim), watching my person (sawadi)." [The poet says "yarqubani" in the dual, because he made death and calamities two kinds of destruction; if it followed the literal form he would have said "tarqubu sawadi."]

He said "kilahuma" (both), and mentioned death and calamities, as I have described, meaning the two kinds. I have been told on the authority of Abu Ubayda Mu'ammar ibn al-Muthanna, who said: Ghalib al-Nafili recited to me from al-Qutami:

"Does it not grieve you that the ties of Qays ... and Taghlib have separated, severed?" [The poet says "tabayanata" in the dual, though the ties of Qays are plural and the ties of Taghlib are plural, so the apparent form would call for "tabayanat."]

So he made the ties of Qays, a plural, and the ties of Taghlib, a plural, into a dual.

* *

As for His words: ﴿and We made from water every living thing﴾

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: We gave life, by the water We send down from the sky, to every thing.

As:

- Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada, ﴿and We made from water every living thing﴾: he said: every living thing was created from water.

If someone says: How is it that "every living thing" is specified as made from water, apart from other things? You know that plants, vegetation and trees are given life by water, and other things that have no life and are called neither living nor dead? It is answered: because none of those is without life and death, though its meaning differs in this respect from the meaning of animate beings, in that they have no spirits, while animate beings have spirits. Therefore it is said ﴿and We made from water every living thing﴾.

* *

As for His words: ﴿Will they not then believe?﴾

He says: Will they not then accept this as true, acknowledge the divinity of the One who did this, and single Him out for worship?

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 21, verse 31:

The interpretation of His saying, ﴿And We placed in the earth firm mountains, lest it should sway with them, and We placed therein broad roads as paths, that they might be guided.﴾

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: Do not these disbelievers also see, among Our proofs against them and against all of Our creation, that We placed in the earth mountains that are firmly set? Al-rawasi (the firmly set ones) is the plural of rasiyah, meaning that which is fixed and stable.

As related:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿And We placed in the earth firm mountains﴾: that is, mountains.

* *

As for His saying ﴿lest it should sway with them﴾:

It means: lest it should lurch with them. He, may His praise be exalted, says: We placed in this earth these firm mountains and fixed them, lest it should lurch with the people, and so that they could stand firmly upon its surface.

As related:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, who said: They were on the earth, which was swaying with them and not settled. Then in the morning God had made the mountains, which are the firm ones, into pegs for the earth. And ﴿We placed therein broad roads as paths﴾, meaning routes; its singular is fajj.

As related:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿We placed therein broad roads﴾: that is, landmarks.

* *

As for His saying ﴿as paths﴾:

That is, ways (turuq), and it is the plural of sabil (path).

Ibn Abbas, as it is reported from him, used to say: By His saying ﴿We placed therein broad roads﴾ He meant: We placed them among the firm mountains. So the ha' and alif in His saying ﴿We placed therein﴾ refer to the mountains.

As related to us by al-Qasim, who said: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij, who said: Ibn Abbas said, regarding His saying ﴿We placed therein broad roads﴾, "paths," he said: between the mountains.

We have chosen the other view in this matter, making the ha' and alif refer to the earth, because when they refer to the earth, both the plain and the mountain are included in it, for all of that is from the earth. God has made for His creatures broad roads as paths in all of that, and there is no indication showing that He meant by it the broad roads of only part of the earth which He made paths for them, to the exclusion of part. Therefore the generality of it is more appropriate.

* *

As for His saying ﴿that they might be guided﴾:

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: We made these broad roads in the earth so that they might be guided to travel in it.

The Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 21, verses 32–33:

On the interpretation of His words, the Exalted: ﴿And We made the sky a protected roof, yet they turn away from its signs (32). And it is He who created the night and the day, and the sun and the moon; each in an orbit is swimming (33).﴾

His saying, may His remembrance be exalted: ﴿And We made the sky a roof﴾ over the earth, raised high, and His saying ﴿protected﴾ means: We protected it from every accursed devil.

The interpreters of the Qur'an (ahl al-ta'wil) have said in accordance with what we have said.

Mention of those who said this:

Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, saying: Abu Asim related to us, saying: Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa' related to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿a protected roof﴾: he said, "Raised up."

al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Juraij, from Mujahid, the like of it.

Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada, regarding His words ﴿And We made the sky a protected roof﴾ ... the verse: a roof raised high, and a wave restrained.

* *

And His words: ﴿yet they turn away from its signs﴾

He says: these polytheists turn away from the signs of the sky. By its signs he means its sun, its moon and its stars. ﴿Turn away﴾ means they turn away from reflecting upon them and pondering the proofs of God against them that they contain, and their indication of the oneness of their Creator, and that worship should be directed only to the One who arranged and fashioned them, and that none is fit for it but Him.

The interpreters of the Qur'an have said in accordance with what we have said.

Mention of those who said this:

Muhammad ibn Amr related to us, saying: Abu Asim related to us, saying: Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa' related to us, all of them, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿yet they turn away from its signs﴾: he said, "The sun, the moon and the stars are the signs of the sky."

al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Juraij, from Mujahid, the like of it.

* *

And His words: ﴿And it is He who created the night and the day, and the sun and the moon; each in an orbit is swimming﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: And God is the One who created for you, O people, the night and the day, as a blessing from Him upon you and as a proof and indication of the greatness of His dominion, and that divinity belongs to Him alone to the exclusion of all else. They alternate for you for the good of your livelihoods and the affairs of your worldly life and your hereafter. And He created the sun and the moon likewise, ﴿each in an orbit is swimming﴾; He says: all of that is in an orbit, swimming.

The interpreters differed concerning the meaning of the orbit (falak) mentioned by God in this verse. Some of them said: it is like the shape of the millstone's iron disc.

Mention of those who said this:

Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, saying: Abu Asim related to us, saying: Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa' related to us, all of them, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿each in an orbit is swimming﴾: he said, "An orbit like the shape of the millstone's iron disc."

al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, saying: Ibn Juraij said: ﴿each in an orbit﴾: he said, "An orbit like the shape of the millstone's iron disc."

Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Jarir related to me, from Qabus ibn Abi Zabyan, from his father, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿each in an orbit is swimming﴾: he said, "The orbit of the sky."

Others said: rather, the orbit mentioned by God in this place is the speed of the running of the sun, the moon, the stars and others.

Mention of those who said this:

It was related to me from al-Husayn, saying: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His words ﴿each in an orbit is swimming﴾: "The falak is the running and the speed."

Others said: the falak is a restrained wave in which the sun, the moon and the stars run.

Others said: rather, it is the axis (qutb) around which the stars revolve, and the proponent of this view cited for his statement the verse of the rajaz poet:

"She spent the night conversing with the revolving axis, until morning, making the ropes [of the well] labour."

[The verse is evidence that the falak is the axis around which the stars revolve. In (Lisan al-Arab: falak) it is said: the falak is the orbit of the stars, its plural being aflak. In a hadith of Ibn Mas'ud, a man came to another man while he was sitting with him and said: "I left your horse as if it were revolving in a falak." Abu Ubayda said: regarding "in a falak," there are two views. As for what the common people know, it is a comparison with the falak of the sky upon which the stars revolve, which is called the qutb, likened to the axle of the millstone. He said: some Arabs said: the falak is the wave when it surges in the sea and churns, coming and going, so the horse in its agitation was likened to that.]

Others said regarding this, that:

Bishr related it to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada, regarding His words ﴿each in an orbit is swimming﴾: i.e., in the orbit of the sky.

Ibn Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada: ﴿each in an orbit is swimming﴾: he said, "It runs in the orbit of the sky as you have seen."

Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words ﴿each in an orbit is swimming﴾: "The falak is that which lies between the sky and the earth, from the courses of the stars, the sun and the moon." And he recited: ﴿Blessed is He who placed in the sky constellations and placed therein a lamp and a luminous moon﴾, and said: those constellations are between the sky and the earth and are not on the earth. ﴿Each in an orbit is swimming﴾: he said, "In the space between the sky and the earth: the stars, the sun and the moon."

It is related from al-Hasan that he used to say: the falak is a mill-wheel, like the shape of a spindle-whorl.

The correct view on this matter is to say, as God, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿each in an orbit is swimming﴾. It is permissible that this orbit is like what Mujahid said, like the iron disc of the millstone, and as related from al-Hasan, like the millstone wheel; and it is permissible that it is a restrained wave, and that it is the axis of the sky. That is because falak in the speech of the Arabs is every thing that revolves; its plural is aflak, and I have mentioned the verse of the rajaz poet:

"She spent the night conversing with the revolving falak..."

And since every thing that revolves is called falak in their speech, and there is no evidence in the Book of God, nor in a report from the Messenger of God (ﷺ), nor from anyone whose word is decisive, indicating which of these it is, it is obligatory that we say what He said and remain silent about what we have no knowledge of.

So if the correct view in this matter, in our opinion, is what we have mentioned, then the meaning of the speech is: and the sun and the moon, each in a revolving orbit, are swimming.

As for His words ﴿yasbahun﴾ (they swim), its meaning is: they run.

Mention of those who said this:

Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, saying: Abu Asim related to us, saying: Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa' related to us, all of them, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿each in an orbit is swimming﴾: he said, "They run."

al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, the like of it.

Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words ﴿yasbahun﴾: "They run."

It has been said: ﴿each in an orbit is swimming﴾, where the report about the sun and the moon is given in the form of a report about the sons of Adam, with the plural masculine ending of wa and nun, and it was not said "yaskhabna" or "tasbah," just as it was said: ﴿And the sun and the moon, I saw them prostrating to me﴾ [Yusuf 4], because prostration is among the actions of the sons of Adam; so when the sun and the moon were described with actions like theirs, the report about them was given the same form as the report about them.

The Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 21, verses 32–33:

On the interpretation of His words, the Exalted: ﴿And We made the sky a protected roof, yet they turn away from its signs (32). And it is He who created the night and the day, and the sun and the moon; each in an orbit is swimming (33).﴾

His saying, may His remembrance be exalted: ﴿And We made the sky a roof﴾ over the earth, raised high, and His saying ﴿protected﴾ means: We protected it from every accursed devil.

The interpreters of the Qur'an (ahl al-ta'wil) have said in accordance with what we have said.

Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, saying: Abu Asim related to us, saying: Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa' related to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿a protected roof﴾: he said, "Raised up."

Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, saying: Abu Asim related to us, saying: Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa' related to us, all of them, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿each in an orbit is swimming﴾: he said, "They run."

al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, the like of it.

Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words ﴿yasbahun﴾: "They run."

It has been said: ﴿each in an orbit is swimming﴾, where the report about the sun and the moon is given in the form of a report about the sons of Adam, with the plural masculine ending of wa and nun, and it was not said "yaskhabna" or "tasbah," just as it was said: ﴿And the sun and the moon, I saw them prostrating to me﴾ [Yusuf 4], because prostration is among the actions of the sons of Adam; so when the sun and the moon were described with actions like theirs, the report about them was given the same form as the report about them.

The Interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: "We did not grant to any human before you immortality. So if you die, will they be immortal? Every soul will taste death. And We test you with evil and with good as a trial. And to Us you will be returned."

His saying, exalted is He, to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): We did not make any human among the sons of Adam eternal in this world before you, O Muhammad, so that We would make you eternal in it. You too must die, just as Our messengers before you died. "So if you die, will they be immortal?" That is: will these polytheists, who associate others with their Lord, be immortal in the world after you? It is not so; rather they will die in every case, whether you live or die. The fa' (then) has been placed after in (if), which is a conditional particle, and in its answer, because the conditional is connected to the speech before it. It has also been placed in His saying "then they" because it is the answer to the conditional. Were the fa' not present in His saying "then they," it would be permissible in two ways: first, that it be omitted while still intended; second, that it be intended as moved forward to the conditional, so that it is as if He had said: "Will they be immortal if you die?"

* *

As for His saying, "Every soul will taste death."

He, exalted is He, says: every soul created from among His creatures, enduring the pangs of death and drinking its cup.

* *

As for His saying, "And We test you with evil and with good as a trial."

He, exalted is He, says: We test you, O people, with evil, which is hardship, by which We try you, and with good, which is ease, abundance, and well-being, by which We put you to trial.

The people of interpretation have said similarly to what we have said regarding this. Those who said so:

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Ibn Abbas said, regarding His saying, "And We test you with evil and with good as a trial," that it means: with ease and hardship, and both are a trial.

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying, "And We test you with evil and with good as a trial," he said: We test you with evil as a trial, and with good as a trial, "And to Us you will be returned."

Yunus narrated to us, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying, "And We test you with evil and with good as a trial, and to Us you will be returned," he said: We test them with what they love and what they dislike, to test them by that, to see how they give thanks for what they love and how they endure what they dislike.

Ali narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying, "And We test you with evil and with good," he said: We test you with hardship and ease, health and sickness, wealth and poverty, the lawful and the unlawful, obedience and disobedience, guidance and misguidance. And regarding His saying, "And to Us you will be returned," he said: and to Us they will be brought back, and they will be recompensed for their deeds, good and bad.

He, exalted is His remembrance, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): ﴿And when those who disbelieve see you﴾, O Muhammad, ﴿in God﴾, ﴿they take you not except in mockery﴾. He means: they take you only as an object of ridicule, some of them saying to others, ﴿"Is this the one who mentions your gods?"﴾ By his saying "mentions" they mean: mentions them with evil and disparages them, in wonder at that. God, exalted is His remembrance, says: they marvel at your mentioning their gods, which neither harm nor benefit, with evil. ﴿And they, at the mention of the Most Merciful﴾, who created them, bestowed favours upon them, from Him is their provision, in His hand is their harm, and to Him is their return, as is fitting for Him from them, that they should mention Him with it, ﴿are disbelievers﴾.

The Arabs use "mention" (dhikr) in the place of praise and blame, so they say: "We heard so-and-so mentioning so-and-so," and they mean: we heard him mentioning him with ugliness and disparaging him. Among this is the verse of 'Antarah:

*Do not mention my mare, nor what I have fed her,*
*lest your skin become like the skin of the mangy camel.* [[The verse is by 'Antarah ibn 'Amr ibn Shaddad al-'Absi (Mukhtar al-Shi'r al-Jahili, with the commentary of Mustafa al-Saqqa, Halabi edition, p. 396). He says: "Do not blame me by mentioning my mare and her feeding, or else you will recoil from me as the healthy recoils from the mangy." He means: do not disparage my mare, nor blame me for my concern for her, for she is my means of defending you and my people.]]

He means by it: do not disparage my mare. And we heard him being mentioned with goodness.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 21, verses 37–38:

Discussion on the interpretation of His words, the Exalted: ﴿Man was created of haste. I will show you My signs, so do not ask Me to hasten.﴾ (21:37) ﴿And they say, "When is this promise, if you are truthful?"﴾ (21:38)

His words, may He be remembered, ﴿Man was created﴾ meaning Adam, ﴿of haste﴾.

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) differed regarding its interpretation. Some of them said: its meaning is: he was created of haste in his structure and creation, so he was of haste and upon haste.

Mention of those who said that:

◆ Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Ibn Yaman related to us, from Ash'ath, from Ja'far, from Sa'id, regarding His words ﴿Man was created of haste﴾, he said: When the spirit was breathed into him, into his knees, he went to stand up, so God said: ﴿Man was created of haste.﴾

◆ Musa related to us, saying: 'Amr related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi, who said: When the spirit was breathed into him, meaning into Adam, it entered his head and he sneezed, so the angels said: Say, "All praise is due to God," and he said, "All praise is due to God." God said to him: "May your Lord have mercy upon you." When the spirit entered his eyes, he looked at the fruits of Paradise, and when it entered his belly, he desired food, so he leapt, before the spirit reached his legs, hastily toward the fruits of Paradise. That is when He says ﴿Man was created of haste﴾, meaning: Man was created hasty.

◆ Ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada, regarding ﴿Man was created of haste﴾, he said: He was created hasty.

Others said: its meaning is: Man was created of haste, that is, from hastening in God's creating him and from swiftness in it, and upon haste. They said: God created him at the end of the day of Friday, before the sun set, in haste in creating him before its setting.

Mention of those who said that:

◆ Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, saying: 'Isa related to us, and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa' related to us, all of them, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding the words of God ﴿Man was created of haste﴾, he said: The words of Adam when he was created after everything else, at the end of the day on which creation was created: "When the spirit gave life to his eyes, his tongue and his head, but had not reached his lower part, he said: 'O Lord, hasten my creation before the sun sets.'" [[This chain is a repetition of the preceding one without difference.]]

◆ Al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa' related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.

◆ Al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Mujahid said, regarding ﴿Man was created of haste﴾: Adam said when he was created after everything else, then he mentioned something similar, except that in his narration he said: "Hasten my creation, for the sun has set."

◆ Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words ﴿Man was created of haste﴾: Adam was hasty at the last part of that day, of those two days, meaning the day of Friday, and He created him in haste, and made him hasty.

Some of the Basran grammarians who held this same view said: He only said ﴿Man was created of haste﴾ meaning that He created him from haste in the matter, because He said ﴿Our word to a thing, when We intend it, is only that We say to it, "Be," and it is﴾ (16:40). He said: this is the haste.

* *

And His words ﴿So do not ask Me to hasten. Indeed, I will show you My signs﴾

According to the view of the proponent of this opinion, every creation of God would have to have been created in haste, because all of it was created by being told "Be," and it was. If that is so, what is the particular point in specifying man as being created of haste, rather than all things, when all of them are created of haste? And in God's specifying man with this mention, that is a clear proof that the correct view on this matter is other than what the proponent of this opinion said.

Others among them said: this is an inversion (maqlub). What was actually meant is that haste was created from man, and that haste was created from man. They said: this is like His words ﴿Indeed, its keys would weigh down a band of strong men﴾ (28:76), when what is meant is that a band of men would be weighed down by them, burdened. They said: this and what resembles it is abundant and well known in the speech of the Arabs. They said: the people were addressed in terms they understand. They said: this is like their saying "I presented the camel" (i.e., the camel was presented to me, inverted), and like their saying: when Sirius rises and the stalk stands on the lizard, meaning the lizard stands on the stalk, as the poet said:

And they ride horses with no slackening between them,
And the spears are wearied by the red, bumbling men.
[[The verse is by Khidash ibn Zuhayr (Lisan: d-ṭ-r). Al-Jawhari: al-Dayṭar is a large man who is of no use; likewise al-Dawati and al-Dawṭari. In the hadith of Ali: "Who will excuse me from these dayatira?" — they are the large ones who have no use, singular dayṭar. Khidash's verse: Ibn Sayyidah said it is possible that he meant the spears are healed by them, i.e., they do not know how to carry them nor to thrust with them; it is also possible that it is an inversion, i.e., the red dayatira are wearied by the spears, meaning they are killed by them. Al-hawada: reconciliation and truce. The verse is evidence for inversion.]]

And like the words of Ibn Muqbil:

I drew back my hand from the garment, taking it,
Solitary, dragged upon the hands of those who ransom me.
[[The verse is by Tamim ibn Abi Muqbil, as the author said. "I drew back my hand from the garment" means I drew the garment back from my hand. The garment (sirbal) is shirt or armour. Al-mufaddun are those who say to me "We ransom you from hardships," magnifying me and exalting my trial in war; it is like the preceding evidence that the speech in it is inverted, because he means "I drew the garment back from my hand" due to my bravery.]]

He means: I drew the garment back from my hand, and similar to that of inversion. The consensus of the people of interpretation is against this view, which is sufficient to dispense with citing other evidence for its invalidity.

Abu Ja'far said: The correct view in

* *

the interpretation of this, according to us, is what we have mentioned from the one who said its meaning is: man was created of haste in his creation, meaning upon haste and swiftness in that. This was said to be so because his creation was hastened before the sun set, in the last hour of the day of Friday, and at that time the spirit was breathed into him.

We have only said that the most correct of the views we have mentioned is the most correct, because of the indication of His words ﴿I will show you My signs, so do not ask Me to hasten﴾ upon it.

Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Ibn Idris related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn 'Amr informed us, from Abu Salama, from Abu Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, on Friday there is an hour which [he made small with his fingers] (ibn Kathir, the narration of Ibn Abi Hatim: "and he closed his fingers to make it small"). No Muslim servant meets it while asking God for good in it except that God gives him it." Abdullah ibn Salam said: "I know which hour it is; it is the last hour of the day of Friday." God said ﴿Man was created of haste. I will show you My signs, so do not ask Me to hasten.﴾

◆ Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: al-Muharibi, 'Abdah ibn Sulayman and Usayr ibn 'Amr related to us, from Muhammad ibn 'Amr, saying: Abu Salama related to us, from Abu Hurayra, from the Prophet (ﷺ), similar to it, and mentioned the words of Abdullah ibn Salam similarly.

So the meaning of the speech, if the correct interpretation is what we have said with what we cited as evidence, ﴿Man was created of haste﴾, and therefore he hastens his Lord for punishment, ﴿I will show you My signs, so do not ask Me to hasten﴾, O you who hasten your Lord for signs, who say to our Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): "Rather, he is a poet; let him bring us a sign as the earlier ones were sent signs." As I showed signs to you before, to the nations whom We destroyed for denying the messengers when the signs came to them, do not hasten. He says: do not hasten your Lord, for We will bring them to you and show them to you.

The readers differed concerning the recitation of ﴿Man was created of haste﴾. The common readers of the cities recited it ﴿khuliqa al-insanu min ajal﴾ with a dammah on the kha', in the passive form (madhhab ma lam yusamma fa'iluh). Humayd al-A'raj recited ﴿khalaqa﴾ with a fatha, meaning: God created man. The recitation upon which the readers of the cities agree is the one whose opposition I do not permit.

* *

His words ﴿And they say, "When is this promise, if you are truthful?"﴾

His words, may He be remembered: And these people who hasten their Lord for signs and punishment say to Muhammad (ﷺ): "When is this promise?" That is: when will this punishment you threaten us with come, if you are truthful in what you threaten us with? It was said that ﴿if you are truthful﴾ means they said that to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and to the believers in him. "Matā" (when) is in the accusative position, because its meaning is: what time is this promise, and what day is it; it is accusative as an adverb of time.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 21, verse 39–41:

On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿Had those who disbelieved known the time when they will not be able to keep the Fire away from their faces or from their backs, and they will not be helped﴾ (39)

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: Had these disbelievers who were hastening the punishment of their Lord known what affliction awaits them when the Fire scorches their faces, while they are grim-faced therein, so that they cannot keep the Fire from their faces, which is scorching them, nor from their backs, so as to ward it off from themselves by their own efforts, ﴿and they will not be helped﴾.

He says: nor will there be any helper for them to rescue them then from the punishment of God, because they persisted in the disbelief in God in which they were persisting, and they would have hastened to repent of it and to believe in God, and they would not have hastened to bring affliction upon themselves.

* *

On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿Nay, it will come upon them suddenly and confound them, so they will not be able to repel it, nor will they be given respite﴾ (40)

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: This Fire that scorches the faces of these disbelievers, whose matter is described in this surah, will not come to them with prior knowledge of its time; rather it will come upon them by surprise, without their perceiving its arrival, and it will confound them. He says: it will overwhelm them suddenly and scorch their faces visibly, like a man who startles another man in his face with something, so that the one startled remains bewildered by it. ﴿So they will not be able to repel it﴾: He says: so when it overtakes them and confounds them, they will not be able to ward it off from themselves. ﴿Nor will they be given respite﴾: He says: nor will they, although unable to ward it off from themselves, be granted delay in the punishment through a repentance they might undertake or a turning back they might make, because that is not a time of action, nor an hour of repentance and turning back, but an hour of recompense and reward.

* *

On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿Certainly messengers were mocked before you, but those who mocked them were encompassed by what they used to mock﴾ (41)

He, exalted is His remembrance, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): If these people who say to you, "Is this but a human being like you? Will you then submit to magic while you see?" and who, when they see you, make you a laughingstock, saying, "Is this the one who mentions your gods?", in disbelief in God and audacity toward Him, should take you in mockery, then indeed messengers from among Our messengers whom We sent before you to their peoples were mocked. He says: there befell and descended upon those who mocked them and scorned them from among their peoples what they used to mock: He, exalted is His praise, says: there came upon them what they used to mock, of affliction and punishment, which their messengers warned them would descend upon them. "They used to mock": He, exalted is His praise, says: so these mockers of you from among these disbelievers will not escape being like their predecessors, the peoples who denied their messengers, so that there will descend upon them from the punishment of God and His wrath, because of their mockery of you, the like of what descended upon those.

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Say: Who protects you by night and by day from the Most Merciful?﴾ (Q. 21:42)

God, may His remembrance be exalted, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): Say, O Muhammad, to these people who are hastening you toward the punishment, who say, "When is this promise, if you are truthful?": ﴿Who protects you, O people?﴾ That is: who guards and watches over you by night when you sleep, and by day when you go about your affairs, ﴿from the Most Merciful?﴾ That is: from the command of the Most Merciful, if it descends upon you, or from His punishment, if it befalls you. The word "command" has been omitted, and "from the Most Merciful" is said, relying on the listeners' understanding of its meaning from the mention.

Those who engage in interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said things in accordance with what we have said regarding this.

Mention of those who said that:

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying, ﴿Say: Who protects you by night and by day from the Most Merciful?﴾ said: "He guards you."

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿Say: Who protects you by night and by day from the Most Merciful?﴾: "Say: who guards you by night and by day from the Most Merciful." It is said from this: kalaɔtu al-qawm (I guarded the people) when I guard them, akla'uhum, as Ibn Harmah said:

"Indeed Sulayma, ﴿and God guards her﴾ ... has withheld something that would not diminish her."

[[The verse is by Ibrahim ibn Harmah, as the author said. It appears in (Lisan al-'Arab: k-l-'-) without attribution, with "bi-zad" in place of "bi-shay'." He said: It is said, "kala'aka Allah kala'atan" (with a kasra), meaning "may God protect you and guard you."

And he recited, "Indeed Sulayma... the verse." The phrase "and God guards her" is a parenthetical supplication. "Yarzu'uha" means: diminishes and harms it. He means: she withheld a trifling thing from herself, which if she had given it to us would have been of no consequence. The author cited it as evidence that the meaning of yakla' is "yahfaz" (guards), as the lexicographers said.]]

His saying, ﴿Nay, but they turn away from the remembrance of their Lord﴾: "Nay" (bal) confirms a denial which the addressees already know from this discourse, even though it is not explicitly mentioned in this place.

The meaning of the speech is: Is it not for them to know that there is no guardian for them against the command of God when it descends upon them, by night or by day? Rather, they turn away from the admonitions of their Lord and the proofs with which He has argued against them, not reflecting upon them, and so they take no lesson from them, out of ignorance and foolishness.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 21, verse 43:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Or do they have gods who can protect them from Us? They are unable to help themselves, nor can they be accompanied by protection from Us.﴾

His saying, exalted is His remembrance: Do these people who hasten their Lord's punishment have gods that protect them if We bring down Our punishment upon them and send Our might against them, apart from Us? The meaning is: Or do they have gods, apart from Us, that protect them from Us? Then Allah, exalted is His praise, described the gods with weakness and humiliation, and with the attribute that they actually have, saying: How can their gods, whom they invoke apart from Us, protect them from Us when they cannot help themselves? As for His saying, ﴿nor can they be accompanied by protection from Us﴾, the people of interpretation differed about who is meant by it, and about the meaning of yuṣḥabūn (they are accompanied). Some of them said: it refers to the gods, and that they are not accompanied by any good from Allah.

Mention of those who said this:

• Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿Or do they have gods who can protect them from Us? They are unable to help themselves﴾, he said: meaning the gods. ﴿Nor can they be accompanied by protection from Us﴾ means: they are not accompanied by any good from Allah.

Others said: rather, the meaning of that is: nor can they be helped by Us.

Mention of those who said this:

• Ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Abu Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿nor can they be accompanied by protection from Us﴾, he said: they will not be helped.

• al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Ibn 'Abbas said, regarding His saying ﴿Or do they have gods who can protect them from Us﴾ up to His saying ﴿can be accompanied﴾, he said: they will be helped. He said: Mujahid said: nor will they be guarded.

• 'Ali narrated to us, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿nor can they be accompanied by protection from Us﴾, it means: they will not be given protection (yujarun).[[The author did not mention the summary of this last statement before naming those who held it, as is his practice. He would say: "Some said: rather, its meaning is yujaʼarun (they cry out for help)."]]

Mention of those who said this:

• Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿nor can they be accompanied by protection from Us﴾, he said: nor will they be given protection from Us, and this is His saying ﴿He gives protection, and none can give protection against Him﴾. The "companion" (al-sahib) is the person who has a guarantor (khafir) against what he fears, and this is the meaning of His saying "they are accompanied (yuṣḥabūn)".

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: The most correct of these opinions is the view of those who said that the statement narrated from Ibn 'Abbas is correct, and that the pronoun "they" (hum) in His saying ﴿nor they﴾ refers to the disbelievers, and that His saying yuṣḥabūn means yujarūn, i.e., they are accompanied by protection (al-jiwar), because the Arabs are reported to say: "I am your neighbour (jar) and companion (sahib) against so-and-so," meaning: I will protect you and defend you. If they are not given protection, and there is no one to prevent them from the punishment of Allah while Allah is displeased with them, then they are not accompanied by any good, nor are they helped.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 21, verse 44:

The interpretation of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Nay, We gave comfort to these and their fathers until life stretched out long for them. Do they not see that We come to the land, reducing it from its outlying parts? Are they then the victors?﴾ (21:44)

Almighty God says: These polytheists have no gods that can protect them from Us, nor any protector who can shield them from Our punishment, should We wish to punish them. Yet they relied upon that and disobeyed Our messengers, trusting in it. But We gave them comfort in this worldly life, and their fathers before them, until life stretched out long for them, while they remained persistent in their disbelief. No warner from Us came to them with a punishment, nor any deterrent of retribution, for their disbelief and their opposition to Our command, and their worship of idols and statues. So they forgot Our covenant and failed to recognise the place of Our blessing upon them, and did not know the proper place of gratitude.

As for His saying, ﴿Do they not see that We come to the land, reducing it from its outlying parts?﴾, Almighty God says: Do these polytheists who associate others with God, who ask Muhammad (ﷺ) for signs and seek the punishment hastily, not see that We come to the land, ruining it from its sides by subduing its people, overpowering them, expelling them from it, and slaying them with swords, so that they might take heed from that and be warned by it, and fear that We might bring down upon them Our might like that which We brought upon those in the outlying regions who were treated thus? The speakers of this view and those who differ with it, together with their narrations, have already been mentioned in Surat al-Ra'd, in a way that makes repeating them here unnecessary.

* *

As for His saying, ﴿Are they then the victors?﴾

Blessed and Exalted is He says: Are these polytheists, who hasten the punishment upon Muhammad, the victors, when they have seen Our overpowering of those whose courtyard Our might has descended upon in the outlying lands? It is not so; rather, We are the victors. This is a rebuke from God the Exalted to these polytheists who associate others with Him, for their ignorance. He says: Do they suppose that they will overcome Muhammad and subdue him, when He has subdued those who opposed him from the people of the outlying lands other than them?

As related:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿Are they then the victors?﴾, he said: They are not victors, but the Messenger of God (ﷺ) is the victor.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 21, verse 45:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Say: I only warn you by revelation, and the deaf do not hear the call when they are warned﴾.

His saying, exalted is He, to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): Say, O Muhammad, to these people who said, "Let him bring us a sign, as the earlier messengers were sent": I only warn you, O people, with the revelation of God, which He sends down to whomever is with Him, and I warn you with His punishment.

As follows:

* Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying, ﴿Say: I only warn you by revelation﴾, meaning: by this Qur'an.

* *

As for His saying, ﴿and the deaf do not hear the call﴾:

The reciters differed regarding the reading of this. The majority of the reciters of the major cities read ﴿wa-la yasma'u﴾ with a fatha on the yaʾ of (yasma'u), meaning that it is the act of the deaf, and the deaf in that case are the subject (marfu'). It is related from Abu ʿAbd al-Rahman al-Sulami that he used to read ﴿wa-la tusma'u﴾ with a taʾ and a damma, so the deaf in this reading are in the nominative case, because His saying ﴿la tusmi'u﴾ has no named agent, and its meaning in this reading is: and God does not make the deaf hear the call.

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: The correct reading in our view is what the reciters of the major cities follow, due to the consensus of the authoritative reciters upon it. Its meaning: the disbeliever in God does not give ear with the hearing of his heart to recall what is in God's revelation of admonitions and remembrance, so that he may remember by it and take heed, and cease from his error in which he persists when it is recited to him and directed at him. Rather, he turns away from taking heed of it and reflecting upon it, like the act of the deaf person who does not hear what is said to him so as to act upon it.

Commentators have said things similar to what we have said regarding this.

Mention of those who said this:

* Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿and the deaf do not hear the call when they are warned﴾: he says, the disbeliever has become deaf to the Book of God, not hearing it, nor benefiting from it, nor understanding it, just as the believer and the people of faith hear it.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 21, verse 46:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And if a breath of the punishment of your Lord should touch them, they would surely say, "Woe to us! Indeed, we were wrongdoers."﴾

He, exalted is He, says: And if a breath of the punishment of your Lord, O Muhammad, touches these who were hastening the punishment, meaning by the nafha (breath, portion) the share and portion, from their saying: "So-and-so breathed (nafaha) to so-and-so from his gift," when he gave him a portion or share of the wealth.

As related by:

Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿And if a breath of the punishment of your Lord should touch them﴾ ... the verse, he said: it means: if a punishment afflicts them.

* *

And as for His saying ﴿they would surely say, "Woe to us! Indeed, we were wrongdoers."﴾

He means: if this breath of the punishment of your Lord, O Muhammad, afflicts them because of their denial of you and their disbelief, then they will surely come to know, at that time, the outcome of their denial of you, and they will surely acknowledge against themselves the blessing of Allah and His kindness toward them, and their ingratitude for His favours upon them. They will say, "Woe to us! Indeed, we were wrongdoers in our worship of the gods and rivals, and in our abandonment of the worship of Allah who created us and bestowed blessings upon us, and we placed worship in other than its proper place."

The Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami' al-Bayan) on Surah 21, verse 47:

The interpretation of His saying, ﴿And We shall set up the scales of justice for the Day of Resurrection, so no soul will be wronged in anything. And even if it be the weight of a mustard seed, We will bring it forth. And sufficient are We as Reckoners.﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: ﴿And We shall set up the scales﴾ of justice, which is ﴿al-qist﴾ (justice). He made al-qist, though singular, an attribute of al-mawazin (the scales), which is plural, because it is in the sense of justice, satisfaction and consideration.

* *

As for His saying ﴿for the Day of Resurrection﴾:

He means: for the people of the Day of Resurrection, and for whoever among His creation comes before Allah on that Day. Some of the grammarians of Arabic gave this meaning the sense of "in" (fi), as if its meaning to them were: "And We shall set up the just scales in the Day of Resurrection."

As for His saying ﴿so no soul will be wronged in anything﴾, He means: Allah will not wrong any soul among those who come before Him by punishing it for a sin it did not commit, or by diminishing the reward of a deed it performed or an act of obedience by which it obeyed Him. Rather, He rewards the doer of good for his good, and punishes the doer of evil only for his evil.

Concerning this, the people of interpretation said what we have said.

Mention of those who said that:

⁕ Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His saying ﴿And We shall set up the scales of justice for the Day of Resurrection﴾ ... to the end of the verse. It is like His saying ﴿And the weighing on that Day is the truth﴾. By "the weighing" is meant the just distribution among them, with truth, concerning the good and evil deeds. Whoever's good deeds outweigh his evil deeds, his scales become heavy, meaning his good deeds have removed his evil deeds; and whoever's evil deeds outweigh his good deeds, his scales become light, and "his mother is the Abyss," meaning his evil deeds have removed his good deeds.

⁕ Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: al-Thawri informed us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning the saying of Allah ﴿And We shall set up the scales of justice for the Day of Resurrection﴾, he said: It is only an example; just as weighing is permissible, so too is truth. al-Thawri said: Layth said, from Mujahid, ﴿And We shall set up the scales of justice﴾, he said: the justice.

* *

As for His saying ﴿And even if it be the weight of a mustard seed, We will bring it forth﴾:

He means: whether that which is of good deeds, or that which is of evil deeds upon him, is the weight of a mustard seed, We will bring it forth: He says, We will bring it and present it to him.

As:

⁕ Yunus narrated to us, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd, concerning His saying ﴿And even if it be the weight of a mustard seed, We will bring it forth﴾, said: We will record it and count it for him and against him.

⁕ Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His saying ﴿And even if it be the weight of a mustard seed, We will bring it forth﴾, he said: It will be brought for you and against you, then He pardons if He wills or takes account, and He recompenses for what was done for Him of obedience. Mujahid used to say concerning this:

⁕ Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning His saying ﴿And even if it be the weight of a mustard seed, We will bring it forth﴾, he said: We will recompense with it.

⁕ 'Amr ibn 'Abd al-Hamid narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Layth, from Mujahid, that he used to say ﴿And even if it be the weight of a mustard seed, We will bring it forth﴾, he said: We will recompense with it. And he said "atayna bihā" (We brought it), so he put the pronoun "bihā" in the feminine form, although the antecedent mentioned before it was "mithqal" (weight), because by "bihā" he meant the grain (ḥabba), not the weight (mithqal). Had he meant the weight, it would have been said "bihi." It is mentioned that Mujahid only interpreted His saying ﴿atayna bihā﴾ in the way we have mentioned from him, because he used to read it as ﴿ātaynā bihā﴾ with an elongated alif.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And sufficient are We as Reckoners﴾:

He means: and sufficient for those who witness that station is Us as Reckoners, because no one knows better their deeds, and what they had done in the world of good or evil, than We do.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 21, verse 48:

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿And We had certainly given Moses and Aaron the Criterion and a light and a reminder for the righteous﴾

His, the Exalted's, saying means: And We had certainly given Moses, son of Imran, and his brother Aaron the Criterion (al-furqan), meaning by it the Book that distinguishes between truth and falsehood. This, according to some of them, is the Torah.

Mention of those who said that:

Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿al-Furqan﴾: he said: "The Book."

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij, from Mujahid, the like of it.

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding His saying ﴿And We had certainly given Moses and Aaron the Criterion﴾: "The Criterion: the Torah, its lawful and its unlawful, and that by which Allah distinguishes between truth and falsehood."

Ibn Zayd used to say concerning this what follows:

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿And We had certainly given Moses and Aaron the Criterion﴾: "The Criterion is the truth that Allah gave to Moses and Aaron, distinguishing between them and Pharaoh, and judging among them with truth." And he recited ﴿And We did not send down upon Our servant on the day of the Criterion﴾, and said: "The day of Badr."

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: This opinion that Ibn Zayd stated is more akin to the apparent sense of the revelation, due to the entry of the conjunction "waw" before "ḍiyā'" (light). Had the Criterion been the Torah, as those who said so claimed, the revelation would have read: "And We had certainly given Moses and Aaron the Criterion, a light," because the light that Allah gave Moses and Aaron is the Torah, which illuminated for them and for those who followed them the matter of their religion, so it made them see the lawful and the unlawful. The intended meaning here is not the light of sight. The presence of the "waw" in this indicates that the Criterion is other than the Torah, which is the light.

If someone says: What prevents "ḍiyā'" from being a description of "al-furqan," with the "waw" there, so that its meaning is "and a light which We gave that," as in His saying ﴿with an adornment, the stars, and a guard﴾? It is said to him: Although the speech may bear that, the more prevalent of its meanings is what we have stated, and it is obligatory to direct the meanings of Allah's speech toward the more common and well-known of its aspects among the Arabs, unless there is something contrary to that which must be accepted by a proof of report or reason.

* *

As for His saying ﴿and a reminder for the righteous﴾:

He says: and a reminder for those who fear Allah by obeying Him, performing His obligations and avoiding His disobedience; it reminds them of what Allah gave Moses and Aaron of the Torah.

* *

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿Those who fear their Lord unseen, and they, of the Hour, are apprehensive﴾ [21:49]

His, the Exalted's, saying means: We gave Moses and Aaron the Criterion, the reminder that We gave them, for the righteous who fear their Lord unseen, meaning in the world, that He would punish them in the Hereafter when they come before Him for neglecting what He obligated them with of His duties. Thus they, out of fear of Him, guard His limits and obligations, and they, of the Hour in which the Resurrection will occur, are apprehensive, wary lest it come upon them while they return to their Lord having fallen short in what is obligatory upon them toward Allah, so that He punishes them with a punishment they cannot bear.

* *

Mention of those who said that:

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid ﴿And We had already given Abraham his rectitude before﴾, he said: "He guided him while he was young."

* *

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 21, verse 53–57:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿They said, "We found our fathers worshipping them."﴾ ﴿He said, "Indeed you were, you and your fathers, in manifest error."﴾ ﴿They said, "Have you brought us the truth, or are you of those who play?"﴾

God, mentioned is He, says: Abu Ibrahim (the father of Ibrahim) and his people said to Ibrahim: "We found our fathers worshipping these idols, so we are upon the religion (millah) of our fathers, worshipping them as they used to worship." ﴿He said﴾ Ibrahim: ﴿"Indeed you were, you and your fathers"﴾, O people, ﴿"in your worship of them"﴾ ﴿"in manifest error"﴾. He says: in going astray from the path of truth and deviating from the straight path. "Manifest" means: clear to whoever considers it with reason, that you are thus in deviation from the truth. ﴿They said, "Have you brought us the truth?"﴾ He says: his father and his people said to him: "Have you brought us the truth in what you say?" ﴿Or are you﴾ jesting and playing ﴿among those who play?﴾

* *

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿He said, "Rather, your Lord is the Lord of the heavens and the earth, who originated them, and I am of that to testify."﴾

God, mentioned is He, says: Ibrahim said to them: "Rather, I have brought you the truth, not play. Your Lord is the Lord of the heavens and the earth, who created them, and I am upon that, that your Lord is the Lord of the heavens and the earth who originated them, apart from the images to which you are devoted, and apart from every other being, is among those who bear witness." He says: so worship Him alone, not these images, which are His creation, which neither harm nor benefit.

* *

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿"And by Allah, I will surely plot against your idols after you have turned away, retreating."﴾ ﴿So he made them into fragments, except a large one among them, that they might turn back to it.﴾

It is mentioned that Abraham, peace be upon him, swore this oath secretly and privately, away from his people, and that no one heard it from him except the one who disclosed it when they said: "Who has done this to our gods? Those who said this: Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, saying: Abu Asim told us, saying: Isa told us. And al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan told us, saying: Warqa' told us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿And by God, I will surely plot against your idols﴾, he said: It is the saying of Abraham when his people invited him to a festival of theirs and he refused and said: "I am sick." * Al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn told us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, the like of it.

As for His saying ﴿So he reduced them to fragments﴾

The reciters differed in reading it. The majority of the reciters of the major cities read ﴿judhadhan﴾ [[The wording here is deficient, and perhaps something has dropped out; the author will clarify it in what follows. The summary is that the common reading "judhadhan" with a damma on the jim is said to be a singular like hutam, and it is said to be from the plural of rarity. Ibn Wathhab and a group read it with a kasra, and it is judhadh, its parallel being karim and kiram.]] meaning the plural of judhadh, as if they intended by it the plural of judhadh and judhadh, just as khafif is pluralized as khifaf and karim as kiram.

The more correct of the two readings in our view is the reading of the one who reads ﴿judhadhan﴾ with a damma on the jim, due to the consensus of the reciters of the major cities upon it, and what the consensus has agreed upon is correct. When read thus, it is a verbal noun like al-rufat, al-futat, and al-duqaq, having no singular. As for the one who reads the jim with a kasra, it is the plural of judhadh, and judhadh is a form of fa'il derived from majdhudh toward it, like kasir and hashim, and al-majdhuda is that which is broken into pieces.

The people of interpretation said in accordance with what we have said.

* Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid told us, saying: Sa'id told us, from Qatada, regarding His saying ﴿So he reduced them to fragments﴾: i.e., pieces.

The cause of Abraham's action, peace be upon him, against his people's gods was that,

as:

* Musa related to us, saying: Amr told us, saying: Asbat told us, from al-Suddi, that Abraham's father said to him: "O Abraham, we have a festival; if only you would come out with us to it, our religion would please you." When the day of the festival came and they went out to it, Abraham went out with them. When they were at some part of the road, he threw himself down and said: "I am sick," meaning: "my leg hurts." They stepped on his legs while he lay prostrate. When they had gone, he called out at the rear of them, and only the weak among the people remained: ﴿And by God, I will surely plot against your idols after you have turned away retreating﴾. Then Abraham returned to the house of the gods, and there they were in a great hall, facing the door of the hall was a great idol, and beside it were smaller ones, each idol next to it smaller than it, until they reached the door of the hall. They had set out food and placed it before the gods, saying: "When we return, we will return, and the gods have blessed our food, so we will eat." When Abraham looked at them and at the food before them, ﴿He said: "Will you not eat?"﴾ When they did not answer him, he said ﴿"What is the matter with you that you do not speak?" So he turned upon them, striking with the right hand﴾. He took an iron axe and struck each idol in its side, then hung the axe on the neck of the largest idol, and went out. As for His saying ﴿except a large one among them﴾

He means: except a great one for the gods. Abraham did not break it, but it is mentioned that he hung the axe on its neck.

On the interpretation of His saying, ﴿They said, "Did you do this to our gods, O Abraham?" (62) He said, "Rather, it was done by this, their chief. So ask them, if they can speak."﴾ (63)

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: They brought Abraham, and when they had brought him, they said to him, "Did you do this to our gods, by breaking them, O Abraham?" Abraham answered them, "Rather, this, their chief and their greatest, did it. So ask the gods who did this to them and broke them, if they are able to speak or to express themselves."

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said things similar to what we have said.

Mention of those who said this: Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: When he was brought and his people gathered before their king Nimrod, ﴿They said, "Did you do this to our gods, O Abraham?" He said, "Rather, this, their chief, did it. So ask them, if they can speak."﴾ He was angered that they worshipped these small things along with him, while he was greater than them, so he broke them.

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿Rather, this, their chief, did it﴾ ... the verse, and this is the stratagem with which he outwitted them.

Some who do not affirm the reports, and accept from the traditions only what is widely transmitted among the common people, have claimed that the meaning of His saying ﴿Rather, this, their chief, did it﴾ is only: "Rather, this, their chief, did it, if they can speak, so ask them," i.e., if the broken gods can speak, then their chief is the one who broke them. This is a view contrary to what the reports from the Messenger of God (ﷺ) have widely established: that Abraham told no lies except three lies, all of them concerning God: His saying ﴿Rather, this, their chief, did it﴾, His saying ﴿Indeed, I am sick﴾, and his saying to Sarah, "She is my sister." It is not impossible that God, may His remembrance be exalted, permitted His intimate friend to do this, in order to rebuke his people with it, argue against them with it, and make them aware of the place of their error and the poor opinion they held of themselves, just as the crier of Joseph said to his brothers, ﴿O caravan, indeed you are thieves﴾, though they had not stolen anything.

And in accordance with what we have said concerning this, the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have spoken.
