As for His saying ﴿Then they were overturned upon their heads﴾:

His majesty, exalted is His praise, says: Then they were overcome in argument, so they argued against Ibrahim with what was (in fact) a proof for Ibrahim against them, and they said: "You certainly know that these idols do not speak."

As (narrated):

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, he said: Then they said, meaning the people of Ibrahim, and they recognised that they, meaning their gods, neither harm nor benefit, nor strike with hands: ﴿"You certainly know that these do not speak"﴾, i.e., they do not speak so as to tell us who did this to them, nor do they strike with hands so that we might believe you. God says, ﴿Then they were overturned upon their heads﴾ in argument against them, for Ibrahim, when he disputed with them; so Ibrahim said at that time, when the proof was made manifest against them by their own words: ﴿"You certainly know that these do not speak."﴾

Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, he said, concerning God's saying ﴿Then they were overturned upon their heads﴾: "The people reached a state of evil bewilderment."

Others said: The meaning of that is: Then they were overturned in sedition.

Mention of those who said this:

Musa narrated to me, he said: Amr narrated to us, he said: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, concerning ﴿Then they were overturned upon their heads﴾: "They were overturned in sedition upon their heads, so they said: 'You certainly know that these do not speak.'"

Some of the people of Arabic grammar (ahl al-'arabiyyah) said: The meaning of that is: Then they returned from what they had recognised of Ibrahim's proof, so they said: "You certainly know that these do not speak."

We have chosen the view we have stated concerning its meaning because *nakkasa al-shay'* ("to overturn a thing upon its head") means: to turn it over onto its head and make its top its bottom. It is known that the people were not turned over upon their own heads; rather, their argument was overturned. So the report about them was placed in the position of a report about their argument. Since this is so, the overturning of an argument is undoubtedly the arguer's pleading against his opponent with what is a proof for the opponent. As for al-Suddi's saying, "Then they were overturned in sedition," they had not come out of the sedition before that, so that they could be overturned within it. As for the saying of those among the grammarians whom we have mentioned, it is a view far from the understanding, for if they had returned from what they recognised of Ibrahim's proof, they would not have argued against him with what was a proof for him; rather, they would have said to him: "Do not ask them, but ask you: tell us who did this to them, for we have heard that you did it. But they spoke the truth," ﴿so they said, "You certainly know that these do not speak."﴾ That is not a return from what they had recognised; rather, it is an acknowledgment of it.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 21, verses 64–65:

The interpretation of His saying, ﴿Then they returned to themselves and said, "Indeed, it is you who are the wrongdoers." Then they were overturned upon their heads, "You certainly know that these do not speak."﴾

His saying, exalted is His mention: They gave thought when Ibrahim (peace be upon him) said to them, ﴿"Rather, it was done by this biggest one of them, so ask them, if they can speak."﴾ They returned to themselves (in their minds), returned to their reason, and looked at one another, and said: "Indeed, you, O people, are the wrongdoers. This man, in your questioning him and your saying to him, 'Who did this to our gods, O Ibrahim?' and these are your gods, to which what was done has been done, are present before you, so ask them."

And in accordance with what we have said concerning this, the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have spoken.

Mention of those who said this:

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, concerning ﴿So they returned to themselves and said, "Indeed, it is you who are the wrongdoers."﴾ He said: They came to their senses and turned back from him, meaning from Ibrahim, regarding what they had claimed against him concerning the breaking of them, to themselves among themselves, and they said: "Indeed we have wronged him, and we do not see him except as he said."

Al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, concerning ﴿So they returned to themselves﴾ he said: Some of them looked at others. ﴿And they said, "Indeed, it is you who are the wrongdoers."﴾

* *

As for His saying ﴿Then they were overturned upon their heads﴾:

His majesty, exalted is His praise, says: Then they were overcome in argument, so they argued against Ibrahim with what was (in fact) a proof for Ibrahim against them, and they said: "You certainly know that these idols do not speak."

His saying, Exalted is He, means: Abraham said to his people, "Do you worship, O people, that which neither benefits you nor harms you, when you know that it does not protect itself from one who intends it harm, and it is not able to speak if asked about the one who does it harm, so that it might inform about him? Will you not then be ashamed to worship something that is like this?"

As related:

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, who said: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, concerning ﴿He said, "Do you then worship, besides Allah, that which can neither benefit you at all nor harm you?"﴾ ... the verse. He said, may Allah have mercy on him: "Do you not see that they did not repel from themselves the harm that befell them, and that they do not speak so as to inform you who did that to them? So how could they benefit you or harm you?"

* *

As for His saying, ﴿Uff to you﴾:

He says: Ugliness (qubhan) to you and to the gods you worship besides Allah. "Will you not then use your reason?" meaning: will you not reason about the ugliness of what you do, in worshipping that which neither harms nor benefits, so that you would abandon its worship and worship Allah, who originated the heavens and the earth, and in whose hand is benefit and harm?

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 21, verses 67–70:

The explanation of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿They said: "Burn him and support your gods, if you are to act."﴾ [68] ﴿We said: "O fire, be coolness and safety upon Abraham."﴾ [69] ﴿And they intended a scheme against him, but We made them the greatest losers.﴾ [70]

Says God, may His remembrance be exalted: Some of the people of Abraham said to others: "Burn Abraham with fire," ﴿and support your gods, if you are to act﴾, meaning: if you are to be supporters of them, and you do not intend to abandon their worship.

It was also said: the one who said this was a man from the Kurds of Persia.

Mention of those who said this:

* Yaqub related to me, saying: Ibn Ulayyah related to us, from Layth, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿Burn him and support your gods﴾, he said: It was said by a man of the A'rab of Persia, meaning the Kurds.

* Al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Wahb ibn Sulayman informed me, from Shu'ayb al-Jubba'i, who said: The one who said "Burn him" was "Haydhan," and God caused the earth to swallow him, and he continues to sink into it until the Day of Resurrection.

* Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Salamah related to us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: Nimrod and his people united against Abraham and said: ﴿Burn him and support your gods, if you are to act﴾, meaning: you will not support them against him except by burning him with fire, if you are to be their supporters.

* Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Salamah related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ishaq related to me, from al-Hasan ibn Dinar, from Layth ibn Abi Sulaym, from Mujahid, who said: I recited this verse to Abdullah ibn Umar, and he said: "Do you know, O Mujahid, who it was that advised burning Abraham with fire?" I said: "No." He said: "A man of the A'rab of Persia." I said: "O Abu Abd al-Rahman, do the Persians have A'rab?" He said: "Yes, the Kurds are the A'rab of Persia, and a man among them is the one who advised burning Abraham with fire."

* * *

As for His saying: ﴿We said: "O fire, be coolness and safety upon Abraham."﴾

There is an omission in the speech, which is indicated by what has been mentioned, and it is: So they lit a fire for him to burn him, then they threw him into it, and We said to the fire: "O fire, be coolness and safety upon Abraham." It was mentioned that when they wanted to burn him, they built a structure for him,

as:

* Musa related to us, saying: Amr related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi, who said regarding ﴿They said: "Build for him a structure and throw him into the blazing fire"﴾: He said: They imprisoned him in a house and gathered firewood for him, until a woman would fall ill and say: "If God restores my health, I will surely gather firewood for Abraham." When they had gathered it and piled up a great deal of firewood, [[A phrase was dropped from this report; al-Tha'labi the exegete mentioned something similar in ʿAra'is al-Majalis, which is: They lit the fire on every side with the firewood, so the fire blazed up, until a bird would pass over it and be burned, etc.]] until the bird would pass by it and be burned from its intense heat, they went to him and raised him to the top of the structure. Abraham ﷺ raised his head to the sky, and the sky, the earth, the mountains and the angels said: "Our Lord, Abraham is being burned for Your sake!" He said: "I know him best. If he calls upon you, then aid him." And Abraham, when he raised his head to the sky, said: "O God, You are the One in the sky, and I am the one on the earth; there is no one on the earth who worships You besides me. Sufficient for me is God, and He is the best Disposer of affairs." Then they cast him into the fire, and He called to it, saying: ﴿O fire, be coolness and safety upon Abraham﴾. It was Gabriel, peace be upon him, who called to it.

Ibn Abbas said: Had its coolness not been followed by safety, Abraham would have died from its intense cold. On that day no fire remained on the earth but was extinguished, thinking that it was the one intended. When the fire was extinguished, they looked at Abraham, and there was another man with him, and Abraham's head was in his lap, wiping the sweat from his face. It is mentioned that this man was the Angel of Shade. God sent down a fire, and the children of Adam benefited from it, and they brought Abraham out and led him in to the king, who had not entered upon him before that.

* Ibrahim ibn al-Miqdam Abu al-Ash'ath related to me, saying: al-Mu'tamir related to us, saying: I heard my father say: Qatadah related to us, from Abu Sulayman, from Ka'b, who said: The fire burned nothing of Abraham except his bonds.

* Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿We said: "O fire, be coolness and safety upon Abraham."﴾ He said: It was mentioned to us that Ka'b used to say: No one among the people benefited from it that day, and Ka'b would say: The fire burned nothing that day except his bonds.

* Muhammad ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Mu'ammal related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, from al-A'mash, from a shaykh, from Ali ibn Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, regarding His saying: ﴿We said: "O fire, be coolness and safety upon Abraham."﴾ He said: It became cold upon him until it nearly killed him, until it was said: "and safety," he said: It did not harm him.

* Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Jabir ibn Nuh related to us, saying: Isma'il informed us, from al-Minhal ibn Amr, who said: Abraham, the Friend of God, said: I was never happier on any days than the days I spent in the fire.

* Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Ya'qub related to us, from Ja'far, from Sa'id, who said: When Abraham, the Friend of God ﷺ, was thrown into the fire, the angel in charge of rain said: "Lord, Your friend Abraham, he hoped that permission would be given to him to send rain." He said: The command of God was swifter than that, and He said: ﴿We said: "O fire, be coolness and safety upon Abraham."﴾ So no fire remained on the earth but was extinguished.

* Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Jarir related to us, from Mughirah, from al-Harith, from Abu Zur'ah, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The finest thing said by the father of Abraham, when the cover was lifted from him while he was in the fire and he found him sweating on his brow, was: "Excellent is the Lord, your Lord, O Abraham!"

* Al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Wahb ibn Sulayman informed me, from Shu'ayb al-Jabasi, who said: Abraham was thrown into the fire when he was sixteen years old, and Isaac was sacrificed when he was seven years old, and Sarah bore him when she was ninety years old, and his place of sacrifice was from the house of Iliya two miles away. Ibn Jurayj said: Ka'b al-Ahbar said: The fire burned nothing of Abraham except the bonds with which they had tied him.

* Al-Hasan related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman al-Taymi related to us, from some of his companions, who said: Gabriel came to Abraham, peace be upon them both, while he was being bound or swaddled to be thrown into the fire, and said: "O Abraham, do you have a need?" Qatadah said: No creature came that day but that the fire was extinguished for him, except the lizard.

Al-Zuhri said: The Prophet ﷺ ordered its killing, and named it "Fuwaysiqa."

Says God, may His remembrance be exalted: Some of the people of Abraham said to others: "Burn Abraham with fire," ﴿and support your gods, if you are to act﴾, meaning: if you are to be supporters of them, and you do not intend to abandon their worship.

It was also said: the one who said this was a man from the Kurds of Persia.

Mention of those who said this:

* Yaqub related to me, saying: Ibn Ulayyah related to us, from Layth, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿Burn him and support your gods﴾, he said: It was said by a man of the A'rab of Persia, meaning the Kurds.

* Al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Wahb ibn Sulayman informed me, from Shu'ayb al-Jubba'i, who said: The one who said "Burn him" was "Haydhan," and God caused the earth to swallow him, and he continues to sink into it until the Day of Resurrection.

* Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Salamah related to us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: Nimrod and his people united against Abraham and said: ﴿Burn him and support your gods, if you are to act﴾, meaning: you will not support them against him except by burning him with fire, if you are to be their supporters.

* Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Salamah related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ishaq related to me, from al-Hasan ibn Dinar, from Layth ibn Abi Sulaym, from Mujahid, who said: I recited this verse to Abdullah ibn Umar, and he said: "Do you know, O Mujahid, who it was that advised burning Abraham with fire?" I said: "No." He said: "A man of the A'rab of Persia." I said: "O Abu Abd al-Rahman, do the Persians have A'rab?" He said: "Yes, the Kurds are the A'rab of Persia, and a man among them is the one who advised burning Abraham with fire."

* * *

As for His saying: ﴿We said: "O fire, be coolness and safety upon Abraham."﴾

There is an omission in the speech, which is indicated by what has been mentioned, and it is: So they lit a fire for him to burn him, then they threw him into it, and We said to the fire: "O fire, be coolness and safety upon Abraham." It was mentioned that when they wanted to burn him, they built a structure for him,

as:

* Musa related to us, saying: Amr related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi, who said regarding ﴿They said: "Build for him a structure and throw him into the blazing fire"﴾: He said: They imprisoned him in a house and gathered firewood for him, until a woman would fall ill and say: "If God restores my health, I will surely gather firewood for Abraham." When they had gathered it and piled up a great deal of firewood, [[A phrase was dropped from this report; al-Tha'labi the exegete mentioned something similar in ʿAra'is al-Majalis, which is: They lit the fire on every side with the firewood, so the fire blazed up, until a bird would pass over it and be burned, etc.]] until the bird would pass by it and be burned from its intense heat, they went to him and raised him to the top of the structure. Abraham ﷺ raised his head to the sky, and the sky, the earth, the mountains and the angels said: "Our Lord, Abraham is being burned for Your sake!" He said: "I know him best. If he calls upon you, then aid him." And Abraham, when he raised his head to the sky, said: "O God, You are the One in the sky, and I am the one on the earth; there is no one on the earth who worships You besides me. Sufficient for me is God, and He is the best Disposer of affairs." Then they cast him into the fire, and He called to it, saying: ﴿O fire, be coolness and safety upon Abraham﴾. It was Gabriel, peace be upon him, who called to it.

Ibn Abbas said: Had its coolness not been followed by safety, Abraham would have died from its intense cold. On that day no fire remained on the earth but was extinguished, thinking that it was the one intended. When the fire was extinguished, they looked at Abraham, and there was another man with him, and Abraham's head was in his lap, wiping the sweat from his face. It is mentioned that this man was the Angel of Shade. God sent down a fire, and the children of Adam benefited from it, and they brought Abraham out and led him in to the king, who had not entered upon him before that.

* Ibrahim ibn al-Miqdam Abu al-Ash'ath related to me, saying: al-Mu'tamir related to us, saying: I heard my father say: Qatadah related to us, from Abu Sulayman, from Ka'b, who said: The fire burned nothing of Abraham except his bonds.

* Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿We said: "O fire, be coolness and safety upon Abraham."﴾ He said: It was mentioned to us that Ka'b used to say: No one among the people benefited from it that day, and Ka'b would say: The fire burned nothing that day except his bonds.

* Muhammad ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Mu'ammal related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, from al-A'mash, from a shaykh, from Ali ibn Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, regarding His saying: ﴿We said: "O fire, be coolness and safety upon Abraham."﴾ He said: It became cold upon him until it nearly killed him, until it was said: "and safety," he said: It did not harm him.

* Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Jabir ibn Nuh related to us, saying: Isma'il informed us, from al-Minhal ibn Amr, who said: Abraham, the Friend of God, said: I was never happier on any days than the days I spent in the fire.

* Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Ya'qub related to us, from Ja'far, from Sa'id, who said: When Abraham, the Friend of God ﷺ, was thrown into the fire, the angel in charge of rain said: "Lord, Your friend Abraham, he hoped that permission would be given to him to send rain." He said: The command of God was swifter than that, and He said: ﴿We said: "O fire, be coolness and safety upon Abraham."﴾ So no fire remained on the earth but was extinguished.

* Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Jarir related to us, from Mughirah, from al-Harith, from Abu Zur'ah, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The finest thing said by the father of Abraham, when the cover was lifted from him while he was in the fire and he found him sweating on his brow, was: "Excellent is the Lord, your Lord, O Abraham!"

* Al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Wahb ibn Sulayman informed me, from Shu'ayb al-Jabasi, who said: Abraham was thrown into the fire when he was sixteen years old, and Isaac was sacrificed when he was seven years old, and Sarah bore him when she was ninety years old, and his place of sacrifice was from the house of Iliya two miles away. When Sarah learned what he intended with Isaac, she fainted for two days and died on the third day. Ibn Jurayj said: Ka'b al-Ahbar said: The fire burned nothing of Abraham except the bonds with which they had tied him.

* Al-Hasan related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman al-Taymi related to us, from some of his companions, who said: Gabriel came to Abraham, peace be upon them both, while he was being bound or swaddled to be thrown into the fire, and said: "O Abraham, do you have a need?" He said: "As for you, no."

* He said: Mu'tamir related to us, saying: Ibn Ka'b related to us, from Arqam: that Abraham said when they began binding him to throw him into the fire: "There is no god but You, glory be to You, Lord of the worlds, to You is praise, and to You is the dominion, You have no partner."

* Al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Abu Ja'far al-Razi, from al-Rabi' ibn Anas, from Abu al-Aliyah, regarding His saying: ﴿We said: "O fire, be coolness and safety upon Abraham."﴾ He said: The safety did not harm him with its coolness; and had He not said "and safety," the cold would have been harsher upon him than the heat.

* Al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, regarding His saying: ﴿coolness﴾, he said: It became cold upon him, ﴿and safety﴾: it did not harm him.

* Ibn Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿We said: "O fire, be coolness and safety upon Abraham."﴾ He said: Ka'b said: No one among the people of the earth benefited from fire that day, and the fire did not burn anything that day except the bonds of Abraham.

Qatadah said: No creature came that day but that the fire was extinguished for him, except the lizard.

Al-Zuhri said: The Prophet ﷺ ordered its killing, and named it "Fuwaysiqa."

* * *

As for His saying: ﴿And they intended a scheme against him﴾

Says God, may His remembrance be exalted: They intended a scheme against Abraham, ﴿but We made them the greatest losers﴾, meaning: the ruined.

* And al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, regarding ﴿And they intended a scheme against him, but We made them the greatest losers﴾, he said: They threw an old man from among them into the fire, hoping to obtain his deliverance, just as Abraham ﷺ was delivered, and he was burned.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 21, verse 71:

The interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿And We delivered him and Lot to the land which We have blessed for the worlds﴾ (21:71).

He, exalted is His mention, says: And We delivered Abraham and Lot from their enemy Nimrod and his people, from the land of Iraq, ﴿to the land which We have blessed for the worlds﴾. It is the land of al-Sham (Syria). He, peace be upon him, separated from his people and their religion and emigrated to al-Sham.

This story which God recounted of the news of Abraham and his people is a reminder from Him to the people of Muhammad ﷺ from Quraysh that they have followed, in their worship of idols, and in their harming of Muhammad for forbidding its worship and for calling them to worship God, sincere to Him in religion, the path of the enemies of their father Abraham and their opposition to his religion. And that Muhammad, in his disavowal of worshipping them and his sincere worship of God, and in his calling them to disavow the idols, and in his patience over what he meets from them in that, is treading the path of his father Abraham; and that He will bring him out from among them, just as He brought Abraham out from among his people when they persisted in their error, to his place of emigration in the land of al-Sham, consoling his prophet Muhammad ﷺ regarding the hardship and harm he meets from his people, and informing him that He will deliver him from them just as He delivered his father Abraham from the disbelievers of his people.

The people of interpretation have differed concerning the land to which God said He delivered Abraham and Lot, and which He described as blessed for the worlds. Some of them said in accordance with what we have said.

Those who said that:

Al-Husayn ibn Hurayth al-Marwazi Abu ʿAmmar narrated to us, saying: al-Fadl ibn Musa narrated to us, from al-Husayn ibn Waqid, from al-Rabiʿ ibn Anas, from Abu al-ʿAliyah, from Ubayy ibn Kaʿb, concerning ﴿And We delivered him and Lot to the land which We have blessed for the worlds﴾, he said: "It is al-Sham, and there is no sweet water except that it springs forth from that rock which is in Bayt al-Maqdis."

Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abu Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Furat al-Qazzaz, from al-Hasan, concerning His words ﴿to the land which We have blessed﴾, he said: "al-Sham."

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words ﴿And We delivered him and Lot to the land which We have blessed for the worlds﴾: "They were in the land of Iraq, and they were delivered to the land of al-Sham. It used to be said that al-Sham is the pillar of the abode of emigration, and whatever is diminished from the land is added to al-Sham, and whatever is diminished from al-Sham is added to Palestine. It used to be said: it is the land of the gathering and the resurrection, the place where people assemble, where ʿIsa son of Maryam will descend, and where God will destroy the leader of misguidance, the lying Dajjal."

Abu Qilabah narrated to us that the Messenger of God ﷺ said: "I saw in a dream as the sleeper sees, as if the angels were carrying the pillar of the Book and placed it in al-Sham. I interpreted it to mean that when tribulations occur, faith will be in al-Sham."

It has been mentioned to us that the Messenger of God ﷺ said one day in his sermon: "There will be an army in al-Sham, an army in Iraq, and an army in Yemen." A man said: "O Messenger of God, choose for me." He said: "Upon you is al-Sham, for God has taken upon Himself to protect al-Sham and its people. Whoever refuses, let him join his Yemen and drink from his well."

It has been mentioned to us that ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, said: "O Kaʿb, will you not move to Medina, for it is the emigration place of the Messenger of God ﷺ and the site of his grave?" Kaʿb said to him: "O Commander of the Believers, I find in the Book of God that was revealed that al-Sham is the treasure of God among His lands, and therein is His treasure among His servants."

al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Maʿmar informed us, from Qatadah, concerning ﴿And We delivered him and Lot to the land which We have blessed for the worlds﴾, he said: "They both emigrated together from Kuthaa to al-Sham."

Musa narrated to us, saying: ʿAmr narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, who said: "Abraham and Lot set out toward al-Sham. Abraham met Sarah, who was the daughter of the king of Harran, and who had criticized her people regarding their religion, and he married her on condition that he would not change her [in Ibn Kathir: on condition that he would flee with her]."

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: "Abraham went out emigrating to his Lord, and Lot went out with him emigrating, and he married Sarah, daughter of his paternal uncle, and went out with her seeking refuge for his religion and security for the worship of his Lord, until he alighted at Harran, and remained there as long as God willed. Then he went out from it emigrating until he came to Egypt, then he went out from Egypt to al-Sham, and alighted at al-Sabʿ from the land of Palestine, which is the desert of al-Sham, and Lot alighted at al-Mu'tafikah, which is from al-Sabʿ at a distance of one day and a night, or nearer than that, and God sent him as a prophet, peace be upon him."

al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, regarding His words ﴿And We delivered him and Lot to the land which We have blessed for the worlds﴾, he said: "He delivered him from the land of Iraq to the land of al-Sham."

al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Abu Jaʿfar al-Razi, from al-Rabiʿ, from Abu al-ʿAliyah, that he said regarding this verse ﴿which We have blessed for the worlds﴾: "There is no sweet water except that it descends to the rock which is in Bayt al-Maqdis; then it disperses through the earth."

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words ﴿And We delivered him and Lot to the land which We have blessed for the worlds﴾: "To al-Sham."

Others said: Rather, it means Mecca, which is the land of which God said ﴿which We have blessed for the worlds﴾.

Those who said that:

Muhammad ibn Saʿd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding His words ﴿And We delivered him and Lot to the land which We have blessed for the worlds﴾: "It means Mecca, and the settling of Ishmael at the House. Do you not see that He says: ﴿Indeed, the first House established for mankind is that at Bakkah, blessed and a guidance for the worlds﴾ (3:96)."

Abu Jaʿfar said: We chose what we chose of the saying in this matter because there is no disagreement among all the people of knowledge that the emigration of Abraham from Iraq was to al-Sham, and there was his residence during his lifetime, although he had come to Mecca, built the House there, and settled his son Ishmael there with his mother Hagar; yet he did not remain there, nor did he take it as a homeland for himself, nor did Lot. God only informed about Abraham and Lot that He delivered them to the land which He blessed for the worlds.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 21, verse 72–73:

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿And We gave him Isaac and Jacob as a additional gift, and We made each of them righteous. And We made them leaders guiding by Our command, and We inspired in them the doing of good deeds, the establishment of prayer, and the giving of zakah, and they were worshippers of Us.﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: And We gave Abraham Isaac as a son, and Jacob, a son's son, as an additional gift to you.

The interpreters differed concerning the meaning of His words ﴿nafilah﴾ (additional gift). Some of them said: It refers to Jacob alone.

Those who said that:

Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, he said: my father narrated to me, he said: my uncle narrated to me, he said: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words ﴿And We gave him Isaac and Jacob as an additional gift﴾: He says: We gave him Isaac as a son, and Jacob, the son of a son, as an additional gift.

Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words ﴿And We gave him Isaac and Jacob as an additional gift﴾: The nafilah is his son's son, Jacob.

Yunus narrated to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words ﴿And We gave him Isaac and Jacob as an additional gift﴾: He asked for one, saying ﴿My Lord, grant me of the righteous﴾, so He gave him one, and added Jacob, and Jacob is a son's son.

Others said: Rather, by that He meant Isaac and Jacob. They said: The meaning of nafilah is only a gift, and both of them were from the bounty of Allah, which He gave them.

Those who said that:

Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, he said: Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, he said: Sufyan narrated to us, from Ibn Juraij, from Ata, regarding His words ﴿And We gave him Isaac and Jacob as an additional gift﴾: He said: a gift.

Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, he said: Abu Asim narrated to us, he said: Isa narrated to us, and al-Harith narrated to me, he said: al-Hasan narrated to us, he said: Warqa' narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿Isaac and Jacob as an additional gift﴾: He said: a bounty.

Al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij, from Mujahid, the like of it.

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: We have already explained earlier that nafilah is the surplus of a thing that comes to a man, whatever that thing may be. Both of his sons, Isaac and Jacob, were a surplus from Allah, a bounty He bestowed upon Abraham and a gift from Him to him. It is permissible that He meant by it that He granted them both to him together as an additional gift from Him, and it is permissible that He meant that He granted him Jacob as an additional gift. No proof indicates which of these is the intended meaning of the speech, so nothing is more appropriate to say about it than what Allah said: "And Allah gave him Isaac and Jacob as an additional gift."

* *

As for His words ﴿And We made each of them righteous﴾:

That is, doers of obedience to Allah, avoiders of His prohibitions. By His words ﴿each﴾ He means Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. As for His words ﴿And We made them leaders guiding by Our command﴾, He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: We made Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob leaders who are followed in goodness, in obedience to Allah, in following His command and prohibition, who are imitated and whose example is followed.

As:

Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words ﴿And We made them leaders﴾: Allah made them leaders who are imitated in the matter of Allah. As for His words ﴿guiding by Our command﴾, He says: they guide people by Allah's command to them in that, and call them to Allah and to His worship. As for His words ﴿And We inspired in them the doing of good deeds﴾, He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: And We inspired, among what We inspired, that they should do good deeds and establish prayer by Our command in that. ﴿And they were worshippers of Us﴾ means: they were humble before Us, not arrogant toward our obedience and worship.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 21, verse 72–73:

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿And We gave him Isaac and Jacob as a additional gift, and We made each of them righteous. And We made them leaders guiding by Our command, and We inspired in them the doing of good deeds, the establishment of prayer, and the giving of zakah, and they were worshippers of Us.﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: And We gave Abraham Isaac as a son, and Jacob, a son's son, as an additional gift to you.

The interpreters differed concerning the meaning of His words ﴿nafilah﴾ (additional gift). Some of them said: It refers to Jacob alone.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 21, verse 74:

The discussion of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And to Lot We gave judgment and knowledge, and We delivered him from the town that was committing abominations. Indeed, they were a people of evil, defiantly disobedient.﴾

He, the Exalted, says: "And We gave Lot judgment," meaning the decisive settlement of disputes between adversaries, "and knowledge," meaning: We also gave him knowledge of the matter of his religion and what he owed to God of His obligations.

There are two possible readings of the case ending of "Lot." The first is that it is in the accusative because it is governed by the conjunction (waw) attached to the verb, as we have said: "And We gave Lot." The second is that it is governed by an implied verb, in the sense of: "And remember Lot."

* *

And His saying ﴿and We delivered him from the town that was committing abominations﴾

He says: "And We delivered him from Our punishment which We sent down upon the people of the town that was committing abominations." This is the town of Sodom, to whose people Lot had been sent. The abominations they committed were: mounting males in their rear passages, pelting people (with pebbles), passing wind openly in their assemblies, along with other evil deeds of wrongdoing they used to commit. So God brought him out, when He willed to destroy them, toward Syria.

As related:

Musa narrated to me, saying: Amr narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, who said: God brought them out, meaning Lot and his two daughters Zaytha and Zar'atha, toward Syria when He willed to destroy his people.

* *

And His saying ﴿Indeed, they were a people of evil, defiantly disobedient﴾

Opposing the command of God, departing from His obedience and from what pleases Him in deeds.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 21, verse 75–77:

The explanation of His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿And We admitted him into Our mercy; indeed, he was among the righteous﴾ [21:75]

Allah, the Exalted, says: And We admitted Lot into Our mercy by saving him from what We brought down upon his people of punishment and affliction, and rescuing him from it, indeed he was among the righteous. That is, indeed Lot was among those who acted in obedience to Us, who submitted to Our command and Our prohibition, and did not disobey Us. Ibn Zayd used to say, regarding the meaning of His saying ﴿And We admitted him into Our mercy﴾:

Yunus narrated to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿And We admitted him into Our mercy﴾, he said: "Into Islam."

* *

The explanation of His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿And Noah, when he called out before; so We responded to him and saved him and his family from the great distress. And We aided him against the people who denied Our signs. Indeed, they were a people of evil, so We drowned them all﴾ [21:76–77]

Allah, the Exalted, says: And mention, O Muhammad, Noah, when he called out to his Lord before you, and before Abraham and Lot, and asked Us to destroy his people, who denied Allah regarding what He threatened them with of His warning, and denied Noah regarding what he brought them of the truth from his Lord. ﴿Noah said, "My Lord, do not leave upon the earth from among the disbelievers an inhabitant"﴾ [71:26], so We responded to his supplication, ﴿and We saved him and his family﴾, meaning by his family: the people of faith from among his offspring and his wives, ﴿from the great distress﴾, meaning by the great distress: the punishment that befell those who denied, from the flood and drowning. The "karb" (distress) is intense grief; it is said from it: "This matter has distressed me (qad karabani), so it distresses me (yakrubuni) with distress (karban)." And His saying: ﴿And We aided him against the people who denied Our signs﴾ says: And We aided Noah against the people who denied Our proofs and evidences, so We saved him from them, and drowned them all. ﴿Indeed, they were a people of evil﴾: Allah, the Exalted, says: indeed the people of Noah who denied Our signs were a people of evil, who committed bad deeds, disobeying Allah and opposing His command.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 21, verse 78–79:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And David and Solomon, when they gave judgment concerning the tilth (al-harth) when the sheep of certain people pastured in it by night; and We were witness to their judgment. So We gave understanding of the matter to Solomon, and to each We gave judgment and knowledge. And We subjected the mountains to glorify [God] along with David, and the birds; and We were doing [it].﴾

His exalted remembrance says to His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ: And mention David and Solomon, O Muhammad, when they gave judgment concerning the tilth.

The interpreters (ahl al-ta'wil) differed concerning what that tilth was. Some of them said: it was plants (nabt).

Those who said that:

- Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from Murrah, concerning His saying ﴿when they gave judgment concerning the tilth﴾, he said: the tilth was plants.

- Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, who said: It was mentioned to us that the sheep of the people fell into the crops by night.

Others said: rather, that tilth was a vineyard (karm).

Those who said that:

- Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: al-Muharibi narrated to us, from Ash'ath, from Abu Ishaq, from Murrah, from Ibn Mas'ud, concerning His saying ﴿And David and Solomon, when they gave judgment concerning the tilth﴾, he said: a vineyard whose clusters had grown.

- Tamim ibn al-Muntasir narrated to us, saying: Ishaq informed us, from Sharik, from Abu Ishaq, from Masruq, from Shurayh, who said: the tilth was a vineyard.

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: The most correct of these sayings is what Allah, blessed and exalted, said: ﴿when they gave judgment concerning the tilth﴾, and the tilth is in fact the cultivation of land; it is permissible that it was crops, and it is permissible that it was planted trees, and ignorance of which of these it was does no harm.

* *

As for His saying ﴿when the sheep of certain people pastured in it﴾:

[[Livestock "nafasha" in the crop means: they scattered into it at night, grazing it without a shepherd with them; the verb ... .]] He says: when the sheep of the other people, not the owners of the tilth, entered this tilth by night, grazing it or spoiling it. ﴿and We were witness to their judgment﴾: He says: and We were witnesses to the judgment of David and Solomon and the people between whom they judged regarding what the sheep of the sheep-owners had damaged of the tilth of the tilth-owners, witnesses from whom nothing is hidden, and whose knowledge is not absent from Us. His saying ﴿So We gave understanding﴾ means: We gave understanding of the case in that matter ﴿to Solomon﴾ rather than David. ﴿and to each We gave judgment and knowledge﴾: He says: and to each of them, David and Solomon and the messengers He mentioned at the beginning of this surah, We gave judgment, which is prophethood, and knowledge: meaning knowledge of the rulings of Allah.

In accordance with what we have said on this, the interpreters said:

- Abu Kurayb and Harun ibn Idris al-Asamm narrated to us, both saying: al-Muharibi narrated to us, from Ash'ath, from Abu Ishaq, from Murrah, from Ibn Mas'ud, concerning His saying ﴿And David and Solomon, when they gave judgment concerning the tilth, when the sheep of certain people pastured in it﴾, he said: a vineyard whose clusters had grown, and they destroyed it. He said: David gave judgment that the sheep belonged to the owner of the vineyard. Solomon said: "Other than this, O Prophet of Allah." He said: "And what is that?" He said: "The vineyard is handed to the owner of the sheep, who tends it until it returns to what it was, and the sheep are handed to the owner of the vineyard, who benefits from them; when the vineyard is as it was, you return the vineyard to its owner and the sheep to their owner." That is His saying ﴿So We gave understanding of the matter to Solomon﴾.

- Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His saying ﴿And David and Solomon, when they gave judgment concerning the tilth﴾ ... to His saying ﴿and We were witness to their judgment﴾, he said: We were witnesses to what they judged. That was because two men entered upon David, one of them the owner of the tilth and the other the owner of the sheep. The owner of the tilth said: "This man let his sheep into my tilth, and it has left nothing of my tilth." David said to him: "Go, for all the sheep are yours." David judged accordingly. The owner of the sheep passed by Solomon and informed him of what David had judged. Solomon entered upon David and they said: "O Prophet of Allah, the judgment is other than what you decided." He said: "How?" Solomon said: "The tilth is not hidden from its owner in what it produces each year, so he may take from the owner of the sheep, by selling their young, wool and hair, until he recovers the value of the tilth, for the sheep have offspring every year." David said: "You are right; the judgment is as you have judged." And Allah gave Solomon understanding of it.

- Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij, from 'Ali ibn Zayd, who said: Khalifah narrated to me, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: David judged the sheep to the owners of the tilth, and the herders went out with their dogs. Solomon said: "How did he judge between you?" They informed him, and he said: "If I had come to your affair, I would have judged other than this." David was informed of that, and he summoned him and said: "How would you judge between them?" He said: "I would hand the sheep to the owners of the tilth, so that they would have their young, their milk, their fleece and their benefits, and the owners of the sheep would plant for the people of the tilth the like of their tilth. When the tilth reaches the state it was in, the owners of the tilth would take back their tilth, and they would return the sheep to their owners."

- Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi Najih narrated to us, from Mujahid, concerning Allah's saying ﴿when the sheep of certain people pastured in it﴾, he said: David gave the owners of the tilth the necks of the sheep in exchange for the tilth, and Solomon judged that the shearing and milk of the sheep belonged to the people of the tilth, and that it was incumbent on them to tend them, and the owners of the sheep were to cultivate the tilth for them until the tilth was as it was on the day it was eaten; then they would hand it to its people and take back their sheep.

- Al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to me, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.

- Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to us similarly, except that he said: and it was incumbent on them to pasture them.

- Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from Murrah, concerning His saying ﴿when the sheep of certain people pastured in it﴾, he said: the tilth was plants, and the sheep grazed in it by night, so they disputed over it before David, who judged the sheep to the owners of the tilth. They passed by Solomon and told him of that. He said: "The sheep should not be handed over, for they would benefit from them, meaning the owners of the tilth, while these people tend to their tilth; when it is as it was, return them to them." Then ﴿So We gave understanding of the matter to Solomon﴾ was revealed.

- Tamim ibn al-Muntasir narrated to us, saying: Ishaq informed us, from Sharik, from Abu Ishaq, from Masruq, from Shurayh, concerning His saying ﴿when the sheep of certain people pastured in it﴾, he said: the grazing was by night, and the tilth was a vineyard. He said: David gave the sheep to the owner of the vineyard. He said: Solomon said: "The owner of the vineyard still has the root of his land and the root of his vineyard, so give him their wool and milk!" He said: this is the saying of Allah ﴿So We gave understanding of the matter to Solomon﴾.

- Ibn Abi Ziyad narrated to us, saying: Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us, saying: Isma'il informed us, from 'Amir, who said: Two men came to Shurayh, and one of them said: "The sheep of this man cut up my spun yarn." Shurayh said: "By day or by night?" He said: "If it was by day, the owner of the sheep is absolved; and if it was by night, he is liable." Then he recited ﴿And David and Solomon, when they gave judgment concerning the tilth, when the sheep of certain people pastured in it﴾ and said: the grazing was by night.

- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Hakkam narrated to us, saying: Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid narrated to us, from 'Amir, from Shurayh, similarly.

- Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, saying: Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid informed us, from al-Sha'bi, from Shurayh, the like of it.

- Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, concerning His saying ﴿And David and Solomon, when they gave judgment concerning the tilth﴾ ... the verse: the nafsh is by night, and the hamal is by day.

It was mentioned to us that the sheep of certain people fell into a crop by night, and the matter was brought to David, who judged the sheep to the owners of the crop. Solomon said: "It is not so; rather, its offspring, its droppings, its milk-yield and its shearing belong to him, until, in the next year, when it is as it was on the day it was eaten, the sheep are handed back to their owner and the owner of the crop takes back his crop." So Allah said ﴿So We gave understanding of the matter to Solomon﴾.

- Ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah and al-Zuhri, concerning ﴿when the sheep of certain people pastured in it﴾, he said: the sheep grazed in the tilth of a people. Al-Zuhri said: nafsh only happens by night. David decided that they should take the sheep; Allah gave Solomon understanding of it. He said: when he was informed of David's judgment, he said: "No, but take the sheep, and you shall have what comes from their droppings, their offspring and their wool until the year's end."

- Al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, concerning His saying ﴿when the sheep of certain people pastured in it﴾, he said: in the tilth of a people. Ma'mar said: al-Zuhri said: nafsh only happens by night, and hamal by day. Qatadah said: He judged that they should take the sheep, and Allah gave Solomon understanding of it. Then he mentioned the rest of the report, similar to the report of Ibn 'Abd al-A'la.

- Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His saying ﴿And David and Solomon, when they gave judgment concerning the tilth, when the sheep of certain people pastured in it﴾ ... the two verses: The sheep of a man got loose and ate the tilth of a man, so he came to David, who judged that the sheep belonged to the owner of the tilth in compensation for what they ate, and he seemed to see that this was the right course. They passed by Solomon, who said: "What has the Prophet of Allah judged between you?" They informed him, and he said: "Shall I not judge between you two, in case you are both content with it?" They said: "Yes." He said: "As for you, owner of the tilth, take this man's sheep and be with them as their owner was, drinking from their milk, their droppings, and such-and-such, what their owner used to receive. And as for you, owner of the sheep, cultivate this man's tilth until his tilth is like it was; on the night his tilth was grazed by your sheep, give him back his tilth and take your sheep." That is the saying of Allah, blessed and exalted: ﴿And David and Solomon, when they gave judgment concerning the tilth, when the sheep of certain people pastured in it﴾, and he recited until His saying ﴿and to each We gave judgment and knowledge﴾.

- Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij, from 'Ata' al-Khurasani, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His saying ﴿when the sheep of certain people pastured in it﴾, he said: they grazed.

- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: al-nafsh is the grazing of livestock at night.

- He said: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from al-Zuhri, from Haram ibn Muhayyisah ibn Mas'ud, who said: "A camel of al-Bara' ibn 'Azib entered a garden of one of the Ansar and spoiled it. The matter was brought to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he judged that the owner of the camel must compensate for what the camel had spoiled, and said: 'For the owners of livestock is the guarding of their livestock by night, and for the owners of gardens is the guarding of their gardens by day.'"

Al-Zuhri said: The judgment of David and Solomon in that was that a man's livestock entered a man's crop and spoiled it, and nafsh only occurs by night. They went to David, who judged the livestock of the owner of the livestock to the owner of the crop. They departed and passed by Solomon, who said: "By what did the Prophet of Allah judge between you?" They said: "He judged the livestock to the owner of the crop." He said: "Indeed, the judgment would be other than this. Come back with me!" He went to his father David and said: "O Prophet of Allah, did you judge this man's sheep to the owner of the crop?" He said: "Yes." He said: "O Prophet of Allah, the judgment would be other than this." He said: "And how, my son?" He said: "Hand the sheep to the owner of the crop, so that he benefits from their milk, their fat and their fleece, and hand the crop to the owner of the sheep, who tends it; when the crop returns to the state in which the sheep damaged it, return the sheep to the owner of the sheep and return the crop to the owner of the crop." David said: "May Allah not cut off your mouth," and he judged by what Solomon had judged. Al-Zuhri said: That is the saying of Allah, ﴿And David and Solomon, when they gave judgment concerning the tilth﴾ ... to His saying ﴿judgment and knowledge﴾.

- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, and 'Ali ibn Mujahid, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, who said: One who heard al-Hasan told me: the judgment was by what Solomon judged, and Allah did not reproach David for his judgment.

* *

As for His saying ﴿And We subjected the mountains to glorify [God] along with David, and the birds﴾:

His exalted remembrance says: We subjected the mountains with David, and the birds glorifying along with him when he glorified.

Qatadah used to say concerning the meaning of His saying ﴿yusabbihna﴾ in this place:

- Bishr narrated to us with it, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, concerning His saying ﴿And We subjected the mountains to glorify [God] along with David, and the birds﴾: that is, they pray with David when he prays.

* *

As for His saying ﴿and We were doing [it]﴾:

He says: We had decreed that We would do it, and We would subject the mountains and the birds to David, peace be upon him, in the Mother of the Book.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 21, verse 78–79:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And David and Solomon, when they gave judgment concerning the tilth (al-harth) when the sheep of certain people pastured in it by night; and We were witness to their judgment. So We gave understanding of the matter to Solomon, and to each We gave judgment and knowledge. And We subjected the mountains to glorify [God] along with David, and the birds; and We were doing [it].﴾

His exalted remembrance says to His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ: And mention David and Solomon, O Muhammad, when they gave judgment concerning the tilth.

The interpreters (ahl al-ta'wil) differed concerning what that tilth was. Some of them said: it was plants (nabt).

Those who said that:

- Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from Murrah, concerning His saying ﴿when they gave judgment concerning the tilth﴾, he said: the tilth was plants.

- Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, who said: It was mentioned to us that the sheep of the people fell into the crops by night.

Others said: rather, that tilth was a vineyard (karm).

Those who said that:

- Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: al-Muharibi narrated to us, from Ash'ath, from Abu Ishaq, from Murrah, from Ibn Mas'ud, concerning His saying ﴿And David and Solomon, when they gave judgment concerning the tilth﴾, he said: a vineyard whose clusters had grown.

- Tamim ibn al-Muntasir narrated to us, saying: Ishaq informed us, from Sharik, from Abu Ishaq, from Masruq, from Shurayh, who said: the tilth was a vineyard.

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: The most correct of these sayings is what Allah, blessed and exalted, said: ﴿when they gave judgment concerning the tilth﴾, and the tilth is in fact the cultivation of land; it is permissible that it was crops, and it is permissible that it was planted trees, and ignorance of which of these it was does no harm.

* *

As for His saying ﴿when the sheep of certain people pastured in it﴾:

[[Livestock "nafasha" in the crop means: they scattered into it at night, grazing it without a shepherd with them; the verb ... .]] He says: when the sheep of the other people, not the owners of the tilth, entered this tilth by night, grazing it or spoiling it. ﴿and We were witness to their judgment﴾: He says: and We were witnesses to the judgment of David and Solomon and the people between whom they judged regarding what the sheep of the sheep-owners had damaged of the tilth of the tilth-owners, witnesses from whom nothing is hidden, and whose knowledge is not absent from Us. His saying ﴿So We gave understanding﴾ means: We gave understanding of the case in that matter ﴿to Solomon﴾ rather than David. ﴿and to each We gave judgment and knowledge﴾: He says: and to each of them, David and Solomon and the messengers He mentioned at the beginning of this surah, We gave judgment, which is prophethood, and knowledge: meaning knowledge of the rulings of Allah.

In accordance with what we have said on this, the interpreters said:

- Abu Kurayb and Harun ibn Idris al-Asamm narrated to us, both saying: al-Muharibi narrated to us, from Ash'ath, from Abu Ishaq, from Murrah, from Ibn Mas'ud, concerning His saying ﴿And David and Solomon, when they gave judgment concerning the tilth, when the sheep of certain people pastured in it﴾, he said: a vineyard whose clusters had grown, and they destroyed it. He said: David gave judgment that the sheep belonged to the owner of the vineyard. Solomon said: "Other than this, O Prophet of Allah." He said: "And what is that?" He said: "The vineyard is handed to the owner of the sheep, who tends it until it returns to what it was, and the sheep are handed to the owner of the vineyard, who benefits from them; when the vineyard is as it was, you return the vineyard to its owner and the sheep to their owner." That is His saying ﴿So We gave understanding of the matter to Solomon﴾.

- Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His saying ﴿And David and Solomon, when they gave judgment concerning the tilth﴾ ... to His saying ﴿and We were witness to their judgment﴾, he said: We were witnesses to what they judged. That was because two men entered upon David, one of them the owner of the tilth and the other the owner of the sheep. The owner of the tilth said: "This man let his sheep into my tilth, and it has left nothing of my tilth." David said to him: "Go, for all the sheep are yours." David judged accordingly. The owner of the sheep passed by Solomon and informed him of what David had judged. Solomon entered upon David and they said: "O Prophet of Allah, the judgment is other than what you decided." He said: "How?" Solomon said: "The tilth is not hidden from its owner in what it produces each year, so he may take from the owner of the sheep, by selling their young, wool and hair, until he recovers the value of the tilth, for the sheep have offspring every year." David said: "You are right; the judgment is as you have judged." And Allah gave Solomon understanding of it.

- Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij, from 'Ali ibn Zayd, who said: Khalifah narrated to me, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: David judged the sheep to the owners of the tilth, and the herders went out with their dogs. Solomon said: "How did he judge between you?" They informed him, and he said: "If I had come to your affair, I would have judged other than this." David was informed of that, and he summoned him and said: "How would you judge between them?" He said: "I would hand the sheep to the owners of the tilth, so that they would have their young, their milk, their fleece and their benefits, and the owners of the sheep would plant for the people of the tilth the like of their tilth. When the tilth reaches the state it was in, the owners of the tilth would take back their tilth, and they would return the sheep to their owners."

- Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi Najih narrated to us, from Mujahid, concerning Allah's saying ﴿when the sheep of certain people pastured in it﴾, he said: David gave the owners of the tilth the necks of the sheep in exchange for the tilth, and Solomon judged that the shearing and milk of the sheep belonged to the people of the tilth, and that it was incumbent on them to tend them, and the owners of the sheep were to cultivate the tilth for them until the tilth was as it was on the day it was eaten; then they would hand it to its people and take back their sheep.

- Al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to me, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.

- Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to us similarly, except that he said: and it was incumbent on them to pasture them.

- Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from Murrah, concerning His saying ﴿when the sheep of certain people pastured in it﴾, he said: the tilth was plants, and the sheep grazed in it by night, so they disputed over it before David, who judged the sheep to the owners of the tilth. They passed by Solomon and told him of that. He said: "The sheep should not be handed over, for they would benefit from them, meaning the owners of the tilth, while these people tend to their tilth; when it is as it was, return them to them." Then ﴿So We gave understanding of the matter to Solomon﴾ was revealed.

- Tamim ibn al-Muntasir narrated to us, saying: Ishaq informed us, from Sharik, from Abu Ishaq, from Masruq, from Shurayh, concerning His saying ﴿when the sheep of certain people pastured in it﴾, he said: the grazing was by night, and the tilth was a vineyard. He said: David gave the sheep to the owner of the vineyard. He said: Solomon said: "The owner of the vineyard still has the root of his land and the root of his vineyard, so give him their wool and milk!" He said: this is the saying of Allah ﴿So We gave understanding of the matter to Solomon﴾.

- Ibn Abi Ziyad narrated to us, saying: Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us, saying: Isma'il informed us, from 'Amir, who said: Two men came to Shurayh, and one of them said: "The sheep of this man cut up my spun yarn." Shurayh said: "By day or by night?" He said: "If it was by day, the owner of the sheep is absolved; and if it was by night, he is liable." Then he recited ﴿And David and Solomon, when they gave judgment concerning the tilth, when the sheep of certain people pastured in it﴾ and said: the grazing was by night.

- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Hakkam narrated to us, saying: Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid narrated to us, from 'Amir, from Shurayh, similarly.

- Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, saying: Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid informed us, from al-Sha'bi, from Shurayh, the like of it.

- Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, concerning His saying ﴿And David and Solomon, when they gave judgment concerning the tilth﴾ ... the verse: the nafsh is by night, and the hamal is by day.

It was mentioned to us that the sheep of certain people fell into a crop by night, and the matter was brought to David, who judged the sheep to the owners of the crop. Solomon said: "It is not so; rather, its offspring, its droppings, its milk-yield and its shearing belong to him, until, in the next year, when it is as it was on the day it was eaten, the sheep are handed back to their owner and the owner of the crop takes back his crop." So Allah said ﴿So We gave understanding of the matter to Solomon﴾.

- Ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah and al-Zuhri, concerning ﴿when the sheep of certain people pastured in it﴾, he said: the sheep grazed in the tilth of a people. Al-Zuhri said: nafsh only happens by night. David decided that they should take the sheep; Allah gave Solomon understanding of it. He said: when he was informed of David's judgment, he said: "No, but take the sheep, and you shall have what comes from their droppings, their offspring and their wool until the year's end."

- Al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, concerning His saying ﴿when the sheep of certain people pastured in it﴾, he said: in the tilth of a people. Ma'mar said: al-Zuhri said: nafsh only happens by night, and hamal by day. Qatadah said: He judged that they should take the sheep, and Allah gave Solomon understanding of it. Then he mentioned the rest of the report, similar to the report of Ibn 'Abd al-A'la.

- Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His saying ﴿And David and Solomon, when they gave judgment concerning the tilth, when the sheep of certain people pastured in it﴾ ... the two verses: The sheep of a man got loose and ate the tilth of a man, so he came to David, who judged that the sheep belonged to the owner of the tilth in compensation for what they ate, and he seemed to see that this was the right course. They passed by Solomon, who said: "What has the Prophet of Allah judged between you?" They informed him, and he said: "Shall I not judge between you two, in case you are both content with it?" They said: "Yes." He said: "As for you, owner of the tilth, take this man's sheep and be with them as their owner was, drinking from their milk, their droppings, and such-and-such, what their owner used to receive. And as for you, owner of the sheep, cultivate this man's tilth until his tilth is like it was; on the night his tilth was grazed by your sheep, give him back his tilth and take your sheep." That is the saying of Allah, blessed and exalted: ﴿And David and Solomon, when they gave judgment concerning the tilth, when the sheep of certain people pastured in it﴾, and he recited until His saying ﴿and to each We gave judgment and knowledge﴾.

- Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij, from 'Ata' al-Khurasani, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His saying ﴿when the sheep of certain people pastured in it﴾, he said: they grazed.

- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: al-nafsh is the grazing of livestock at night.

- He said: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from al-Zuhri, from Haram ibn Muhayyisah ibn Mas'ud, who said: "A camel of al-Bara' ibn 'Azib entered a garden of one of the Ansar and spoiled it. The matter was brought to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he judged that the owner of the camel must compensate for what the camel had spoiled, and said: 'For the owners of livestock is the guarding of their livestock by night, and for the owners of gardens is the guarding of their gardens by day.'"

Al-Zuhri said: The judgment of David and Solomon in that was that a man's livestock entered a man's crop and spoiled it, and nafsh only occurs by night. They went to David, who judged the livestock of the owner of the livestock to the owner of the crop. They departed and passed by Solomon, who said: "By what did the Prophet of Allah judge between you?" They said: "He judged the livestock to the owner of the crop." He said: "Indeed, the judgment would be other than this. Come back with me!" He went to his father David and said: "O Prophet of Allah, did you judge this man's sheep to the owner of the crop?" He said: "Yes." He said: "O Prophet of Allah, the judgment would be other than this." He said: "And how, my son?" He said: "Hand the sheep to the owner of the crop, so that he benefits from their milk, their fat and their fleece, and hand the crop to the owner of the sheep, who tends it; when the crop returns to the state in which the sheep damaged it, return the sheep to the owner of the sheep and return the crop to the owner of the crop." David said: "May Allah not cut off your mouth," and he judged by what Solomon had judged. Al-Zuhri said: That is the saying of Allah, ﴿And David and Solomon, when they gave judgment concerning the tilth﴾ ... to His saying ﴿judgment and knowledge﴾.

- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, and 'Ali ibn Mujahid, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, who said: One who heard al-Hasan told me: the judgment was by what Solomon judged, and Allah did not reproach David for his judgment.

* *

As for His saying ﴿And We subjected the mountains to glorify [God] along with David, and the birds﴾:

His exalted remembrance says: We subjected the mountains with David, and the birds glorifying along with him when he glorified.

Qatadah used to say concerning the meaning of His saying ﴿yusabbihna﴾ in this place:

- Bishr narrated to us with it, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, concerning His saying ﴿And We subjected the mountains to glorify [God] along with David, and the birds﴾: that is, they pray with David when he prays.

* *

As for His saying ﴿and We were doing [it]﴾:

He says: We had decreed that We would do it, and We would subject the mountains and the birds to David, peace be upon him, in the Mother of the Book.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 21, verse 80:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We taught him the making of coats of mail for you, to protect you from your violence. Then will you be grateful?﴾

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: We taught Dawud the crafting of a coat of mail for you. Among the Arabs, al-labus (coat of mail, armour) means all weaponry, whether it is a coat of mail, a jawshan (armour), a sword or a spear. The verse of al-Hudhali is evidence for this:

"And with me is a labus for the fight, as if it were a horn on the forehead of a fleeing bull of wild cattle"

[The verse is in (Lisan al-Arab: lbs). Al-labus is what is worn; al-labus means clothing and weaponry, and it is masculine. If you take it to mean a coat of mail, you make it feminine. Allah, exalted is He, said: (And We taught him the making of labus for you). They said: it is the coat of mail worn in battles.

The author cited the verse as evidence that al-labus is general to all weaponry: the coat of mail, the sword, the spear and the jawshan. The simile in the verse supports what the author said, because the poet compares a spear to the horn of a fleeing bull, which defends its cattle, and they are the wild oxen.]

He describes a spear with that, but in this context the people of interpretation said: it means coats of mail.

Mention of those who said that:

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿And We taught him the making of coats of mail for you﴾ ... the verse, he said: Before Dawud there were plates; and he said: the first to make this ring-mail and link it was Dawud.

* Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah ﴿And We taught him the making of coats of mail for you﴾, he said: They were plates, and the first to weave and link them was Dawud, peace be upon him.

The reciters differed regarding the reading of His saying ﴿li-tuhsinakum﴾. The majority of the reciters of the major cities read ﴿liyuhsinakum﴾ with a yā', meaning: the coat of mail protects you from your violence; they made it masculine to match the masculine noun labus. Abu Ja'far Yazid ibn al-Qa'qa' read ﴿lituhsinakum﴾ with a tā', meaning: the craft protects you; he made it feminine to match the feminine noun ṣan'ah. Shaybah ibn Nisah and Asim ibn Abi al-Najud read ﴿linuhsinakum﴾ with a nūn, meaning: We protect you from your violence.

Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of these readings in my view is the reading of those who read it with a yā', because it is the reading upon which the majority of the reciters of the major cities agree. Although the three readings we have mentioned have closely related meanings, since the craft is the coat of mail and the coat of mail is the craft, and God is the one by whom one is protected from violence, and He is the one who protects through making it so. The meaning of His saying ﴿liyuhsinakum﴾ is "to keep you safe," from the saying "Fulan has secured (ahsana) his slave-girl," and we have already explained this meaning with its evidence earlier. Al-ba's means fighting. The meaning is: We taught Dawud the making of weapons for you, so that they keep you safe when you wear them and meet your enemies in them, from being killed.

* *

As for His saying ﴿Then will you be grateful?﴾

He says: Will you, O people, be thankful to God for His blessing upon you in teaching you the craft of the coat of mail that protects in war and His other blessings upon you? He means: then give thanks to Me for that.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 21, verse 81:

On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿And to Solomon [We subjected] the wind, blowing forcefully, running by his command toward the land which We had blessed. And We are ever, of all things, Knowing.﴾

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: ﴿And⦆ We subjected ﴿to Solomon﴾ the son of David ﴿the wind, blowing forcefully﴾, and its blowing forcefully means the intensity of its gusting; ﴿running by his command toward the land which We had blessed﴾. He says: the wind runs by Solomon's command toward the land which We had blessed, meaning: toward Syria. That is because it would carry Solomon and his companions wherever Solomon wished, and then return him to his dwelling in Syria. Therefore it was said: ﴿toward the land which We had blessed﴾.

As follows:

* Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Salamah narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from some people of knowledge, from Wahb ibn Munabbih, who said: When Solomon went out to his assembly, the birds would gather around him, and the jinn and humans would stand for him until he sat upon his throne. He was a man of frequent campaigns, rarely sitting out of raiding, and he would not hear of a king in any region of the earth without coming to him until he subdued him. It is claimed that when he wished to campaign, he would order his army, and they would erect for him a structure of wood, then set him upon the wood, then load upon it the people, the beasts, and all the instruments of war. When it had carried what he wanted, he would command the forceful wind, and it would enter beneath that wood and lift it up. When it rose, he would command the gentle breeze, and it would carry him for a month in his morning journey and a month in his evening journey to wherever he wished. God, mighty and majestic, says: ﴿So We subjected to him the wind, running gently by his command, wherever he intended﴾ [38:36], and ﴿And to Solomon the wind: its morning journey was a month and its evening journey was a month﴾ [34:12]. He said: It was mentioned to me that a dwelling by the Tigris had written upon it an inscription written by one of Solomon's companions, either from the jinn or from humans: "We alighted here, and we did not build it; it was built and we found it. We set out from Istakhr in the morning and said it, and we, God willing, are departing from it, resting in Syria."

* Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words ﴿And to Solomon the wind, blowing forcefully﴾ ... to His words ﴿and We were guardians over them﴾. He said: God made Solomon the heir of David; He gave him his prophethood and his kingdom, and additionally subjected to him the wind and the devils.

* Yunus narrated to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words ﴿And to Solomon the wind, blowing forcefully, running by his command﴾: "Blowing forcefully, a severe gust, running by his command toward the land which We had blessed," he said: "Syria."

The readers differed concerning the recitation of His words ﴿And to Solomon the wind﴾. The majority of the readers of the major cities recited it in the accusative (al-nasb), according to the meaning we have mentioned. ʿAbd al-Rahman al-Aʿraj recited it as ﴿al-rīḥu﴾ in the nominative (raf'), as an inchoative statement about Solomon, meaning that the wind belongs to Solomon.

Abu Ja'far said: The recitation which I do not permit to recite otherwise is that upon which the readers of the major cities agree, due to the consensus (ijma') of the authoritative readers upon it.

* *

As for His words ﴿And We were, of all things, Knowing﴾:

He says: And We were knowing that what We did for Solomon, by subjecting to him [the wind], and giving him what We gave him of kingship and the welfare of creation, We did with knowledge of the place of what We did for him of that; and We are knowing of all things, nothing of them being hidden from Us.

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And of the devils were those who dived for him and performed other work than that; and We were guardians over them.﴾ (21:82)

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: And We also subjected to Solomon some of the devils, who dove for him in the sea, and performed work other than that, such as construction, statues, and prayer niches (mihrabs). ﴿And We were guardians over them﴾ means: We were guardians over their works and their numbers, and the preservation of all of that does not burden Us.

**Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 21, verses 83–84 (part 1 of 4):**

On the interpretation of His words, ﴿And Job, when he called out to his Lord, "Indeed, adversity has touched me, and You are the Most Merciful of the merciful." So We responded to him and removed what afflicted him of adversity, and We gave him his family and the like of them with them, as a mercy from Us and a reminder for the worshippers.﴾

His saying, may His remembrance be exalted, to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): "And mention Job, O Muhammad, when he called out to his Lord while adversity and affliction had touched him. ﴿My Lord, indeed adversity has touched me, and You are the Most Merciful of the merciful. So We responded to him.﴾" That is, may His remembrance be exalted: We responded to Job's supplication when he called out to Us, so We removed from him the harm, affliction and hardship that he had. The harm that befell him and the affliction that descended upon him were a trial and a test from Allah for him.

The cause of that was, as related:
