Muhammad ibn Sahl ibn Askar al-Bukhari narrated to me, saying: Isma'il ibn Abd al-Karim ibn Hisham narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Samad ibn Ma'qil narrated to me [[Abd al-Samad ibn Ma'qil, with a kasra on the qaf, al-Yamani; he narrates from his paternal uncle Wahb ibn Munabbih, and from him his nephew Isma'il ibn Abd al-Karim. Ahmad declared him trustworthy. He died in the year 183 AH. (From al-Khulasa.) This narration is among the reports of the People of the Book, narrated by Wahb, Ka'b and others from the People of the Book, as al-Tha'labi said in ʿAra'is al-Majalis (pp. 153–163), edition of the Sharikat Maktabah wa Matba'ah Mustafa al-Babi al-Halabi wa Awladihi in Cairo. Its origin is in the Bible, the Book of Job (chapters 7–8, verses 93–833).]], who said: I heard Wahb ibn Munabbih say: The beginning of the matter of Job, the truthful (al-Siddiq, the one who is sincerely truthful), may Allah's blessings be upon him, was that he was patient, an excellent servant.

Wahb said: Gabriel has a station before Allah that none of the angels has in nearness to Allah and in merit before Him, and Gabriel is the one who receives the speech. When Allah mentions a servant with good, Gabriel receives it from Him, then Michael receives it, and around them are the angels brought near, encircling the Throne. That spreads among the angels brought near, and the blessing upon that servant becomes the prayer of the inhabitants of the heavens. When the angels of the heavens bless him, they descend with the blessing to the angels of the earth. Iblis was not barred from anything in the heavens; he would stand in them wherever he wished. From there he reached Adam when He expelled him from Paradise. He continued like that, ascending through the heavens, until Allah raised Jesus, son of Mary. Then he was barred from four, and he used to ascend through three. When Allah sent Muhammad (ﷺ), he was barred from the remaining three, so he and all his armies are barred from all the heavens until the Day of Resurrection. ﴿Except one who steals a hearing, and he is pursued by a clear flaming fire.﴾ That is why the jinn denied what they had known when they said: ﴿And that we had touched the heaven and found it filled with severe guards and burning flames … ﴾ up to His saying ﴿a watching flame.﴾

Wahb said: Iblis was not alarmed except by the responses of the angels of the heavens blessing Job, and that was when Allah mentioned him and praised him. When Iblis heard the prayer of the angels, envy and resentment seized him. He rose swiftly until he stood before Allah in the place where he used to stand, and said: "O my God, I considered Your servant Job, and I found him a servant upon whom You bestowed blessings and he thanked You, and You granted him health and he praised You. Then You did not test him with hardship, nor did You try him with affliction. I guarantee to You that if You strike him with affliction, he will disbelieve in You, he will forget You, and he will worship other than You." Allah, blessed and exalted, said to him: "Go, for I have given you power over his wealth, since that is the matter for which you claim he will thank Me. You have no authority over his body, nor over his mind."

The enemy of Allah swooped down until he fell to the earth. Then he gathered the demonic devils and their chiefs. Job had al-Bashaniyyah in all of Syria, with everything in it from east to west, and he had there a thousand sheep with their shepherds, and five hundred ploughs following them, with five hundred servants, each servant having a wife, a child and wealth, and each plough carrying the equipment of a she-ass, and every she-ass having offspring of two, three, four, five, and more.

When Iblis gathered the devils, he said to them: "What power and knowledge do you have? I have been given power over the wealth of Job, and it is a grievous calamity and a trial which men cannot bear patiently." One demon from the devils said: "I have been given such power that, if I wish, I can transform myself into a whirlwind of fire, and I burn everything I come upon." Iblis said to him: "Go to the camels and their herdsmen." So he set out aiming for the camels, at the time when they had lowered their heads and settled in their pastures. People had not noticed until a fire-whirlwind erupted from beneath the earth, from which blew the winds of poison. No one drew near it without being burned. It continued burning them and their herdsmen until it had consumed the last of them. When he had finished with them, Iblis took the form of one of the camels with its herdsman, then set out aiming for Job, until he found him standing in prayer. He said: "O Job." He said: "Here I am." He said: "Do you know what your Lord has done? He has done it with your camels and their herdsmen, the One whom you chose, worshipped and affirmed as one." Job said: "It is His wealth, which He lent to me, and He has more right to it; when He wills He takes it back. I have long settled my soul and my wealth for perishing." Iblis said: "Your Lord has sent a fire upon them from the sky, and they and their herdsmen have burned, until it consumed the last thing of theirs and of their herdsmen." Then the people were left bewildered, standing over them and wondering. Some of them said: "Job did not worship anything, and he was only in delusion." Others said: "If the God of Job could prevent any of that, He would have protected His friend." Others said: "Rather, He did what He did to make his enemy gloat and to grieve his friend."

Job said: "Praise be to Allah, who gave me and who took from me. I came out naked from my mother's womb, and I will return naked to the earth, and naked I will be gathered to Allah. It is not fitting for you to rejoice when Allah lends you, and to despair when He takes back His loan. Allah has more right over you, and over what He gave you. If Allah had known good in you, O servant, He would have taken your soul along with the Angel of Souls, and He would have rewarded you for it and made you a martyr. But He knew evil from you, so He delayed you for its sake. Allah has stripped you of calamity and freed you from affliction, as chaff is separated from wheat, the separation."

Then Iblis returned to his companions, humiliated and abased, and said to them: "What power do you have, for I have not moved his heart?" A demon from their great ones said: "I have such power that if I wish, I can let out a cry that no living soul hears without his spirit leaving him." Iblis said to him: "Go to the sheep and their shepherds." So he set out aiming for the sheep and their shepherds, until, when he was in their midst, he gave a cry, and they all dropped dead from the last of them to the first, along with their shepherds. Then Iblis went out in the form of the steward of the shepherds [[What is meant by the steward of the shepherds: the agent of the owner of the property, in charge of managing his affairs.]], until he came to Job and found him standing in prayer. He said to him the first words, and Job gave him the first answer. Then Iblis returned to his companions and said: "What power do you have, for I have not moved Job's heart?" One of their great ones said: "I have power such that if I wish, I can turn into a violent wind that scatters everything I touch, until I leave nothing." Iblis said to him: "Go to the ploughs and the tillage." So he set out aiming for them, at the time when they had gathered the ploughs and begun the tillage, while the she-asses and their offspring were grazing. They did not notice until a violent wind blew, scattering everything of that, until it was as if it had never been. Then Iblis went out in the form of the steward of the tillage, until he came to Job, who was standing in prayer, and said to him the like of his first words, and Job answered him the like of his first answer.

When Iblis saw that he had destroyed Job's wealth without success, he rose swiftly until he stood before Allah in the station where he used to stand, and said: "O my God, Job considers that You did not provide for him through his own person and his children. So You give him wealth. Will You then give me power over his children? For that is a misleading trial and a calamity which the hearts of men cannot withstand, nor can their patience endure it." Allah, exalted, said to him: "Go, for I have given you power over his children, but you have no authority over his heart, nor over his body, nor over his mind." The enemy of Allah swooped down like a horse, until he came to the sons of Job while they were in their palace. He continued shaking them until it collapsed from its foundations. Then he began to make the walls collide with one another, and threw at them wood and stones, until he had mutilated them in every way. Then he raised the palace with them, until, when he lifted it with them inside, they were turned upside down. Then he went to Job, in the form of the teacher who used to instruct them in wisdom, wounded, with a split face, his blood and brains flowing, altered and almost unrecognizable because of the extent of the change and the mutilation in which he came. When Job saw him, he was dismayed, grieved, and his eyes shed tears, and he said to him: "O Job, if you had seen how I escaped from where I escaped, and the one who hurled us down upon us from above and from below. And if you had seen how your sons were tortured, and how they were mutilated, and how they were overturned so that they were upside down on their heads, their blood and brains flowing from their noses and their insides, dripping from their eyelids. And if you had seen how their bellies were split open, so that their intestines were scattered. And if you had seen how they were struck with wood and stones, their brains crushed, and how the wood broke their bones, tore their skins, and cut their sinews. And if you had seen the sinews bare, and if you had seen the bones shattered within their bodies, and if you had seen the faces smashed, and if you had seen the walls colliding over them, and if you had seen what I saw, it would have broken your heart." He continued saying this and similar things, and kept softening him, until Job softened and wept, and took a handful of dust and placed it on his head. Then Iblis seized the opportunity from him at that moment, and rose swiftly, delighted with the anguish of Job. Then Job did not delay until he returned to himself and regained his sight, and sought forgiveness. His fellow angels ascended with his repentance, and they hurried ahead of Iblis to Allah, and found that He already knew of the repentance of Job which had been raised to Him. Iblis stood, disgraced and humiliated, and said: "O my God, what made Job bear the loss of wealth and children lightly is that he considers that You did not provide for him through his own person. So You restore to him his wealth and his children. Will You then give me power over his body? I guarantee to You that if You afflict him in his body, he will forget You, disbelieve in You, and deny Your favour." Allah said: "Go, for I have given you power over his body, but you have no authority over his tongue, nor over his heart, nor over his mind."

The enemy of Allah swooped down like a horse and found Job prostrating. He hurried before he could raise his head, and came at him from the direction of the earth, at the place of his face. He blew into his nostril a blast from which his body caught fire, and it swelled up, and boils like the rumps of sheep sprouted on him, and an itch fell upon him that he could not control. He scratched himself with his fingernails until they all fell off. Then he scratched with bones, with rough stones, and with pieces of coarse hair-cloth. He continued scratching until his flesh was consumed and cut. When Job's skin rotted, changed and stank, the people of the town expelled him, and they placed him on a dunghill and made him a shelter. All of Allah's creatures abandoned him except his wife, who would go to him with what would set him right and sustain him. Three of his companions had followed his religion, but when they saw what Allah had afflicted him with, they abandoned him without leaving his religion, and they accused him. They were called Bildad, Eliphaz and Zophar [[The names of Job's three companions appear in the Bible, p. 795, namely: Eliphaz the Temanite, Bildad the Shuhite, and Zophar the Naamathite.]]. He said: The three of them went to him while he was in his affliction, and rebuked him. When he heard from them, he turned to his Lord and said, Job (ﷺ): "My Lord, for what reason did You create me? If You had wanted to abandon me when You had disliked me in goodness, You would not have created me. Would that I had been a miscarriage which my mother cast forth, and would that I had died in her womb, so that I had known nothing and You had not known me. What sin have I committed that no one else has committed, and what deed have I done that You have turned away Your noble face from me? If You had caused me to die and joined me to my fathers, death would have been more fitting for me. There is an example for me in the sultans, before whom armies were arrayed, who struck with swords those who stood against them, out of miserliness with their lives and eagerness for their survival. They became crouching in their graves, until they thought that they would be immortal. And there is an example for me in the kings who hoarded treasures, filled storehouses, gathered hosts, and thought that they would be immortal. And there is an example for me in the tyrants who built cities and fortresses, and lived in them for hundreds of years, then they became ruins, a refuge for wild beasts and a dwelling for devils."

Eliphaz the Temanite said: "Your affair has defeated us, O Job. If we speak to you, we find no room in you for speech, and if we keep silent about you, in view of the affliction we see in you, that is upon us. We used to see from your deeds actions for which we hoped you would receive reward, other than what we now see. A man reaps only what he sowed, and he is repaid for what he did. I call to witness Allah, whose greatness no one can measure, and whose blessings cannot be counted, who sends down water from the sky by which He gives life to the dead, who raises the lowly, and who strengthens the weak. Before whose wisdom the wisdom of the wise goes astray, and before whose knowledge the knowledge of the learned is confounded, until you see them in darkness, in ignorance, groping about. Whoever hopes for the help of Allah, He is the Strong, and whoever relies upon Him is sufficed. He is the One who breaks and mends, who wounds and heals."

Job said: "That is why I was silent, and I bit upon my tongue, and I lowered my head because of the ill treatment, for I knew that His punishment had changed the light of my face, and that His might had removed the strength of my body. I am His servant. What He decreed upon me has befallen me, and I have no strength except what He has laden upon me. Even if my bones were of iron, my body of copper, and my heart of stone, I could not bear this matter. But He has tested me, and He bears it for me. You came to me angry, you feared before being made to fear, and you wept before being struck. What would I do if I said to you: Give charity from your wealth on my behalf, perhaps Allah will free me, or offer a sacrifice on my behalf, perhaps Allah will accept it from me and be pleased with me. When I awake I wish for sleep, hoping to find rest, and when I sleep my soul almost departs. My fingers have been cut off. I raise a morsel of food with both my hands, and they cannot bring it to my mouth except with great effort. My uvula has fallen, and my head is hollowed, so that there is no solidity between my ears, until one of them can see the other. My brain flows from my mouth. My hair has fallen from me, and my face is as if it had been burned with fire. My eyeballs hang upon my cheeks. My tongue has swollen until it fills my mouth, so that when I put food in it, it chokes me. My lips have swollen until the upper one covers my nose and the lower one covers my chin. My intestines have been cut inside my belly, for I put food in and it comes out as it went in, and I do not feel it nor does it benefit me. The strength of my legs has gone, as if they were two water-skins filled, I cannot bear their weight. I carry my blanket with my hands and teeth, and I cannot bear its weight until someone else carries it with me. My wealth has gone, so I beg with my palm, and the one I used to support feeds me a single morsel, reminds me of it, and reproaches me. My sons and daughters have perished, and if any of them had remained he would have helped me in my affliction and benefited me. This is not the torment of this world, for it passes from its people, and they die and leave it. But blessed is the one who has rest in the abode whose people do not die, nor do they move from their dwellings. The happy is the one who is made happy there, and the wretched is the one who is wretched in it."

Bildad said: "How can your tongue utter this speech, and how can you express it? Do you say that justice is unjust, or do you say that the mighty is weak? Weep over your sin, and humble yourself before your Lord, perhaps He will have mercy upon you and pardon your sin, and perhaps, if you are innocent, He will make this a treasure for you in the Hereafter. If your heart has hardened, our words will not benefit you, and they will not reach you. Far-fetched is it that thickets grow in deserts, and far-fetched is it that papyrus grows in the wilderness. How can one who relies upon the weak hope to be protected by him, and how can one who denies the truth hope that his right will be fulfilled?"

Job said: "I know well that this is the truth. A servant cannot prevail over his Lord, nor can he dispute with Him. What speech have I with Him? If strength is to me, He is the One who raised the heaven and established it alone, He is the One who rolls it up when He wills, so it folds up for Him, He is the One who spread out the earth and made it level alone, and set firm the mountains upon it, and then He is the One who shakes it from its foundations until its lowest parts become its highest. And if speech is to me, what speech have I with Him? He created the mighty Throne by a single word, and filled with it the heavens and the earth and what is in them of creation, and it contained them, though it is in a vast expanse. He is the One who spoke to the seas, and they understood His word and obeyed His command, and did not oppose His order. He is the One who understands the fish, the birds and every creature. He is the One who speaks to the dead, and His word brings them to life, who speaks to stones, which understand His word and obey His command."

Eliphaz said: "How great is what you say, O Job! The skins would shudder at mention of what you say. You were struck by what struck you without a sin you had committed. Such sharpness, and such speech, has brought you to this station. Your sin has grown great, your petitioners have multiplied, and you have seized the people of wealth's wealth. You clothed yourself while they were naked, you ate while they were hungry, you shut your door to the weak, your food to the hungry, and your kindness to the needy. You kept this hidden and concealed it in your house, while you displayed deeds that we used to see you doing. So you thought that God would only repay you for what appeared from you, and you thought that God would not be aware of what you hid in your house. And how would He not be aware of that, when He knows what the earths conceal, what is beneath the darknesses, and the air?"

Job (ﷺ) said: "If I speak, speech will not benefit me, and if I remain silent, you will not excuse me. My scheming has befallen me, I have angered my Lord by my sin, I have made my enemies rejoice, and I have let them have my neck. You have made me a target for calamity and a mark for trial. You did not let me breathe with all this, but you followed me with affliction upon affliction. Was I not a home for the stranger, a refuge for the poor, a guardian for the orphan, and a protector for the widow? I never saw a stranger without being a home for him in place of his home, and a refuge in place of his refuge. I never saw a poor man without being wealth for him in place of his wealth, and family in place of his family. I never saw an orphan without being a father to him in place of his father, and I never saw a widow without being a guardian for her, seeking her approval of my guardianship. I am a humble servant: if I do good, I have no claim to good, for the favor belongs to my Lord and not to me. And if I do evil, my punishment is in His hand. A calamity has befallen me which, if You had let it fall upon a mountain, it would have weakened under its burden. How then can my weakness bear it?"

Eliphaz said: "Do you dispute with God, O Job, concerning His affair, or do you wish to be equitable with Him while you are a sinner, or to declare yourself innocent while you are not innocent? He created the heavens and the earth with truth, and He counted what is in them of creation. How then would He not know what you have concealed, and how would He not know what you have done, so as to recompense you for it? God placed angels in rows around His Throne and upon the edges of His heavens, then He veiled Himself with light. Their sight is dimmed before Him, their strength is weak before Him, and their mighty ones are humbled before Him. And you claim that if He disputed with you, and brought Himself forward to judge with you, [you could contend]. Have you seen Him so that you could be equitable with Him, or have you heard Him so that you could converse with Him? We have known His judgment concerning you: whoever wishes to be raised up, his station is lowered, and whoever humbles himself before Him, He raises."

Job (ﷺ) said: "If He destroys me, who is there who can confront Him concerning His servant, or question Him about His affair? Nothing turns back His wrath except His mercy, and nothing benefits His servant except supplication to Him. He said: 'My Lord, turn toward me with Your mercy, and inform me what my sin is that I have committed, or for what reason You have turned Your noble face away from me, and made me like an enemy to You, when You used to honor me. Nothing is hidden from You; You count the drops of rain, the leaves of trees, and the dust particles. My skin has become like a rotten garment. Whatever You hold me by, I am left helpless. So grant me a sacrifice from Your presence, and relief from my affliction, by the power by which You raise the dead of the servants and by which You revive the dead lands. Do not destroy me without informing me of my sin, and do not spoil the work of Your hands, though You are independent of me. Injustice does not befit Your judgment, nor haste in Your retribution. Only the weak need injustice, and only one who fears missing out hastens. Do not remind me of my errors and my sins. Remember how You created me from clay, then made me a clot, then created the clot into bones, clothed the bones with flesh and skin, and made the sinews and veins a support and strength for that. You nurtured me as a child and provided for me as an adult. Then I kept Your covenant and carried out Your command. So if I have erred, make it clear to me, and do not destroy me with grief, and inform me of my sin. If I have not pleased You, then I deserve that You punish me, and if You, among Your creation, count my deeds against me, and I seek Your forgiveness, You will not forgive me. If I do good, I cannot lift my head, and if I do evil, You do not let me swallow my saliva, nor relieve me of my stumbling. You see my weakness beneath You and my humbling before You. So why did You create me, or why did You bring me out from my mother's womb? Had I been as one who never was, it would have been better for me. The world is not of any worth to me in the face of Your anger, and my body cannot endure Your punishment. So have mercy on me, and let me taste the sweetness of well-being before I go to the narrowness of the grave, the darkness of the earth, and the grief of death."

Zophar said: "You have spoken, O Job, and no one can bind your mouth. You claim that you are innocent. Would it benefit you, if you were innocent, when there is one over you who counts your deeds? You claim that you know God forgives your sins. Do you know how far the height of the sky is? Or do you know how deep the air is? Or do you know which of the earth is widest? Or do you have a measure by which you can gauge it? Or do you know which of the sea is deepest? Or do you know with what you hold it back? If you know this knowledge, or if you do not know it, God created it and He counts it. If you would leave off excessive speech and request of your Lord, you would hope that He would have mercy on you, and by that His mercy would be drawn out. But if you persist in your sin, and raise your hands to God at the time of need while you are insistent upon your sin, like the persistence of flowing water on a slope that cannot be held back, then at the time of seeking needs from the Merciful, the faces of the wicked blacken and their eyes are darkened. At that time, those who abandoned desires in adornment before their Lord rejoice at the success of their needs. They advanced in supplication, so that by that they deserve mercy when they need it. They are the ones who endured the night, withdrew from beds, and awaited the pre-dawn hours."

Job said: "You are a people whom your own selves have made you proud. I was in times past, and men used to honor me, and I was known for my right, victorious over my adversary, and dominant over one who today dominates me. You ask me about the knowledge of God's unseen which I do not know, and you ask me. By my life, a brother did not counsel his brother this way when calamity befell him, but rather he weeps with him. And if you are serious, my intellect falls short of what you ask me about. Ask the birds of the sky whether they will inform you, and ask the beasts of the earth whether they will return to you. Ask the predators of the wilderness whether they will answer you. Ask the whales of the sea whether they will describe to you all that I have counted. You know that this was made by His wisdom and fashioned by His kindness. Does not the son of Adam know of speech what he heard with his ears, what he tasted with his mouth, and what he smelled with his nose? And the knowledge you asked about is known only by God who created it, to whom belong wisdom and majesty, greatness and gentleness, glory and power. If He corrupts, who can set right? If He makes dumb, who can make eloquent? If He looks at the seas, they dry up from His fear, and if He permits them, they swallow the earth. It is He who carries them by His power. He before whose kingship kings are stunned, before whose knowledge scholars falter, before whose wisdom the wise are confounded, and before whose authority the falsifiers are humbled. He is the one who recalls the forgotten and forgets the remembered, and who causes the darknesses and the light to flow. This is my knowledge, and His creation is greater than my intellect can count, and His majesty is greater than someone like me can measure."

Bildad said: "The hypocrite is recompensed for what he conceals of his hypocrisy. The openness with which he deceived goes astray from him, and the recompense is entrusted to the one who did it. His mention perishes from the world, his light is darkened in the Hereafter, his path becomes desolate, his inner nature ensnares him in the trap, and his name is cut off from the earth, so that there is no remembrance of him nor prosperity. No righteous descendants inherit him after him, and no origin remains by which he is known. Whoever sees him is confounded, and poetry falls silent at mention of him."

Job said: "If I have strayed, then my straying is upon me, and if I am innocent, what protection do I have? If I cry out, who will hear my cry? If I am silent, who will excuse me? My hope has gone, my dreams have ended, and my acquaintances have turned strange to me. I called my servant and he did not answer me. I humbled myself before my maidservant, and she did not have mercy on me. Calamity befell me and they abandoned me. You were harsher upon me than my misfortune. Look, and be astonished at the wonders that are in my body. Have you not heard what has befallen me, and what you have seen of me has not distracted you from me? If a servant disputed with his Lord, I would hope to prevail in judgment. But I have a mighty Lord, exalted above His heavens, who has cast me here and abased me. He has neither excused me by my excuse, nor brought me near so that I might argue on my own behalf. He hears me and I do not hear Him; He sees me and I do not see Him; He encompasses me. Were He to reveal Himself to me, my kidneys would melt and my soul would swoon. And if He were to let me breathe, so that I could speak with the full of my mouth, and He removed the awe from me, I would know for what sin He is punishing me." He was called out, and it was said: "O Job!" He said: "At Your service!" He said: "Here I am, I have drawn near to you. So rise, tighten your waistband, and stand in the station of a mighty one, for it is not fitting that one should dispute with Me except a mighty one like Me. And it is not fitting that one should dispute with Me except one who places the girdle in the mouth of the lion, the kids in the mouth of the phoenix, and the flesh in the mouth of the dragon, who measures a measure of light, weighs a weight of wind, binds a bundle of the sun, and returns yesterday to tomorrow. Your soul has deluded you into a matter that does not reach to the likes of your strength. And if, when your soul deluded you into that and invited you to it, you had remembered what aim was aimed at you, did you wish to dispute with Me through your transgression? Or did you wish to argue with Me through your error? Or did you wish to outnumber Me through your weakness? Where were you with Me on the day I created the earth and set it upon its foundation? Did you know the measure of its power? Or were you with Me passing over its edges? Or do you know how far its corners extend? Or upon what did I place its supports? Was the carrying of the earth's water by your obedience? Or by your wisdom was the earth made a covering for the water? Where were you with Me on the day I raised the sky as a roof in the air, without ties that hold it from above, nor supports that carry it from below? Does your wisdom reach to make its light flow, or to make its stars move, or to change its night and day by your command? Where were you with Me on the day I kindled the seas and caused the rivers to gush forth? Did your power hold back the waves of the seas within their boundaries? Or did your power open the wombs when their term was reached? Where are you with Me on the day I poured water upon the dust and set up the lofty mountains? Do you have an arm that can bear them? Or do you know how much they weigh? Or where is the water that was sent down from the sky? Do you know whether a mother gives birth to it, or a father begets it? Does your wisdom count the rain and divide the provisions? Or does your power stir up the clouds and cover them with water? Do you know what the sounds of thunder are? Or from what the flashes of lightning are kindled? Have you seen the depths of the seas? Or do you know how far the air extends? Or have you stored away the souls of the dead? Do you know where the treasury of snow is, or where the storehouses of hail are, or where the mountains of hail are? Or do you know where the treasury of night is with the day, and where the treasury of day is with the night? And where is the path of light? And in what language do the trees speak? And where is the treasury of the wind, and how do locks hold it? And who placed the intellects in the bodies of men? And who split the hearing and the sight? And who made the angels submissive to His kingship, and subdued the tyrants by His might, and divided the provisions of the animals by His wisdom? And who apportioned for the lion its provision and made the bird know its livelihood, and inclined it toward its young? Who freed the wild beasts from servitude, and made their dwellings in the wilderness not familiar with voices, nor fearful of the dominant ones? Is it from your wisdom that the young of birds and the offspring of animals follow their mothers? Or is it from your wisdom that their mothers incline toward them, until they bring out food for them from their bellies, and prefer them with life over their own souls? Or is it from your wisdom that the eagle sees, so that it comes to the places of the slain? Where were you with Me on the day I created Behemoth in its place in the uttermost dust, and the two Tanninim [In the Bible, p. 381: "Leviathan".] who carry the mountains, the villages, and the habitations? Their ears are like tall pine trees at their heads, their heads are like hills of ropes, the veins of their thighs are like iron pegs, their skins are like splits of rock, and their bones are like pillars of copper. They are the two heads of my creation, which I created for war. Did you fill their skins with flesh? Or did you fill their heads with brains? Do you have a share in their creation? Or do you have a pair of hands with which you made them? Or does your strength reach so far that you could put a ring in their noses, or put your hand upon their heads, or sit for them on a road and hold them back, or turn them away from their strength? Where were you on the day I created the dragon, and provided for it in the sea, and made its dwelling in the clouds? Its eyes blaze with fire, its nostrils billow smoke, its ears are like the rainbow, from which a flame erupts like a whirlwind of dust. Its belly burns and its breath ignites. Its foam is like rocks, and the grinding of its teeth is like the sound of thunderbolts, and the look of its eyes is like the flash of lightning. Its secrets are not entered by worries. Armies pass by it while it reclines, nothing frightens it, and it has no joint. Iron in its presence is like figs, and copper in its presence is like threads. It does not fear arrows, and does not feel the impact of rocks upon its body, and it laughs at the meteors, and moves through the air like a sparrow, and destroys everything that passes by it, the king of beasts. And it is He whom I preferred with strength over my creation. Will you take it with your trap, and tie it by its tongue, or put a bridle in its jaw? Do you think it will fulfill your covenant, or glorify out of your fear? Can you count its lifespan, or do you know its term, or cause its provision to pass? Or do you know what has been ruined of the earth? Or what it ruins of what remains of its life? Can you bear its anger when it becomes angry, or will you command it and it obeys you? Blessed is God, exalted!"

Job (ﷺ) said: "I have fallen short of this matter that you have presented to me. Would that the earth had split open for me, so that I might have gone into my affliction without speaking anything that angers my Lord. Affliction has gathered upon me. My God, You have carried me as an enemy to You, although You used to honor me and know my sincerity. I know that what you have mentioned is the work of Your hands and the arrangement of Your wisdom, and greater than this is whatever You wish to do. Nothing can outdo You, and no hidden thing is concealed from You, and nothing unseen is absent from You. Who is it that thinks he can conceal a secret from You, when You know what occurs to hearts? I have come to know from You, in this affliction of mine, what I did not know, and when Your command was tested, I feared more than I used to fear. I used to hear of Your might only by hearing, but now it is by the sight of the eye. I spoke when I spoke only so that You would excuse me, and I was silent when I was silent only so that You would have mercy on me. It was a word that slipped, and I will not return to it. I have placed my hands upon my mouth, bit down on my tongue, pressed my cheek to the dust, and lowered my face to my children. I have kept silent as my sin silenced me. So forgive me what I said, for I will not return to anything You dislike from me."

God, blessed and exalted, said: "O Job, My knowledge has been executed upon you, and by My forbearance I have turned away My wrath from you. Since you erred, I have forgiven you, and I have returned to you your family, your wealth, and the like of them with them. So bathe with this water, for in it is your cure. Offer a sacrifice on behalf of your companions, and seek forgiveness for them, for they have disobeyed Me concerning you."

⁕ Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Salamah related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ishaq related to me, from someone whose reliability is not in doubt, from Wahb ibn Munabbih al-Yamani and others from the People of the Earlier Scriptures, that the account concerning Ayyub was that he was a man from the Romans. Allah had chosen him, made him a prophet, and tested him with wealth, through abundant children and property, and worldly provision was extended to him generously. He had an estate in al-Bathaniyyah in the land of al-Sham, its upper and lower parts, its plains and its mountains. In it he had every kind of property: camels, cattle, sheep, horses and donkeys, in a number and abundance that no other man could surpass. Allah had given him a household and children, men and women. He was righteous, pious and merciful to the needy: he fed the poor, supported widows, cared for orphans, honoured guests and provided for the wayfarer. He was grateful for Allah's blessings upon him and fulfilled Allah's right in wealth. He was protected from the enemy of Allah, Iblis, from achieving against him what he achieved against the wealthy through pride, heedlessness, forgetfulness and being preoccupied with the world away from the command of Allah. With him were three men who had believed in him and affirmed him, and who recognised the excellence of what Allah had given him over others: a man from Yemen called Alifaz, and two men from his country, one called Sufar and the other Bildad. They were middle-aged men from his land.

Iblis, the enemy of Allah, had a dwelling in the seventh heaven, to which he would descend each year at a set time to make his petition. On the day he ascended, Allah said to him, or it was said to him on behalf of Allah: "Have you gained any power over My servant Ayyub?" He said: "My Lord, how could I gain power over him? Did You not test him with ease, blessing, plenty and health, and give him family, property, children, wealth and health in his body, household and wealth? Why would he not thank You, worship You and obey You, when You have done that for him? If You tested him by taking away what You gave him, he would certainly change from the gratitude he had for You, abandon Your worship, and go out from Your obedience to something else." Or as the enemy of Allah said. Allah said: "I have given you power over his family and his property." Allah knew him best, and He gave him power over him only as a mercy, to magnify his reward through the affliction that befell him, to make him a lesson for the patient and a reminder for the worshippers in every affliction that befalls them, so that they might take him as an example, and hope for the reward of the Hereafter in exchange for patience in the passing matters of this world, and for what Allah did with Ayyub.

The enemy of Allah quickly withdrew. He gathered the mighty jinn and rebellious devils from among his hosts and said: "I have been given power over the family and property of Ayyub. What do you say?" One of them said: "I will become a whirlwind of fire, and I will not pass by anything of his property without destroying it." He said: "You may do as you wish." So he went off until he reached his camels, and burned them and their herdsmen all together. Then the enemy of Allah came to Ayyub in the form of his overseer over them, while Ayyub was in his place of prayer, and said: "O Ayyub, a fire came and overtook your camels, and burned them and everyone with them except me. I have come to inform you of that." Ayyub recognised him and said: "Praise be to Allah, who gave them and who took them. He who took you out of them is the one who removes the chaff from the pure grain." Then he left him. Ayyub's property was lost piece by piece until it was all gone. Each time news came to him of the destruction of some of his property, he praised Allah, spoke highly of Him, was content with the decree and prepared himself to bear the affliction with patience. When no property remained to him, he went to his family and children, who were in a palace of theirs with their concubines and servants. Iblis took the form of a violent wind, lifted the palace from its sides and dropped it upon his family and children, crushing them beneath it. Then he came to Ayyub in the form of their steward, with his face crushed, and said: "O Ayyub, a violent wind came and lifted the palace from its sides, and dropped it upon your family and children, and crushed them, except me. I have come to inform you of that." Ayyub did not grieve over anything that befell him as he grieved over his family and children. He took dust, placed it on his head and said: "Would that my mother had not borne me, and that I had been nothing." The enemy of Allah was pleased by this, so he ascended to the heavens rejoicing. Ayyub then returned to repentance for what he had said and praised Allah. His repentance reached Allah before the enemy of Allah did. When Iblis came and mentioned what he had done, it was said to him: "His repentance and return have preceded you to Allah." He said: "My Lord, give me power over his body." He said: "I have given you power over his body, but not over his tongue, his heart, his soul, his hearing or his sight." So the enemy of Allah came to him while he was prostrating, and blew upon his body a blast that set alight everything from his horn to his foot, like the burning of fire. Then pustules came out on his body like the tails of sheep. He scratched them with his nails until they were gone, then with potsherds and stones until his flesh fell away. Nothing remained of him but the veins, the sinews and the bones. His eyes moved in his head to look, and his heart remained for understanding. Nothing reached the inner contents of his belly, for life cannot remain without them. He ate and drank with difficulty from his inner parts. He remained in that state for as long as Allah willed.

Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Salamah related to us from Ibn Ishaq, from Ibn Dinar, from al-Hasan, that he used to say: Ayyub remained in that affliction for seven years and six months, lying on the ashes of a sweeping-pile at the edge of the town. Wahb ibn Munabbih said: None of his family remained except one woman who looked after him and earned for him. The enemy of Allah could not gain power over him in anything, small or great, that he wished. When the affliction lasted long upon him and upon her, and people grew weary of them, and she was earning to provide him with food and drink, Wahb ibn Munabbih said: I was told that she sought food for him one day, but she found nothing until she cut off a lock of her hair and sold it for a loaf of bread. She brought it to him and fed him. He remained in that affliction for those years, to the point that a passer-by would pass and say: "If this man had any good with Allah, He would relieve him of what he is in."

⁕ Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Salamah related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ishaq related to me, saying: Wahb ibn Munabbih used to say: He remained in that affliction for three years, not a single day more. When Ayyub had overcome him and he could gain no power over him, he confronted his wife in a form not like the form of the sons of Adam in size, body or height, mounted on a mount that was not one of the mounts of men, possessing a grandeur, splendour and beauty that she did not have. He said to her: "Are you the wife of this afflicted man, Ayyub?" She said: "Yes." He said: "Do you know me?" She said: "No." He said: "I am the god of the earth, and I am the one who did to your companion what he did. He worshipped the God of the heavens and left me, so he angered me. If he had prostrated to me one single prostration, I would have restored to him and to you all the property and children you had, for it is with me." Then he showed her them, as she was seeing them, in the bottom of the valley where she had met him. He said: "I have heard that he only said: 'If your companion had eaten food without saying the name of Allah over it, he would have been healed from what he has of affliction.' And Allah knows best." The enemy of Allah wished to approach him through her. She returned to Ayyub and informed him of what he had said to her and what he had shown her. He said: "Has the enemy of Allah come to you so as to tempt you away from your religion?" Then he swore that if Allah healed him, he would strike her one hundred blows.

When the affliction lengthened upon him, those men who had been with him, who had believed in him and affirmed him, came to him, along with a young man, young in years, who had also believed in him and affirmed him. They sat with Ayyub and looked upon the affliction that he had, and they were greatly alarmed by it and were appalled at it. Ayyub, may the blessings of Allah be upon him, had reached the limit of his endurance, and that was when Allah wished to relieve him of what he had. When Ayyub saw how greatly they were alarmed by what had befallen him, he said: "My Lord, for what reason did You create me? Would that, when You decreed affliction for me, You had left me and not created me. Would that I had been blood that my mother cast out." Then he mentioned something similar to the report of Ibn Askar, from Isma'il ibn Abd al-Karim, up to: "They were wakeful at night, withdrew from their beds and waited for the dawns." He then added: "They are the secure ones who do not fear, nor are they anxious or grieved. So where is the outcome of your affair, O Ayyub, compared with their outcomes?"

A young man who had been present and had heard their words, and whom they had not noticed or paid attention to in his seat, spoke. Allah had sent him to them because of their excess in speech and their transgression. Allah wished to make them feel small through him and to show the foolishness of their judgement through his youth. When he spoke he continued speaking, and he increased only in wisdom. The people were accustomed to listening attentively and being humble when they were admonished or reminded. He said: "You, O elders, have spoken before me. You were more deserving of speech and more entitled to it than I, because of your age, because you have experienced more than I, because you have seen and known what I have not known and have recognised what I have not recognised. Yet you have left out of speech what is better than what you said, of opinion what is more correct than what you held, of conduct what is more beautiful than what you did, and of admonition what is wiser than what you described. Ayyub had a right and a claim upon you that is greater than what you have described. Do you know, O elders, the right of the one you have belittled, and the sanctity of the one you have violated, and the man you have blamed and accused? Did you not know, O elders, that Ayyub is the prophet of Allah, His chosen one and His elect from the people of the earth? On this day of yours, Allah chose him for His revelation, selected him for Himself and entrusted him with His prophethood. Then you did not know, and Allah did not inform you, that He had been displeased with any part of his affair since what befell him up to this day of yours; nor that He had taken from him any of the honour with which He had honoured him since what befell him up to this day of yours; nor that Ayyub had altered the truth during the long time you have accompanied him up to this day of yours. If it is the affliction that has diminished him in your estimation and lowered him in your minds, then you know that Allah tests the prophets, the truthful ones, the martyrs and the righteous. His affliction for them is not a proof of His displeasure with them, nor of His humiliation of them, but it is an honour and a choice for them. Even if Ayyub were not of such standing with Allah, nor in prophethood, nor in distinction, nor in excellence, nor in honour, but were merely a brother whom you loved in the manner of companionship, it would still not be fitting for a wise man to reproach his brother in the time of affliction, nor to rebuke him for a calamity without knowing, while he is distressed and grieved. Rather he should have mercy on him and weep with him, pray for his forgiveness, grieve at his grief and guide him to the right course of his affair. A man who is ignorant of this is neither wise nor rightly guided. So, Allah, Allah, O elders, regarding yourselves."

He said: Then he turned to Ayyub, peace be upon him, and said: "In the greatness and majesty of Allah, and in the mention of death, there is what cuts off the tongue, breaks the heart and makes one forget one's proofs. Do you not know, O Ayyub, that Allah has servants whom the fear of Him has silenced, not from incapacity nor from dumbness? They are the eloquent, the articulate, the noble, the wise, those who know Allah and His signs. But when they remember the greatness of Allah, their tongues are cut off, their skins shiver, their hearts are broken and their minds are overwhelmed, out of magnifying Allah, honouring Him and exalting Him. When they recover from that, they hasten to Allah with pure deeds. They count themselves among the wrongdoers and sinners, though they are in truth pure and innocent, and among the negligent and the neglectful, though they are in truth clever and strong. Yet they do not regard their great deeds as much for Allah, nor are they satisfied with little for Allah, and they do not boast of their deeds before Him. They are alarmed, terrified, anxious, humble, fearful, submissive and confessing. Wherever you see them, O Ayyub."

Ayyub said: "Allah sows wisdom through mercy in the heart of the young and the old. When it takes root in the heart, Allah makes it manifest on the tongue. Wisdom does not come from age, nor from youth, nor from long experience. When Allah makes a servant wise in his fasting, his standing among the wise is not diminished, and they see upon him the light of honour from Allah. But you have been pleased with yourselves, and you have thought that you were made well because of your good deeds. Then you were insolent and you exalted yourselves. If you had looked at what lies between you and your Lord, and then been truthful with yourselves, you would have found in yourselves faults which Allah has covered with the well-being with which He clothed you. But today I have become one with no opinion and no speech among you. In the past my words were heeded, my right was recognised, I obtained justice from my opponent, I subdued those who now subdue me, my position was revered, and men listened to me and honoured me. Today, however, my hope has been cut off and my caution lifted. My family has grown weary of me, my kin have disowned me, my acquaintances have turned strange to me, my friend has turned away from me, my companions have cut me off, my household has disbelieved in me, my rights have been denied, and my favours have been forgotten. I cry out and they do not answer me; I offer my excuse and they do not accept it. His decree has humiliated me, disgraced me and abased me, and His authority has made me sick and wasted my body. If my Lord were to remove the awe that is in my breast and loosen my tongue so that I could speak with my full mouth, and if a servant were then to argue on his own behalf, I would hope that He would heal me of what I have. But He has cast me aside and withdrawn Himself from me. He sees me but I do not see Him, He hears me but I do not hear Him. He has neither looked upon me in mercy nor drawn near to me nor brought me near. So I present my excuse, speak of my innocence and argue on my own behalf."

When Ayyub and his companions said this in his presence, a cloud overshadowed him, so that his companions thought it was a punishment. Then a voice called out from it, and it was said to him: "O Ayyub, Allah says: 'Here I am, I have drawn near to you, and I have never been far from you. So rise, present the excuse you claim, speak of your innocence, argue on your own behalf, and gird up your loins.'" Then he mentioned something similar to the report of Ibn Askar, from Isma'il, up to its end, and he added in it: "My mercy has preceded My anger. Strike your foot; this is a cool place to wash and a drink in which is your healing. I have given you back your family and their like with them, and your property and its like with it." And they claimed: "and its like with it, so that they may be a sign for those who come after you, and a lesson for the people of affliction, and a consolation for the patient." He struck his foot, and a spring gushed forth for him. He entered it and washed, and Allah removed from him everything that had been upon him of affliction. Then he came out and sat down. His wife came seeking him in his resting place, but she did not find him. She stood up like one bewildered, distracted, and said: "O servant of Allah, do you have any knowledge of the afflicted man who was here?" He said: "No." Then he smiled, and she recognised him by his smile, and she embraced him.

⁕ Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Salamah related to us, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from some people of knowledge, from Wahb ibn Munabbih, who said: I related to Abd Allah ibn Abbas his account and her embracing him. Abd Allah said: "By Him in whose hand is the soul of Abd Allah, I did not separate from her embrace until every property and child they had came back to them."

⁕ Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Salamah related to us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: I have heard some of those who relate this report say that when she asked about him, he called her and said to her: "Would you recognise him if you saw him?" She said: "Yes, and why would I not recognise him?" He smiled and then said: "Here I am, he," and Allah had relieved me of what I was in. At that she embraced him. Wahb said: Allah then revealed concerning his oath, that he should strike her with the one with whom he had spoken: ﴿And take in your hand a bunch of grass and strike with it, and do not break your oath﴾, meaning: your oath has been fulfilled. Allah says: ﴿Indeed, We found him patient; an excellent servant. Indeed, he was one who often turned back in repentance﴾. Allah says: ﴿And We gave him his family and the like of them with them, as a mercy from Us and a reminder to people of understanding﴾.

⁕ Yahya ibn Talhah al-Yarbu'i related to us, saying: Fudayl ibn Iyad related to us, from Hisham, from al-Hasan, who said: Ayyub remained lying on a dunghill for seven years and some months, not asking Allah to remove what was upon him. He said: There is no creature on the face of the earth more honoured by Allah than Ayyub. They claim that some of the people said: "If the Lord of this man had any need of him, He would not have done this to him." At that he prayed.

⁕ Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim related to me, saying: Ibn Ulayyah related to us, from Yunus, from al-Hasan, who said: Ayyub remained on a dunghill belonging to the Children of Israel for seven years and some months, while animals moved about him.

⁕ Muhammad ibn Ishaq related to me, saying: Yahya ibn Ma'in related to us, saying: Ibn Uyaynah related to us, from Amr, from Wahb ibn Munabbih, who said: Ayyub did not have an ulcer; rather, there would emerge from him something like women's breasts, which he would then squeeze.

⁕ Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Makhlad ibn Husayn narrated to us, from Hisham, from al-Hasan, and Hajjaj, from Mubarak, from al-Hasan, and one of them added to the other, saying: Ayyub (Job), peace be upon him, was given wealth by God and was granted abundance. He had wives, cattle, sheep, and camels. The enemy of God, Iblis, was asked: "Can you tempt Ayyub?" He said: "My Lord, Ayyub is in a world of wealth and children, and he cannot help but thank You. But give me power over his wealth and children, and You will see how he obeys me and disobeys You!" He said: So God gave him power over his wealth and children. He said: Iblis would bring the livestock from Ayyub's wealth, the sheep, and burn them with fire. Then he would come to Ayyub while he was praying, disguised as a shepherd, and say: "O Ayyub, you pray to your Lord, but God has left you no livestock of sheep except that I have burned them with fire. I was away, and I came to inform you." Ayyub would say: "O God, You gave, and You took. Whatever You leave me, I will praise You for Your good trial." So Iblis could not achieve anything he wanted. Then he would come to Ayyub's cattle and burn them with fire, then come to Ayyub and tell him that, and Ayyub would reply in the same way. He said: He did the same with the camels, until he left him no livestock at all. Then he demolished the house upon his children, and came saying: "O Ayyub, God sent upon your children those who demolished the houses over them until they perished." Ayyub would say the same as before. He said: "My Lord, this is when You have done me all kindness. Previously, love of wealth occupied me by day, and love of children occupied me by night out of compassion for them. Now I empty my hearing, my sight, my night and my day for remembrance and praise, sanctification and proclamation of God's oneness (tahlil)." Thus the enemy of God departed from him, having gained nothing of what he wanted.

He said: Then God, blessed and exalted, said: "How did you find Ayyub?" Iblis said: "Ayyub knows that You will return to him his wealth and children, but give me power over his body. If harm reaches him in it, he will obey me and disobey You." He said: So power over his body was given to him. He came to him and blew upon him a blow that caused sores from his crown to his foot. He said: Affliction came upon him after affliction, until he was carried and placed on a refuse heap (kunasah) of the Children of Israel. No wealth, child, or friend remained to him, and no one approached him except his wife. She remained with him in sincerity, bringing him food, and praising God with him when he praised. Ayyub, for his part, did not cease from remembrance of God, from glorifying and praising God, and from patience over what God had tested him with.

al-Hasan said: Then the enemy of God, Iblis, let out a cry by which he gathered his armies from the ends of the earth, out of distress at Ayyub's patience. They gathered to him and said: "You have summoned us. What is your news? What has overcome you?" He said: "This servant has overcome me, the one about whom I asked my Lord to give me power over his wealth and children, and I left him neither wealth nor child. Yet he only increased in patience, praise of God, and glorification of Him. Then I was given power over his body, and I left him as a sore lying on the refuse heap of the Children of Israel, approached by no one except his wife. I have been exposed before my Lord, so I seek your help. Help me against him." They said to him: "Where is your cunning? Where is your knowledge with which you destroyed those who passed before?" He said: "All of that has come to nothing with Ayyub. So advise me." They said: "We will advise you. Do you recall Adam, when you expelled him from Paradise? From where did you approach him?" He said: "From the side of his wife." They said: "Then deal with Ayyub through his wife, for he cannot disobey her, and no one approaches him except her." He said: "You are right." So he set off until he came to his wife, while she was selling (charity, tasaddaq), and he appeared to her in the form of a man and said: "Where is your husband, O servant of God?" She said: "He is over there, scratching his sores, and the worms are crawling over his body." When he heard her, he hoped that a word of despair would come from her, so he entered her heart and whispered to her. He reminded her of the blessings, wealth, and livestock they had been in, and reminded her of Ayyub's beauty and youth, and of the harm he was now in, and that this would never end for them. al-Hasan said: She cried out. When she cried out, he knew that she had cried out and become distressed. He brought her a young goat and said: "Let Ayyub slaughter this for me, and he will be healed." She came crying out: "O Ayyub! O Ayyub! How long will your Lord torment you? Will He not have mercy on you? Where is the livestock? Where is the wealth? Where are the children? Where is the friend? Where is your handsome complexion? It has changed and become like ashes! Where is your beautiful body that has decayed and in which the worms crawl? Slaughter this young goat and find rest." Ayyub said: "The enemy of God came to you, blew upon you, found in you some softness, and you responded to him! Woe to you! Do you see what you weep over, what you mention of what we had of wealth, children, health, and youth? Who gave them to us?" She said: "God." He said: "How long did He let us enjoy them?" She said: "Eighty years." He said: "Since when has God tested us with this affliction with which He has tested us?" She said: "Seven years and some months." He said: "Woe to you! By God, you have not been just, nor have you been fair to your Lord! Would you not endure, until we are in this affliction with which our Lord has tested us for eighty years, as we were in ease for eighty years? By God, if God heals me, I will flog you one hundred lashes. Indeed, you ordered me to slaughter for other than God. The food and drink you bring me is forbidden to me, and I will not taste what you bring me afterward. Since you have said this to me, get away from me, and I will not see you." He drove her away, and she went off. Then Satan said: "This man has steeled himself for eighty years against this affliction in which he is, and he has been defeated and has rejected it." Ayyub looked at his wife, after he had driven her away, and he had no food, no drink, and no friend.

al-Hasan said: Two men passed by him while he was in that state. By God, on the earth at that time there was no one more honored by God than Ayyub. One of the two men said to his companion: "If God had any need for this man, He would not have brought him to this." Ayyub heard nothing harder for him than this statement.

⁕ Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Jarir ibn Hazim, from Abd Allah ibn Ubayd ibn Umayr, who said: Ayyub had two brothers. They came to him and stood at a distance, unable to draw near him because of his smell. One of them said to the other: "If God had known any good in Ayyub, He would not have afflicted him with what we see." He said: Ayyub had never been distressed by anything that befell him as he was distressed by the statement of the man. Ayyub said: "O God, if You know that I never spent a night satisfied while I knew of a hungry person nearby, then confirm it for me." It was confirmed, while they were listening. Then he said: "O God, if You know that I never took two garments while I knew of a naked person nearby, then confirm it for me." It was confirmed, while they were listening. He said: Then he fell down in prostration.

⁕ Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Makhlad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, from Hisham, from al-Hasan, who said: He said: ﴿My Lord, harm has touched me, and You are the Most Merciful of the merciful﴾ [Qur'an 21:83]. Then he referred that to his Lord, saying: ﴿And You are the Most Merciful of the merciful﴾ [Qur'an 21:83].

⁕ Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Jarir, from Abd Allah ibn Ubayd ibn Umayr, who said: It was said to him: "Raise your head, for your supplication has been answered."

⁕ Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Mubarak, from al-Hasan and Makhlad, from Hisham, from al-Hasan, the narration of one of them entering into the other, they said: It was said to him: ﴿Strike with your foot; this is a cool place to wash and a drink﴾ [Qur'an 38:42]. He struck with his foot, and a spring gushed forth, and he washed in it, and no outward ailment remained upon him except that it fell away. God removed every pain and every sickness, and his youth and beauty returned to him, better and more excellent than they had been. Then he struck with his foot again, and another spring gushed forth, and he drank from it, and no disease remained in his inside except that it came out. He stood up healthy, and he was clothed in a robe of honor. He said: He began to look around and saw nothing that had belonged to him of family and wealth except that God had multiplied it for him. By God, it was related to us that the water with which he had washed scattered upon his chest as golden locusts. He began to gather it with his hand. God revealed to him: "O Ayyub, did I not make you rich?" He said: "Yes, but it is Your blessing. Who can have enough of it?" He said: Then he went out and sat down in an elevated place. Then his wife said: "What do you think? If he had driven me away, to whom would I have gone? Shall I leave him to die of hunger, or be lost, and the beasts devour him? I will certainly return to him." So she returned, and she saw no refuse heap, nor anything of the state she had been in. Things had changed. She began to circle the place where the refuse heap had been, weeping. That was in front of Ayyub's eyes. She said: She was too awed by the man in the robe to go to him and ask about him. So Ayyub sent for her and called her. He said: "What do you want, O servant of God?" She wept and said: "I want that afflicted one who was thrown on the refuse heap. I do not know whether he was lost or what became of him." Ayyub said to her: "What was your situation?" She wept and said: "My husband. Have you seen him? He was here, weeping." He said: "Would you recognize him if you saw him?" She said: "Would anyone who saw him be hidden from him?" Then she began looking at him while she was in awe of him. Then she said: "Indeed, he was the most similar of God's creatures to you when he was healthy." He said: "I am Ayyub, whom you ordered to slaughter for Satan. I obeyed God and disobeyed Satan. I called upon God, and He returned to me what you see." al-Hasan said: Then God, out of mercy to her for her patience with him in the trial, commanded him, to lighten her burden, to take a bundle of branches and strike her with it in one blow, as a relief to her for her patience with him.

⁕ Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words ﴿And Ayyub, when he called to his Lord: "Harm has touched me"﴾ [Qur'an 21:83], to the end of the two verses. When Satan touched him with fatigue and torment, God made him forget to supplicate Him to remove the harm he had. Yet he continued to remember God much, and his affliction only increased him in desire for God and in good faith. When the term came to its end, and God decreed that He would remove the harm he had, He permitted him to supplicate and made it easy for him. Before that, God, blessed and exalted, had said: "It is not fitting for My servant Ayyub to call upon Me and then for Me not to respond to him." When he supplicated, God responded to him, and gave him in exchange for everything he had lost double. He returned to him his family and their like with them, and praised him, saying: ﴿Indeed, We found him patient; an excellent servant; indeed, he was one who turned back in repentance﴾ [Qur'an 38:44].

The people of ta'wil (interpretation of Qur'anic meaning) differed concerning the family mentioned in His words ﴿And We gave him his family and their like with them﴾ [Qur'an 21:84]: were they his family whom he was given in this world, or is that a promise God made to Ayyub that He would do for him in the Hereafter? Some of them said: God only gave Ayyub in this world the like of his family who had perished, for they were not returned to him in this world. God promised Ayyub that He would give them to him in the Hereafter.

⁕ Abu al-Sa'ib Salm ibn Janada narrated to me, saying: Ibn Idris narrated to us, from Layth, who said: Mujahid sent a man called Qasim to Ikrimah to ask him about God's words to Ayyub: ﴿And We gave him his family and their like with them﴾ [Qur'an 21:84]. He said: It was said to him: "Your family is for you in the Hereafter. If you wish, We will hasten them to you in this world, and if you wish, they will be yours in the Hereafter, and We will give you their like in this world." He said: "They will be mine in the Hereafter, and I will be given their like in this world." He said: So he returned to Mujahid and said: "He was right."

Others said: Rather, He returned them to him in their very persons and gave him their like with them.

Mention of those who said that:

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Hakkam ibn Salm narrated to us, from Abu Sinan, from Thabit, from al-Dahhak, from Ibn Mas'ud, regarding ﴿And We gave him his family and their like with them﴾ [Qur'an 21:84]: He said: "His family in their very persons."

⁕ Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas: When Ayyub supplicated, God responded to him and gave him in exchange for everything he had lost double. He returned to him his family and their like with them.

⁕ Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿And We bestowed upon him his family and their like with them﴾ [Qur'an 21:84]: He said: "He gave them life in their very persons, and returned to him their like." [[This is suitable for citing as evidence that they were not returned in their very persons. So perhaps it has been placed later than it should be.]]

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Layth, from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿We bestowed upon him his family and their like with them﴾: He said: It was said to him: "If you wish, We will bring them back to life for you; and if you wish, they will be yours in the Hereafter and you will be given their like in this world." So he chose that they be in the Hereafter, and their like in this world.

⁕ Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿And We gave him his family and their like with them﴾: al-Hasan and Qatadah said: God gave life to his family in their very persons, and added to them their like.

Others said: Rather, He gave him the like from the offspring of his wealth which He returned to him, and his family; as for the family and wealth, He returned both to him.

Mention of those who said that: Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from a man, from al-Hasan, regarding ﴿and their like with them﴾: He said: "From their offspring."

* *

As for His words ﴿as a mercy﴾ [Qur'an 21:84], it is in the accusative as meaning: We did that to them as a mercy from Us toward him.

* *

As for His words ﴿and a reminder for the worshippers﴾ [Qur'an 21:84], it means: and a reminder for the worshippers of their Lord. We did that to him so that they might take heed from it and know that God may test His friends and whomever of His servants He loves in this world with various kinds of affliction in their self, family, and wealth, not out of contempt for them, but as a test from Him to bring them, through their patience with it, their seeking reward from it, and their good certainty, to the rank that He has prepared for them, blessed and exalted be He, of honor in His presence.

And: al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Abu Ma'shar, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, regarding His words ﴿as a mercy from Us and a reminder for the worshippers﴾ and His words ﴿as a mercy from Us and a reminder for those of understanding﴾: He said: "Whenever a believer is afflicted with an affliction and mentions what afflicted Ayyub, let him say: 'One better than us has been afflicted, a prophet among the prophets.'"

**Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 21, verses 83–84 (part 1 of 4):**

On the interpretation of His words, ﴿And Job, when he called out to his Lord, "Indeed, adversity has touched me, and You are the Most Merciful of the merciful." So We responded to him and removed what afflicted him of adversity, and We gave him his family and the like of them with them, as a mercy from Us and a reminder for the worshippers.﴾

His saying, may His remembrance be exalted, to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): "And mention Job, O Muhammad, when he called out to his Lord while adversity and affliction had touched him. ﴿My Lord, indeed adversity has touched me, and You are the Most Merciful of the merciful. So We responded to him.﴾" That is, may His remembrance be exalted: We responded to Job's supplication when he called out to Us, so We removed from him the harm, affliction and hardship that he had. The harm that befell him and the affliction that descended upon him were a trial and a test from Allah for him.

The cause of that was, as related:

Muhammad ibn Sahl ibn Askar al-Bukhari narrated to me, saying: Isma'il ibn Abd al-Karim ibn Hisham narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Samad ibn Ma'qil narrated to me [[Abd al-Samad ibn Ma'qil, with a kasra on the qaf, al-Yamani; he narrates from his paternal uncle Wahb ibn Munabbih, and from him his nephew Isma'il ibn Abd al-Karim. Ahmad declared him trustworthy. He died in the year 183 AH. (From al-Khulasa.) This narration is among the reports of the People of the Book, narrated by Wahb, Ka'b and others from the People of the Book, as al-Tha'labi said in ʿAra'is al-Majalis (pp. 153–163), edition of the Sharikat Maktabah wa Matba'ah Mustafa al-Babi al-Halabi wa Awladihi in Cairo. Its origin is in the Bible, the Book of Job (chapters 7–8, verses 93–833).]], who said: I heard Wahb ibn Munabbih say: The beginning of the matter of Job, the truthful (al-Siddiq, the one who is sincerely truthful), may Allah's blessings be upon him, was that he was patient, an excellent servant.

Wahb said: Gabriel has a station before Allah that none of the angels has in nearness to Allah and in merit before Him, and Gabriel is the one who receives the speech. When Allah mentions a servant with good, Gabriel receives it from Him, then Michael receives it, and around them are the angels brought near, encircling the Throne. That spreads among the angels brought near, and the blessing upon that servant becomes the prayer of the inhabitants of the heavens. When the angels of the heavens bless him, they descend with the blessing to the angels of the earth. Iblis was not barred from anything in the heavens; he would stand in them wherever he wished. From there he reached Adam when He expelled him from Paradise. He continued like that, ascending through the heavens, until Allah raised Jesus, son of Mary. Then he was barred from four, and he used to ascend through three. When Allah sent Muhammad (ﷺ), he was barred from the remaining three, so he and all his armies are barred from all the heavens until the Day of Resurrection. ﴿Except one who steals a hearing, and he is pursued by a clear flaming fire.﴾ That is why the jinn denied what they had known when they said: ﴿And that we had touched the heaven and found it filled with severe guards and burning flames … ﴾ up to His saying ﴿a watching flame.﴾

Wahb said: Iblis was not alarmed except by the responses of the angels of the heavens blessing Job, and that was when Allah mentioned him and praised him. When Iblis heard the prayer of the angels, envy and resentment seized him. He rose swiftly until he stood before Allah in the place where he used to stand, and said: "O my God, I considered Your servant Job, and I found him a servant upon whom You bestowed blessings and he thanked You, and You granted him health and he praised You. Then You did not test him with hardship, nor did You try him with affliction. I guarantee to You that if You strike him with affliction, he will disbelieve in You, he will forget You, and he will worship other than You." Allah, blessed and exalted, said to him: "Go, for I have given you power over his wealth, since that is the matter for which you claim he will thank Me. You have no authority over his body, nor over his mind."

The enemy of Allah swooped down until he fell to the earth. Then he gathered the demonic devils and their chiefs. Job had al-Bashaniyyah in all of Syria, with everything in it from east to west, and he had there a thousand sheep with their shepherds, and five hundred ploughs following them, with five hundred servants, each servant having a wife, a child and wealth, and each plough carrying the equipment of a she-ass, and every she-ass having offspring of two, three, four, five, and more.

When Iblis gathered the devils, he said to them: "What power and knowledge do you have? I have been given power over the wealth of Job, and it is a grievous calamity and a trial which men cannot bear patiently." One demon from the devils said: "I have been given such power that, if I wish, I can transform myself into a whirlwind of fire, and I burn everything I come upon." Iblis said to him: "Go to the camels and their herdsmen." So he set out aiming for the camels, at the time when they had lowered their heads and settled in their pastures. People had not noticed until a fire-whirlwind erupted from beneath the earth, from which blew the winds of poison. No one drew near it without being burned. It continued burning them and their herdsmen until it had consumed the last of them. When he had finished with them, Iblis took the form of one of the camels with its herdsman, then set out aiming for Job, until he found him standing in prayer. He said: "O Job." He said: "Here I am." He said: "Do you know what your Lord has done? He has done it with your camels and their herdsmen, the One whom you chose, worshipped and affirmed as one." Job said: "It is His wealth, which He lent to me, and He has more right to it; when He wills He takes it back. I have long settled my soul and my wealth for perishing." Iblis said: "Your Lord has sent a fire upon them from the sky, and they and their herdsmen have burned, until it consumed the last thing of theirs and of their herdsmen." Then the people were left bewildered, standing over them and wondering. Some of them said: "Job did not worship anything, and he was only in delusion." Others said: "If the God of Job could prevent any of that, He would have protected His friend." Others said: "Rather, He did what He did to make his enemy gloat and to grieve his friend."
