Mention of the narration on this from them: Muhammad ibn Bashshar related to us, he said: Mu'ammal related to us, he said: Sufyan related to us, from al-A'mash, from al-Minhal ibn 'Amr, from 'Abd Allah ibn al-Harith: that a prophet among the prophets said: "Whoever will guarantee to me that he will fast by day, stand in prayer by night, and not become angry?" A young man stood and said: "I will." He said: "Sit down." Then he returned and said: "Who will guarantee to me that he will stand in prayer by night and fast by day, and not become angry?" That young man stood and said: "I will." He said: "Sit down." Then he returned and said: "Who will guarantee to me that he will stand in prayer by night, fast by day, and not become angry?" That young man stood and said: "I will." He said: "You will stand in prayer by night, fast by day, and not become angry." Then that prophet died, and that young man sat in his place judging between the people, and he did not become angry. The Devil came to him in the form of a man to anger him while he was fasting and wished to take a midday rest. He struck the door violently. He said: "Who is this?" He said: "A man with a need." So he sent someone with him, and said: "I am not satisfied with this man." He sent another with him, and said: "I am not satisfied with this." He went out to him, took his hand, and went with him, until when he was in the market he left him and departed. So he was named Dhul-Kifl.

⁕ Ibn al-Muthanna related to us, he said: 'Affan ibn Muslim related to us, he said: Wuhayb related to us, he said: Dawud related to us, from Mujahid, he said: When al-Yasa' grew old he said: "If only I could appoint over the people a man who would act among them during my lifetime, so that I might see how he acts." He gathered the people and said: "Who will undertake for me three things, that I may appoint him: he fasts by day, stands in prayer by night, and does not become angry?" A man whom people looked down upon stood and said: "I will." He said: "You fast by day, stand in prayer by night, and do not become angry?" He said: "Yes." He dismissed them that day, and said the same thing the next day. The people were silent, and that man stood and said: "I will," so he appointed him. Iblis then began saying to the devils: "Against so-and-so, do such-and-such," but they were unable (to overcome him). He said: "Leave him to me." He came to him in the form of an old, poor shaykh, as he lay down for his midday rest, for he did not sleep by night or by day except that nap. He knocked at the door. He said: "Who is this?" He said: "An old oppressed shaykh." So he got up and opened the door, and the shaykh began recounting to him: "Between me and my people there is a dispute, and they have wronged me and done this and that to me," and he prolonged it upon him until the time of the afternoon came and the midday rest had passed. He said: "When you go out (to pray), come to me and I will take your right for you." So he went and returned, and sat in his place, looking to see whether he would see the shaykh, but he did not see him. He sought him out, and on the next day he judged among the people while awaiting him, but did not see him. When he returned to his midday rest and lay down, (the shaykh) came, knocked at the door, and said: "Who is this?" He said: "The old oppressed shaykh." He opened for him, and said: "Did I not tell you: when you sit, come to me?" He said: "They are the most wicked people; when they know you are sitting, they say: 'We will give you your right,' and when you rise they deny me." He said: "Go, and when you go out (to pray), come to me." He said: "The midday rest escaped him. He went out and looked, but did not see him, and sleep overcame him. He said to some of his household: 'Do not let anyone approach this door until I have slept, for sleep has overpowered me.' When that hour came, (the shaykh) came. The man said to him: 'Behind you!' He said: 'I came to him yesterday and told him my affair.' He said: 'By God, we were ordered not to let anyone approach him.' When (the shaykh) was unable (to enter), he looked and saw a window in the house, so he climbed in through it, and found that he was inside the house, and that he was knocking at the door." He said: "The man awoke and said: 'O so-and-so, did I not order you?'" (The shaykh) said: "As far as I am concerned, by God, I was not brought (in). Look where I came from." He said: "So he got up to the door, and found it locked as he had locked it, and found him inside the house with him. He recognized him and said: 'Are you an enemy of God?' He said: 'Yes, you have defeated me in everything, so I did what you see to anger you.' So he named him Dhul-Kifl, because he undertook a matter and fulfilled it."

⁕ al-Qasim related to us, he said: al-Husayn related to us, he said: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿and Dhul-Kifl⁠﴾: He said: "A righteous man, not a prophet, who undertook for the prophet of his people that he would suffice him in the affair of his people, establish them, and judge among them with justice, and he did so, and so he was named Dhul-Kifl."

⁕ Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, he said: Abu 'Asim related to us, he said: 'Isa related to us, and al-Harith related to me, he said: al-Hasan related to us, he said: Warqa' related to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, similarly, except that he said: "and judges among them with truth."

⁕ al-Qasim related to us, he said: al-Husayn related to us, he said: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Abu Ma'shar, from Muhammad ibn Qays, who said: There was in the Children of Israel a righteous king who grew old, so he gathered his people and said: "Which of you will guarantee for me this my kingship, on condition that he fasts by day, stands in prayer by night, judges among the Children of Israel by what God has sent down, and does not become angry?" None stood except a young man, so (the king) looked down on him for his youth and said: "Which of you will guarantee for me this my kingship, on condition that he fasts by day, stands in prayer by night, does not become angry, and judges among the Children of Israel by what God has sent down?" None stood except that young man. He (the king) looked down on him, and when it was the third time he said the same, and none stood except that young man. He said: "Come," and left between him and his kingship. The young man stood (in prayer) one night, and when morning came he began judging among the Children of Israel. When midday came he went to take a midday rest, and the Devil came to him in the form of a man from the sons of Adam, pulled his garment, and said: "Do you sleep while the litigants are at your door?" He said: "When evening comes, come to me." So he waited for him in the evening, but he did not come. When midday came he went to take a midday rest, (the Devil) pulled his garment and said: "Do you sleep while the litigants are at your door?" He said: "I told you: come to me in the evening; you did not come to me. Come to me in the evening." When evening came he waited for him, but he did not come. When he went to take a midday rest, he pulled his garment and said: "Do you sleep while the litigants are at your door?" He said: "Tell me who you are; if you were of mankind you would have heard what you said." He said: "I am the Devil. I came to tempt you, but God protected you from me." He then judged among the Children of Israel by what God had sent down for a long time, and he is Dhul-Kifl. He was named Dhul-Kifl because he undertook the kingship.

⁕ Bishr related to us, he said: Yazid related to us, he said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada, from Abu Musa al-Ash'ari, who said while addressing the people: "Dhul-Kifl was not a prophet, but he was a righteous servant who undertook the work of a righteous man at his death. He used to pray a hundred prayers to God every day, and God praised him well for his undertaking of it."

⁕ Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: al-Hakam related to us, he said: 'Amr related to us, he said: As for Dhul-Kifl, there was a king over the Children of Israel, and when death came to him he said: "Who will guarantee for me that he will suffice me over the Children of Israel, not become angry, and pray a hundred prayers every day?" Dhul-Kifl said: "I will." So Dhul-Kifl began judging among the people, and when he finished he prayed a hundred prayers. The Devil plotted against him, and waited until he had judged among the people, finished his prayer, lay down and slept. The Devil came to his door and began knocking, so he went out to him and said: "I have been wronged and treated badly." He gave him his ring and said: "Go, and bring me your companion, and wait for him." The other was slow to come, until when (the Devil) knew that he had slept and lain down, he came to the door again in order to anger him, and began knocking, and scratched his own face so that blood flowed. He came out to him and said: "What is the matter with you?" He said: "He did not follow me, and I was struck and treated thus." Dhul-Kifl seized him and was surprised at his affair, and said: "Tell me who you are?" and seized him forcefully. He told him who he was.

⁕ al-Hasan related to us, he said: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, he said: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatada, regarding His saying ﴿and Dhul-Kifl⁠﴾: He said: Abu Musa al-Ash'ari said: "Dhul-Kifl was not a prophet, but he undertook the prayer of a man who used to pray a hundred prayers every day, and he fulfilled it, so he was named Dhul-Kifl." He placed Ishmael, Idris and Dhul-Kifl in the accusative, in conjunction with Ayyub, then resumed with His saying ﴿kull⁠﴾ (each), and said ﴿kullun min al-sabirin⁠﴾ (each of them of the patient). The meaning of the statement: all of them were people of patience in what befell them for God's sake.

* *

As for His saying ﴿And We admitted them into Our mercy; indeed they were of the righteous⁠﴾:

He, exalted is He, says: And We admitted Ishmael, Idris and Dhul-Kifl (the pronominal suffixes of "them" referring back to them) ﴿into Our mercy; indeed they were of the righteous⁠﴾, meaning: indeed they were among those who were righteous, who obeyed God and acted on what He commanded.

The words concerning the interpretation (ta'wil, the scholarly explanation of meaning) of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And Dhu al-Nun, when he went off in anger, thinking that We would not decree (a restriction) upon him, and he called out in the darkness: There is no god but You; glory be to You; indeed I have been among the wrongdoers﴾ [21:87]

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: Remember, O Muhammad, Dhu al-Nun, meaning the companion of the fish (al-nun), and al-nun is the fish. By Dhu al-Nun He means Yunus ibn Matta (Jonah son of Matthew), and we have mentioned his story in Surat Yunus in a way that makes repeating it here unnecessary. His saying ﴿when he went off in anger﴾ means: when he went off angry.

The exegetes (ahl al-ta'wil) differed over the meaning of his going off angry, about whom his going was, and at whom his anger was directed. Some of them said: his going was away from his people, and he was angry at them.

Those who said this include: Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, he said: my father related to me, he said: my paternal uncle related to me, he said: my father related to me from his father, from Ibn Abbas, concerning His saying ﴿And Dhu al-Nun, when he went off in anger﴾: he was angry at his people.

⁕ I was told, on the authority of al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd related to us, who said: I heard al-Dahhak say concerning His saying ﴿when he went off in anger﴾: as for his anger, it was directed at his people.

Others said: he went away from his people angry at his Lord, when He removed the punishment from them after He had promised it to them.

Those who said this, and the mention of the cause of his anger at his Lord, in their words:

⁕ Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Salamah related to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from Yazid ibn Ziyad, from Abd Allah ibn Abi Salamah, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, who said: Allah sent him, meaning Yunus, to the people of his town, but they rejected what he brought them and refused him. When they did that, Allah revealed to him: I am sending the punishment upon them on such-and-such a day, so leave from among them and inform his people of what Allah promised him of His punishment upon them. They said: Watch him, for if he leaves from among you, then by Allah it will certainly happen as he promised you. When the night came in which they had been promised the punishment, and at its dawn he set out at night and was seen by the people, they left the town for an open area of their land, and they separated every animal from its young, then they cried out to Allah and asked Him to revoke (the decree), and He revoked it for them. Yunus waited for news of the town and its people, until a passer-by came past him and he said: What did the people of the town do? He said: They did that their prophet had left from among them; they knew that he had spoken truly about what he promised them of punishment, so they left their town for an open area of land, then they separated every mother from her young, cried out to Allah and repented to Him, and He accepted from them and delayed the punishment from them. He said: At that Yunus became angry and said: By Allah, I will never return to them as a liar, ever! I promised them punishment on a day, then it was averted from them, and he went off on his own way, angry.

⁕ Ibn Bashshar related to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far related to us, he said: Awf related to us, from Sa'id ibn Abi al-Hasan, who said: It reached me that when Yunus committed the sin, he set off angry at his Lord, and Satan made him slip.

⁕ al-Qasim related to us, he said: al-Husayn related to us, he said: Yahya ibn Zakariyya ibn Abi Za'ida related to us, from Mujalid ibn Sa'id, from al-Sha'bi, concerning His saying ﴿when he went off in anger﴾, he said: angry at his Lord.

⁕ al-Harith related to us, he said: Abd al-Aziz related to us, he said: Sufyan related to us, from Isma'il ibn Abd al-Malik, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, and he mentioned something like the report of Ibn Humayd from Salamah, and he added in it: He said: So Yunus went out looking for the punishment, but he saw nothing. He said: They had tested me with a lie, so he went off angry at his Lord until he came to the sea.

⁕ Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Salamah related to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Ishaq related to us, from Rabi'a ibn Abi Abd al-Rahman, from Wahb ibn Munabbih al-Yamani, who said: I heard him say: Yunus ibn Matta was a righteous servant, but he had a narrowness in his nature. When the burdens of prophethood were placed upon him, and it has burdens which only a few can bear, he buckled under them like a young camel [[al-rab'": the young of the she-camel, the first one that is loaded.]] buckles under its load. He threw it down before him and fled from it. Allah said to His Prophet (ﷺ): ﴿So be patient as the steadfast messengers were patient﴾ and ﴿be patient for the judgment of your Lord, and do not be like the companion of the fish﴾, meaning: do not meet My command as he met it. This statement, I mean the statement of the one who said: he went away from his people angry at his Lord, is more fitting to the interpretation of the verse, due to the indication of His saying ﴿and thought that We would not decree upon him﴾ on that. As for those who interpreted it to mean that he went off angry at his people, they only claimed that they did that out of disapproval, that a prophet among the prophets would be angry at his Lord, and out of magnifying that. By saying that he went off angry at his people, they have entered into a matter even greater than what they denounced. That is because those who said that he went off angry at his Lord also differed about the cause of his going away in that way. Some of them said: he only did what he did out of distaste at being among a people who had tested him concerning the falsity of what he promised them, and he was ashamed before them, and he did not know the reason by which the affliction had been averted from them. Some who held this view said: among the customs of his people from whom he parted was the killing of whoever had been tested with lying, perhaps they would kill him because he had promised them punishment, and the punishment they had been promised did not descend upon them. We have already mentioned the report concerning that in Surat Yunus, so we disliked repeating it in this place.

Others said: rather, he was only angry at his Lord because He commanded him to go to a people to warn them of His might and call them to Him. So he asked his Lord to give him respite so that he could prepare himself to set out to them. It was said to him: The matter is quicker than that. He was not given respite until he wished to be given respite to take a sandal to put on. He was told something similar to the first statement, and he was a man with narrowness in his nature. He said: My Lord hurried me so that I could not take a sandal, and so he went off angry.

Among those to whom this statement is attributed is al-Hasan al-Basri. al-Harith related this to me, he said: al-Hasan ibn Musa related to us, from Abu Hilal, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, from him.

Abu Ja'far said: Neither of these two statements contains any description of the Prophet of Allah Yunus (peace be upon him) except that it falls short of what was described by those who said he went off angry at his people. That is because his going away from his people angry at them, when Allah, exalted is He, had commanded him to remain among them to convey His message to them and warn them of His might and His punishment for their abandoning belief in Him and acting in obedience to You, there is no doubt that this contains what it contains. Had it not been that he (ﷺ) committed what those who described him attributed to him, namely the committing of a sin, Allah, exalted is His remembrance, would not have punished him with the punishment He mentioned in His Book, nor described him with the description He described him with, saying to His Prophet (ﷺ): ﴿And do not be like the companion of the fish, when he called out while he was distressed﴾, and He says: ﴿So the fish swallowed him while he was blameworthy. Had he not been of those who glorify (Allah), he would have remained in its belly until the day they are resurrected﴾.

* *

His saying ﴿and thought that We would not decree upon him﴾

The exegetes differed over its interpretation. Some of them said: its meaning is: he thought that We would not punish him with constriction, from their saying "I decreed (qadartu) upon so-and-so" when I restricted him, as Allah, exalted is His praise, said: ﴿And whoever has his provision restricted, let him spend from what Allah has given him﴾.

Those who said this include: Ali related to me, he said: Abd Allah ibn Salih related to us, he said: Mu'awiya related to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, concerning His saying ﴿and thought that We would not decree upon him﴾, he says: he thought that the punishment which had befallen him would not seize him.

⁕ Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, he said: my father related to me, he said: my paternal uncle related to me, he said: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, ﴿and thought that We would not decree upon him﴾, he says: he thought that We would not inflict upon him punishment or affliction for what he did to his people in his anger when he was angry at them, and his fleeing, and the punishment of the fish seizing him.

⁕ Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna related to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far related to us, from Shu'ba, from al-Hakam, from Mujahid, that he said concerning this verse ﴿and thought that We would not decree upon him﴾, he said: he thought that We would not punish him for his sin.

⁕ Musa ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Masruqi related to me, he said: Zayd ibn Hubab related to us, he said: Shu'ba related to me, from Mujahid, and he did not mention al-Hakam in it.

⁕ Bishr related to us, he said: Yazid related to us, he said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada, concerning His saying ﴿and thought that We would not decree upon him﴾, he said: he says: he thought that We would not punish him.

⁕ Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la related to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada and al-Kalbi, concerning ﴿and thought that We would not decree upon him﴾, the two of them said: he thought that We would not inflict punishment upon him.

⁕ I was told, on the authority of al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd related to us, who said: I heard al-Dahhak say concerning His saying ﴿and thought that We would not decree﴾, he says: he thought that Allah would not inflict upon him punishment or affliction for his anger which he showed at his people, and his separation from them.

⁕ Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Jarir related to us, from Mansur, from Ibn Abbas, concerning His saying ﴿and thought that We would not decree upon him﴾, he said: the affliction which had befallen him.

Others said: rather, the meaning of that is: he thought that He would be unable to (decree), so that He would not be able to restrict him.

Those who said this: Ibn Bashshar related to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far related to us, he said: Awf related to us, from Sa'id ibn Abi al-Hasan, who said: It reached me that when Yunus committed the sin, he set off angry at his Lord, and Satan made him slip, until he thought that We would not be able to restrict him. He said: He had prior devotion and glorification, but Allah refused to leave him to Satan. So He seized him and cast him into the belly of the fish, and he remained in the belly of the fish for forty periods of night and day. Allah held back his soul so that He did not kill him there, and he repented to his Lord in the belly of the fish and reconsidered himself. He said: So he said ﴿Glory be to You; indeed I have been among the wrongdoers﴾. He said: So Allah drew him out of the belly of the fish through His mercy, because of the prior worship and glorification he had performed, and made him among the righteous. Awf said: It also reached me that he said in his supplication: I have built for You a mosque in a place which no one has built before me.

⁕ Ibn Bashshar related to us, he said: Hawdha related to us, he said: Awf related to us, from al-Hasan, ﴿and thought that We would not decree upon him﴾. He had prior worship and glorification, so Allah made up for it with them and did not leave him to Satan.

⁕ Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Salamah related to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Harith, from Ayas ibn Mu'awiya al-Madani, that whenever Yunus was mentioned in his presence, and His saying ﴿and thought that We would not decree upon him﴾, Ayas would say: Then why did he flee?

Others said: rather, that has the meaning of a question, and its interpretation is: Did he think that We would not be able to restrict him?

Those who said this: Yunus related to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His saying ﴿and thought that We would not decree upon him﴾: He said: This is a question. And concerning His saying ﴿then of what use would warnings be﴾, he said: this is also a question.

Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of these statements in its interpretation, in my view, is the statement of the one who said: it refers to: Yunus thought that We would not confine him and restrict him, as a punishment for him for going off angry at his Lord.

We said that this is more fitting to the interpretation of the word, because it is not permissible to attribute to him disbelief when He had chosen him for prophethood, and described him as having thought that his Lord would be unable to do what He willed for him and would not be able to (decree) upon him, and it is described for him that he was ignorant of the power of Allah, and that is a description of him as a disbeliever, and it is not permissible for anyone to describe him with that. As for what Ibn Zayd said, it is a statement which would be good if there were evidence in the speech that it was a question, but there is no indication in it that it is so. The Arabs do not omit anything from speech for which they have a need unless they leave an indication that it is intended in the speech. So if there is no indication in His saying ﴿and thought that We would not decree upon him﴾ that the intended meaning is a question, as Ibn Zayd said, it is known that it is not that. When these two views are invalid, the third is sound, and it is what we have said.

* *

His saying ﴿and he called out in the darkness﴾

The exegetes differed over who is meant by these darknesses. Some of them said: by them is meant the darkness of the night, the darkness of the sea, and the darkness of the belly of the fish.

Those who said this: al-Qasim related to us, he said: al-Husayn related to us, he said: Hajjaj related to me, from Isra'il, from Abu Ishaq, from Amr ibn Maymun, ﴿and he called out in the darkness﴾, he said: the darkness of the belly of the fish, the darkness of the sea, and the darkness of the night. Ibn Jurayj likewise said.

⁕ Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Salamah related to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from Yazid ibn Ziyad, from Abd Allah ibn Abi Salamah, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, who said: He called out in the darkness: the darkness of the night, the darkness of the sea, and the darkness of the belly of the fish ﴿There is no god but You; glory be to You; indeed I have been among the wrongdoers﴾.

⁕ Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Sulami related to me, he said: Abu Asim related to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Rifa'a informed us, he said: I heard Muhammad ibn Ka'b say concerning this verse ﴿and he called out in the darkness﴾, he said: the darkness of the night, the darkness of the sea, and the darkness of the belly of the fish.

⁕ Bishr related to us, he said: Yazid related to us, he said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada, his saying ﴿and he called out in the darkness﴾, he said: the darkness of the night, the darkness of the sea, and the darkness of the belly of the fish.

⁕ Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la related to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada ﴿and he called out in the darkness﴾, he said: the darkness of the belly of the fish, the darkness of the sea, and the darkness of the night.

Others said: he only meant by that that he called out in the darkness of the inside of a fish, inside another fish in the sea. They said: that is what the darknesses are.

Those who said this: Ibn Bashshar related to us, he said: Abd al-Rahman related to us, he said: Sufyan related to us, from Mansur, from Salim ibn Abi al-Ja'd, ﴿and he called out in the darkness﴾, he said: Allah revealed to the fish that it should not harm his flesh or bones. Then a fish swallowed another fish, and (Yunus) said ﴿and he called out in the darkness﴾, he said: the darkness of the fish, then a fish, then the darkness of the sea.

Abu Ja'far said: The correct statement on this matter is to say: Allah informed us about Yunus that he called out to Him in the darknesses ﴿that there is no god but You; glory be to You; indeed I have been among the wrongdoers﴾. There is no doubt that by one of the darknesses He meant the belly of the fish, and by the other the darkness of the sea, and about the third there is disagreement. That third may be the darkness of the night, and it may be that the fish was inside another fish. There is no evidence that indicates which of these is which, so there is no statement on this that is closer to the truth than submitting to the apparent wording of the revelation.

* *

His saying ﴿There is no god but You; glory be to You﴾

It means: Yunus called out with this statement, confessing his sin and repenting of his error ﴿indeed I have been among the wrongdoers﴾ in my disobedience toward You.

As (it was reported):

⁕ Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Salamah related to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from Yazid ibn Ziyad, from Abd Allah ibn Abi Salamah, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, who said: ﴿and he called out in the darkness, that there is no god but You; glory be to You; indeed I have been among the wrongdoers﴾, confessing his sin, repenting of his error.

⁕ al-Qasim related to us, he said: al-Husayn related to us, he said: Hajjaj related to me, he said, Abu Ma'shar said: Muhammad ibn Qays said: His saying ﴿There is no god but You; glory be to You﴾: I have done nothing, for I have not worshipped anything other than You. ﴿Indeed I have been among the wrongdoers﴾ when I disobeyed You.

⁕ al-Qasim related to us, he said: al-Husayn related to us, he said: Ja'far ibn Sulayman related to us, from Awf al-A'rabi, who said: When Yunus was in the belly of the fish, he thought that he had died. Then he moved his leg, and when it moved, he prostrated in that very place, then he called out: O my Lord, I have taken for You a mosque in a place which no one has taken before.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 21, verse 87 (part 2 of 2):

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, saying: Ibn Ishaq narrated to me from one who narrated to him, from Abdullah ibn Rafi', the freedman of Umm Salamah, wife of the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: I heard Abu Hurairah saying: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When Allah willed to imprison Yunus (Jonah) in the belly of the fish, Allah revealed to the fish: Take him, but do not tear any flesh of his nor break any of his bones. So it took him, then plunged with him down to its dwelling place in the sea. When it reached the bottom of the sea, Yunus heard a sound, and he said to himself: What is this? He said: Then Allah revealed to him, while he was in the belly of the fish: This is the glorification of the creatures of the sea. He said: So he glorified (Allah) while in the belly of the fish, and the angels heard his glorification. They said: O our Lord, we hear a weak sound in a strange land? He said: That is My servant Yunus, who disobeyed Me, so I imprisoned him in the belly of the fish in the sea. They said: Is it the righteous servant from whom a righteous deed ascended to You every day and night? He said: Yes. He said: Then they interceded for him at that point, so He commanded the fish, and it cast him onto the shore, as Allah, blessed and exalted, said: ﴿And he was sick﴾."

On the interpretation of His words, ﴿So We answered him and delivered him from distress. And thus do We deliver the believers﴾ (21:88):

He, exalted is His mention, says: ﴿So We answered him﴾, meaning, We answered Yunus's supplication to Us when he called upon Us in the belly of the fish, and We delivered him from the distress he was in, by imprisoning him in the belly of the fish, and his distress was because of his sin and wrongdoing. ﴿And thus do We deliver the believers﴾: He, whose praise is exalted, says: Just as We delivered Yunus from the anguish of confinement in the belly of the fish in the sea when he called upon Us, so too do We deliver the believers from their distress when they seek Our aid and call upon Us.

Reports consistent with what we have said about this have come down.

Mention of those who said this: Imran ibn Bakkar al-Kulla'i related to us, saying: Yahya ibn Abd al-Rahman related to us, saying: Abu Yahya ibn Abd al-Rahman related to us, saying: Bishr ibn Mansur related to me, from Ali ibn Zayd, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, who said: I heard Sa'd ibn Malik say: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "The Name of Allah which, when invoked by it, He answers, and when asked by it, He gives, is the supplication of Yunus ibn Matta." He said: I said: "O Messenger of Allah, is it specific to Yunus ibn Matta, or is it for the whole community of Muslims?" He said: "It is specific to Yunus ibn Matta, and general for the believers when they call upon Him with it. Have you not heard the saying of Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He: ﴿Then he called out in the darknesses: There is no god but You, glory be to You, indeed I have been of the wrongdoers. So We answered him and delivered him from distress, and thus do We deliver the believers﴾?" So it is a condition from Allah for whoever calls upon Him with it.

The readers differed concerning the recitation of His words ﴿nunji al-mu'minin﴾. The readers of the regional centres, other than Asim, recited it with two nuns, the second one silent, from anjaynahu, so that it means "We deliver him." They recited it that way, while its writing in the codices is with one nun, because if it were recited with one nun and a doubled jim, in the passive sense, "al-mu'minun" would be in the nominative, whereas in the codices it is in the accusative; and if it were recited with one nun and a single jim, the verb would belong to the believers and they would be in the nominative, and it would also necessarily have been written with an alif, since "najja" is from the "waw" class, whereas in the codices it is written with a ya.

If someone says: How was it written with one nun, when you know that the rule for it when recited as "nunajji" is that it be written with two nuns? It is said: Because the second nun became silent, and a silent letter is not clearly audible on the tongue, so it was dropped, just as they did with "illa": they dropped the nun from "in" because it was hidden, being assimilated into the lam of "la." Asim recited it as "nujji al-mu'minin" with one nun, a doubled jim, and a silent ya. If Asim's basis for this recitation was the Arab usage "darab al-darb Zaydan," in which he referred to the verbal noun, which is the rescue, and made the predicate, namely the nominal complement of the passive, "al-mu'minin," as though he intended "wa-kadhalika najja al-mu'minin," referring to the rescue, then it is a valid line of reasoning, though others are more correct. Otherwise, whoever recited it as Asim did has committed a grammatical error, because "al-mu'minin" is a noun in the passive reading, and the Arabs put nouns of that kind in the nominative. What led Asim to this reading was that he found the codices with one nun, while in his recitation, following what the readers recite, he would have to add another nun not present in the codex; he thought that was an addition to what is not in the codex, and he did not know a reason for its omission that would direct him to it.

Abu Ja'far says: The correct recitation, which we do not consider permissible to depart from, is what the readers of the regional centres recite, with two nuns and a single jim, because of the consensus of the authoritative readers upon it and their rejection of anything contrary to it.

The commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 21, verses 89–90:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And Zakariyya, when he called out to his Lord, "My Lord, do not leave me alone (without an heir), though You are the best of inheritors."﴾ (21:89) ﴿So We answered him and gave him Yahya, and We made his wife fit for him. Indeed, they used to hasten to good deeds and would call upon Us in hope and in fear, and they were humbly submissive to Us.﴾ (21:90)

Allah, exalted is His remembrance, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ):

And mention, O Muhammad, Zakariyya when he called out to his Lord, ﴿"My Lord, do not leave me alone"﴾, solitary, ﴿"alone"﴾, having no child and no offspring, ﴿"though You are the best of inheritors"﴾. He means: grant me an heir from the family of Ya'qub who will inherit from me. Then he referred the matter to Allah and said, "though You are the best of inheritors." Allah, mighty is His praise, says: So We answered Zakariyya's supplication, and We gave him Yahya as a son and an heir who would inherit from him, and We made his wife fit for him.

The people of ta'wil (interpretation) differed regarding the meaning of the rectification which Allah, mighty is His praise, intended in His saying ﴿and We made his wife fit for him﴾. Some of them said: She was barren, so He rectified her by making her fertile.

Those who said this:

- Muhammad ibn Ubayd al-Muharibi narrated to us, saying: Hatim ibn Isma'il narrated to us, from Humayd ibn Sakhr, from Ammar, from Sa'id, regarding His saying ﴿and We made his wife fit for him﴾: she was unable to bear children.

- Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Ibn 'Abbas said, regarding His saying ﴿and made his wife fit for him﴾: He gave him her child.

- Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding His saying ﴿and We made his wife fit for him﴾: she was barren, so Allah made her fertile, and granted him Yahya from her.

Others said: She had a bad character, and Allah rectified her for him by granting her good character.

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: The correct view on this is that it be said: Allah rectified his wife for Zakariyya, as He informed, exalted is His remembrance, by making her fertile and of good character, because all of these are among the meanings of His rectifying her. Allah, mighty is His praise, did not single out any one of these over the others in His Book, nor through the tongue of His Messenger, nor did He establish any evidence for specifying it, so it remains general unless there comes something that necessitates accepting that it is meant to be specific to some and not others.

* *

As for His saying ﴿Indeed, they used to hasten to good deeds﴾:

Allah says: Indeed those whom We named, meaning Zakariyya, his wife, and Yahya, used to hasten to good deeds in obedience to Us and in acting by what brings them near to Us. As for His saying ﴿and would call upon Us in hope and in fear﴾, exalted is His remembrance says: and they used to worship Us in hope and in fear. Here, by "calling upon" is meant worship, as He said: ﴿And I will withdraw from you and what you call upon besides Allah, and I will call upon my Lord; perhaps I will not be unhappy in calling upon my Lord.﴾ By His saying ﴿in hope﴾ is meant that they worshipped Him out of desire for what they hoped from His mercy and bounty, ﴿and in fear﴾ means fear of His punishment and retribution, through their abandoning His worship and their committing disobedience.

The people of interpretation said similar to what we have said on this.

Those who said this: Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, regarding ﴿Indeed, they used to hasten to good deeds and would call upon Us in hope and in fear﴾: in hope of Allah's mercy, and in fear of Allah's punishment.

- Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿and would call upon Us in hope and in fear﴾: fear and longing, and he said: It is not fitting for either of them to separate from the other.

The reciters differed in reading this. The majority of the reciters of the major cities read ﴿raghaban wa rahaban﴾ with a fatha on the ghayn and the ha, from al-raghab and al-rahab. It was narrated from al-A'mash that he agreed with the reciters on this, but it was also narrated from him that he read rughban wa ruhban, with a damma on the ra' in both words and a sukun on the ghayn and the ha.

The correct reading is that of the majority of the reciters of the cities, which is the fatha on both words.

* *

As for His saying ﴿and they were humbly submissive to Us﴾:

He says: they were humble and submissive to Us, not arrogant in refusing our worship and our supplication.

The commentary on the verse: "And she who guarded her chastity, so We breathed into her of Our spirit, and We made her and her son a sign for the worlds" (21:91).

Interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And she who guarded her chastity, so We breathed into her of Our spirit, and We made her and her son a sign for the worlds﴾ (21:91).

He, exalted is His remembrance, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): "And mention her who guarded her chastity," meaning Maryam bint Imran.

By His saying ﴿guarded﴾ He means that she preserved her private part and kept it from what Allah had forbidden her to make lawful.

Scholars differed concerning the private part which Allah, mighty is His praise, meant when He said she guarded it. Some said: He meant by this her own private part, that she guarded it from immorality.

Others said: He meant by this the opening of her garment (jayb), that she prevented Jibril from it before she knew that he was a messenger of her Lord, and before she recognised him with knowledge. They said: What indicates this is His saying ﴿so We breathed into her﴾, and His saying ﴿And she who guarded her chastity﴾ follows it. They said: It was thus known that the meaning of the speech is: "and she who guarded her garment's opening, so We breathed into her of Our spirit."

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: The more correct of the two opinions in our view regarding the interpretation of this is the statement of the one who said: she guarded her private part from immorality, because that is the more prevalent of its two meanings, and the more apparent in the outward sense of the speech. ﴿So We breathed into her of Our spirit﴾ means: so We breathed into the opening of her garment of Our spirit. We have already mentioned the disagreement of those who differed concerning the meaning of His saying ﴿so We breathed into her﴾ in other than this place, and the more correct of what is said about it has been mentioned earlier, in a way that makes repeating it here unnecessary.

* *

And His saying ﴿and We made her and her son a sign for the worlds﴾.

He says: We made Maryam and her son an admonition for the people of their time, who take lesson from them and reflect upon their affair, so that they know Our great authority and Our power over what We will. It is said "a sign" (ayah) and not "two signs," although two were mentioned, because the meaning of the speech is: We made them both a banner for Us and a proof. Each of them, in indicating Allah and His great power, stands in place of the other, when their matter in indicating Allah is one.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 21, verses 92–93:

The interpretation of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, this community of yours is one community, and I am your Lord, so worship Me⁠﴾ (92)

His saying, may His remembrance be exalted, means: Indeed, this religion of yours is one religion, and I am your Lord, O people, so worship Me, rather than the deities, the idols, and all else that you worship besides Me.

The interpreters of the Qur'an have said the same as what we have said concerning this.

Those who said this: ʿAlī narrated to me, saying: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, saying: Muʿāwiyah narrated to me, from ʿAlī, from Ibn ʿAbbās, regarding His saying ﴿your community⁠﴾ [and] ﴿one community⁠﴾, he said: your religion is one religion.

Al-Qāsim narrated to us, saying: al-Ḥusayn narrated to us, saying: Ḥajjāj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Mujāhid said, regarding His saying ﴿Indeed, this community of yours is one community⁠﴾, he said: your religion is one religion.

The second word "community" (ummah) is put in the accusative as a circumstantial (qaṭʿ) construction, and the majority of the reciters of the major cities read it in the accusative, and this is the correct reading in our view, because the second "community" is indefinite while the first is definite.

Since that is so, and since the predicate, before the indefinite noun came, was complete without it, the proper construction is the accusative. This is in addition to the consensus of the authoritative reciters upon it. It has been reported that ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Isḥāq, in the nominative, recited it as ﴿ummah wāḥidah⁠﴾ with the intention of repeating the statement, as though he meant: Indeed, this community of yours, this is one community.

* *

The interpretation of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿But they cut their affair among themselves into sects; each to Us they will return⁠﴾ (93)

His saying, may His remembrance be exalted, means: The people separated in their religion, which God had commanded them and called them to, and so they became factions. The Jews became Jewish, the Christians became Christian, and the idols were worshipped. Then He, may His praise be exalted, informed them of what they would come to, and that the return of all the adherents of religions is to Him, warning by this the deviant and misguided among them, and informing them that He is watching them, and that He will requite all of them: the good-doer with his goodness, and the wrongdoer with his wrongdoing.

The interpreters of the Qur'an have said the same as what we have said concerning the interpretation of His saying ﴿But they cut their affair among themselves⁠﴾.

Those who said this: Yūnus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿But they cut their affair among themselves⁠﴾, he said: "They cut" means: they differed, concerning the religion.

**The interpretation of His words, may He be exalted: ﴿So whoever does righteous deeds while he is a believer, there will be no rejection of his effort, and indeed, We are recording it for him﴾ [21:94]**

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Whoever among these people who have divided their religion does righteous deeds that God has commanded, obeying Him in His commands and prohibitions, while affirming the oneness of God, believing in His promise and His threat, and disavowing rivals and false gods, ﴿there will be no rejection of his effort﴾. That is, God will show gratitude for the deed he performed in obedience to Him while he is a believer. He will reward him in the Hereafter with the reward He promised to those who obey Him, and He will not reject that reward or deny him the recompense for his righteous deed. ﴿And indeed, We are recording it for him﴾: that is, We record all of his righteous deeds, so We do not leave any of them unrewarded, whether small or great, few or many.

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: The word al-kufran (rejection, ingratitude) is a verbal noun from the saying of a speaker: "I rejected (kafartu) so-and-so's favour, so I reject it (akfuruhu) kufran and kufranan." The poet's verse also illustrates this:

*Among the people are some whose cheeks do not sleep,*
*and my cheek; and none ungrateful to God sleeps.*

[The verse is evidence that al-kufran in His words ﴿there will be no kufran for his effort﴾ is a verbal noun from the saying of a speaker: "I rejected so-and-so's favour, so I reject it, kufran and kufranan." It is said in Lisan al-Arab (under k-f-r): "One says: he rejected God's favour, or with God's favour, kufran, kufranan, and kufuran."]

* *

The interpretation of His words, may He be exalted: ﴿And it is forbidden for a town which We destroyed that they will not return﴾ [21:95]

The readers (qurra') differed in reading His words ﴿wa-haram﴾. The majority of the readers of Kufa read it ﴿wa-hirm﴾ with a kasra on the ha', while the majority of the readers of Medina and Basra read it ﴿wa-haram﴾ with a fatha on the ha' and an alif.

The correct view on this is that both are well-known readings (qira'at) with the same meaning, not different meanings. The hirm is the haram, and the haram is the hirm, just as the hall is the halal and the halal is the hall. Whichever of the two a reader recites is correct. Ibn 'Abbas used to read it ﴿wa-hirm﴾, interpreting it as "and resolved (wa-'azm)."

⁕ Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah narrated to us, from Abu al-Mu'alla, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, that he used to read it ﴿wa-hirma 'ala qaryah﴾. He said: I said to Sa'id: "What does ḥaram mean?" He said: "Resolved (ʿazama)."

⁕ Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Abu al-Mu'alla, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, that he used to read it ﴿wa-hirmun 'ala qaryah﴾. I said to Abu al-Mu'alla: "What is al-haram?" He said: "He resolved upon it (ʿazama ʿalayha)."

⁕ Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Dawud narrated to us, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, that he used to read this verse ﴿wa-hirmun 'ala qaryatin ahlaknaha annahum la yarji'un﴾, and then none of them would return, and none of them would repent.

⁕ Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Wahhab narrated to us, saying: Dawud narrated to us, from 'Ikrimah, who said: ﴿wa-haramun 'ala qaryatin ahlaknaha annahum la yarji'un﴾. He said: "None of them could return; that is forbidden for them."

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: 'Isa ibn Farqad narrated to us, saying: Jabir al-Ju'fi narrated to us, saying: I asked Abu Ja'far about the return (al-raj'ah), and he recited this verse: ﴿wa-haramun 'ala qaryatin ahlaknaha annahum la yarji'un﴾.

So it seems that Abu Ja'far directed the interpretation of this to mean: "And it is forbidden for the people of a town whom We have caused to die that they should return to the world." However, the view stated by 'Ikrimah on this is more correct in my opinion. God, may His remembrance be exalted, informed us about the people's division of their religion, which the messengers were sent with, then He informed us about His treatment of those who were guided by what His messengers called them to, of faith in Him and obedience to Him. He then followed this with His words ﴿And it is forbidden for a town which We destroyed that they will not return﴾. It is more fitting that this be an account of His treatment of those who refused to answer His messengers, who did disobedient deeds and disbelieved in Him, so that it clarifies the state of the other town, which did not do righteous deeds and rejected Him.

If that is the case, then the meaning of the speech is: "It is forbidden for the people of a town whom We have destroyed, by sealing their hearts and sealing their hearing and sight, because they turned away from Our way and disbelieved in Our signs, that they repent and return to faith in Us, follow Our command, and do obedience to Us." And if this is the interpretation of His words ﴿wa-hirm﴾, meaning "and resolved," as Sa'id said, then the "la" in His words ﴿annahum la yarji'un﴾ is not a redundant particle (sila); rather it carries the meaning of negation, and the meaning of the speech becomes: "And We resolved upon a town We destroyed that they will not return from their disbelief." Likewise, if the meaning of ﴿wa-haram﴾ is "We make obligatory," then... Some have claimed that it is a redundant particle in this place, so the meaning of the speech is: "It is forbidden for a town We destroyed that they return." But the people of interpretation whom we have mentioned were more knowledgeable about the meaning of that than he was.

**The interpretation of His words, may He be exalted: ﴿So whoever does righteous deeds while he is a believer, there will be no rejection of his effort, and indeed, We are recording it for him﴾ [21:94]**

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Whoever among these people who have divided their religion does righteous deeds that God has commanded, obeying Him in His commands and prohibitions, while affirming the oneness of God, believing in His promise and His threat, and disavowing rivals and false gods, ﴿there will be no rejection of his effort﴾. That is, God will show gratitude for the deed he performed in obedience to Him while he is a believer. He will reward him in the Hereafter with the reward He promised to those who obey Him, and He will not reject that reward or deny him the recompense for his righteous deed. ﴿And indeed, We are recording it for him﴾: that is, We record all of his righteous deeds, so We do not leave any of them unrewarded, whether small or great, few or many.

*Among the people are some whose cheeks do not sleep,*
*and my cheek; and none ungrateful to God sleeps.*
