The Interpretation of His Words, Exalted Be He: ﴿Until, when Gog and Magog are let loose, and they swarm down from every mound﴾ (21:96)

He, exalted be His remembrance, says: until, when Gog and Magog are opened up, and they are two nations among the nations, behind their barrier.

As follows:

⁕ Isam ibn Dawud ibn al-Jarrah narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: Sufyan ibn Sa'id al-Thawri narrated to us, saying: Mansur ibn al-Mu'tamir narrated to us, from Rib'i ibn Hirash, who said: I heard Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The first of the signs: the Dajjal, the descent of 'Isa, a fire that comes out from the depths of 'Adan Abyan, driving people to the place of assembly, napping with them when they nap, and the smoke, and the beast, and then Gog and Magog." Hudhayfah said: I said: "O Messenger of Allah, what are Gog and Magog?" He said: "Gog and Magog are nations, each nation four hundred thousand, and no man among them dies until he sees a thousand eyes glancing before him from his own loins, and they are the children of Adam. They will set out toward the ruin of the world. Their vanguard will be in al-Sham and their rearguard in Iraq. They will pass by the rivers of the world and drink the Euphrates, the Tigris and the Lake of Tiberias, until they come to Bayt al-Maqdis. They will say: 'We have killed the people of the world, so let us fight those in the heavens.' They will shoot arrows toward the sky, and their arrows will come back stained with blood, and they will say: 'We have killed those in the heavens.' 'Isa and the Muslims will be on the mountain of Tur Sinin. Allah, majestic is His majesty, will reveal to 'Isa: 'Shelter My servants in the Tur and what lies beyond Ayla.' Then 'Isa will raise his head to the sky, and the Muslims will say 'Amin.' Allah will send upon them a worm called al-Naghaf, which enters their nostrils, and they will wake up dead, from the edge of al-Sham to the edge of Iraq, until the earth stinks from their corpses. Allah will command the sky, and it will rain like the mouths of water-skins, washing the earth of their corpses and their stench. At that time the sun will rise from its west."

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Hakkam narrated to us, from Abu Ja'far, from al-Rabi', from Abu al-'Aliyah, who said: Gog and Magog exceed the rest of mankind by double, and the jinn exceed mankind by double. Gog and Magog are two men whose names are Gog and Magog.

⁕ Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, who said: I heard Wahb ibn Jabir narrate, from 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr, that he said: Gog and Magog — their first will pass by a river like the Tigris, and their last will pass and say: "There was once water in this." No man among them dies without leaving behind a thousand or more descendants. And he said: After them are three nations whose number none knows but Allah: Ta'wil, Taris, and Nasik or Mansak (Shu'bah was uncertain).

⁕ Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Yahya narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from Wahb ibn Jabir al-Khaywani, who said: I asked 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr about Gog and Magog: "Are they of the children of Adam?" He said: "Yes, and after them are three nations whose number none knows but Allah: Taris, Ta'wil, and Mansak."

⁕ Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Sahl ibn Hammad Abu 'Attab narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, from al-Nu'man ibn Salim, who both said: We heard Nafi' ibn Jubayr ibn Mut'im say: 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr said: Gog and Magog have rivers which they drink dry as they wish, and women with whom they have intercourse as they wish, and trees which they devour as they wish, and no man dies without leaving behind a thousand or more descendants.

⁕ Muhammad ibn 'Ammarah narrated to us, saying: 'Abdullah ibn Musa narrated to us, saying: Zakariyya informed us, from 'Amir, from 'Amr ibn Maymun, from 'Abdullah ibn Salam, who said: No one of Gog and Magog dies without leaving behind a thousand offspring or more.

⁕ Yahya ibn Ibrahim al-Mas'udi narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to us, from his father, from his grandfather, from al-A'mash, from 'Atiyyah, who said: Abu Sa'id said: Gog and Magog will come out and leave no one alive except that they kill him, except the people of the fortresses. They will pass by the lake and drink it, and a passer-by will come and say: "It seems there was water here." Then Allah sends upon them the naghaf, until it breaks their necks and they become corpses. The people of the fortresses will say: "The enemies of Allah have perished," and they will lower a man to look, stipulating with them that if he finds them alive they will raise him up. He finds them all dead. Then Allah sends water from the sky which casts them into the sea, the earth is purified of them, and the people after them plant trees and palms, and the earth brings forth its fruit as it did in the time of Gog and Magog.

⁕ Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, from 'Ubaydullah ibn Abi Yazid, who said: Ibn 'Abbas saw children leaping upon one another while playing, and Ibn 'Abbas said: "This is how Gog and Magog will come out."

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: al-Hakam narrated to us, saying: 'Amr ibn Qays narrated to us, saying: It reached us that an angel beyond the barrier sends horsemen each day to guard the barrier, for Gog and Magog cannot feel safe that they will come out against them. He said: So they hear a clamor and a terrible noise.

⁕ Ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Abu Ishaq, that 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr said: No man of Gog and Magog dies until a thousand are born to him from his loins, and behind them are three nations whose number none knows but Allah: Mansak, Ta'wil, and Taris.

⁕ Ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, from 'Amr al-Bakali, who said: Allah divided the angels, mankind and the jinn into ten parts. Nine of them are the Karubiyun, who are the angels that carry the Throne, and they also are those who glorify Allah night and day without cease. And those of the angels who remain are for the command of Allah, His revelation and His message. Then He divided mankind and the jinn into ten parts, and nine of them are the jinn; no child is born of mankind except that nine children are born of the jinn. Then He divided mankind into ten parts, nine of which are Gog and Magog, and the rest of mankind is one part.

⁕ al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij, regarding His words ﴿until, when Gog and Magog are let loose﴾: They are two nations beyond the barrier of Dhu al-Qarnayn.

⁕ Ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from others, from Humayd ibn Hilal, from Abu al-Saff, who said: Ka'b said: When the time of the emergence of Gog and Magog comes, they will dig until those next to them hear the clinking of their picks. When night falls they say: "We will come tomorrow and go out," and Allah restores it as it was. They come the next day and find that Allah has restored it as it was, so they dig until those next to them hear the clinking of their picks. When night falls, Allah puts into the tongue of one of them: "We will come tomorrow and go out, God willing." They come the next day and find it as they left it, so they dig and then go out. The first troop passes by the lake and drinks its water; then the second troop passes and licks its mud; then the third troop passes and says: "There was once water here." People flee from them, and nothing stands before them. They shoot their arrows toward the sky, and they return stained with blood, and they say: "We have overcome the people of the earth and the people of the heavens." Then 'Isa ibn Maryam prays against them, saying: "O Allah, we have no power nor strength against them, so suffice us against them however You wish." Allah then sends upon them a worm called al-Naghaf, which pierces their necks. Allah sends birds which seize them with their beaks and cast them into the sea. Allah sends a spring called al-Hayat, which purifies the earth of them and makes it grow, until a pomegranate is enough to satisfy a whole household (al-Sukan). It was said: "What is al-Sukan, O Ka'b?" He said: "The household." He said: While people are in that state, news comes to them that Dhu al-Suwaykatayn is coming toward them. 'Isa sends a vanguard of seven hundred, or between seven and eight hundred. When they are in part of the road, Allah sends a pleasant southern wind, by which Allah takes the soul of every believer. Then there remain crowds of people who copulate like beasts. The likeness of the Hour is that of a man circling his mare, awaiting when she will give birth. Whoever goes beyond what I have said, and imposes upon this anything, is a fabricator.

⁕ al-'Abbas ibn al-Walid al-Bayruti narrated to us, saying: My father informed me, saying: I heard Ibn Jabir say: Muhammad ibn Jabir al-Ta'i, then al-Himsi, narrated to me, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Jubayr ibn Nufayr al-Hadrami narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me that he heard al-Nawwas ibn Sam'an al-Kilabi say: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) mentioned the Dajjal, and mentioned his affair, and that 'Isa ibn Maryam would kill him. Then he said: While he is in that state, Allah reveals to him: 'O 'Isa, I have brought forth servants of Mine against whom no one has the power to fight. So shelter My servants in the Tur.' Then Allah sends Gog and Magog, and they come from every mound, swarming down. One of them passes by the Lake of Tiberias and drinks all that is in it; then the last of them comes and says: 'There was once water in this.' The prophet of Allah, 'Isa, and his companions are besieged, until the head of an ox that day is better for one of them than a hundred dinars for one of you. The prophet of Allah, 'Isa, and his companions beseech Allah, and Allah sends upon them the naghaf in their necks, and they wake up as a single soul dead. The prophet of Allah, 'Isa, and his companions descend, and they find no place but that it is filled with their filth, their stench and their blood. The prophet of Allah, 'Isa, and his companions beseech Allah, and He sends upon them birds like the necks of Bukht camels, which carry them and cast them wherever Allah wills. Then Allah sends rain which leaves no house of clay or wool, and it washes the earth until it leaves it like a mirror."

As for His words ﴿and they swarm down from every mound﴾, the people of interpretation differed concerning who is meant by it. Some of them said: By that is meant the children of Adam, that they will come out from every place in the earth where they were buried; and by that is meant only the gathering to the place where people stand on the Day of Resurrection.

Those who said that:

⁕ Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿from every mound they swarm down﴾, who said: The people will be gathered from every place they came from on the Day of Resurrection, and that is a mound.

⁕ al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij, ﴿and they swarm down from every mound﴾. Ibn Juraij said: Mujahid said: The people will be gathered from every mound, from every place they came from on the Day of Resurrection, and that is a mound.

Others said: Rather, by it is meant Gog and Magog, and His words "they" are a pronoun for their names.

Those who said that: Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Salamah ibn Kuhayl, who said: Abu al-Za'ra' narrated to us, from 'Abdullah, that he said: Gog and Magog will come out and roam the earth and cause corruption in it. Then 'Abdullah recited ﴿and they swarm down from every mound﴾. He said: Then Allah sends upon them a beast like the naghaf, which enters their ears and nostrils, and they die of it; the earth stinks from them, and Allah, mighty and majestic, sends water which purifies the earth of them.

The correct view on this matter is what those said who said: By it is meant Gog and Magog, and that His words "they" are a pronoun for their names, on the basis of the report which Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from 'Asim ibn 'Umar, from Qatadah al-Ansari, then al-Zufari, from Mahmud ibn Labid, brother of the Banu 'Abd al-Ashhal, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Gog and Magog will be let loose, and they will come out upon the people as Allah said: ﴿from every mound they swarm down﴾, and they will cover the earth."

⁕ Ahmad ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Hushaym ibn Bashir narrated to us, saying: al-Awwam ibn Hawshab informed us, from Jabalah ibn Suhaym, from Mu'thir, who is Ibn 'Afazah al-'Abdi, from 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said, concerning what is related from 'Isa ibn Maryam: 'Isa said: "My Lord has charged me that the Dajjal will come out, and that I will descend to him. He mentioned that with him are two rods; when he sees me, Allah will destroy him." He said: "The lead will melt, until the tree and the stone will say: 'O Muslim, this is a disbeliever, so kill him.' Allah, blessed and exalted, will destroy them, and the people will return to their lands and homelands. Then Gog and Magog will meet them, swarming down from every mound. They will not come upon anything without destroying it, and they will not pass by water without drinking it."

⁕ 'Ubayd ibn Isma'il al-Hibari narrated to me, saying: al-Muharibi narrated to us, from Asbagh ibn Zayd, from al-Awwam ibn Hawshab, from Jabalah ibn Suhaym, from Mu'thir ibn 'Afazah, from 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), in a similar report.

As for His words ﴿from every mound﴾, it means from every height, elevation and hill.

Those of the people of interpretation said similarly to what we have said on this.

Those who said that: 'Ali narrated to me, saying: 'Abdullah narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words ﴿from every mound they swarm down﴾, he said: They come from every height.

⁕ Ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿from every mound they swarm down﴾, he said: From every hill.

⁕ Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words ﴿and they swarm down from every mound﴾: The mound is the elevated thing. And the poet said:

Upon the hills they sway [[This is part of a verse whose author the compiler did not name, at His words (and they swarm down from every mound). In al-Lisan (hdb) it says: he means they emerge from thick, elevated land. al-Farra' said: "from every mound they swarm down": from every hill and every elevated place; the plural is ahdab and hidab. The hadbah is what rises from the land and is thick and high, and it exists only on a mound or thick land. Tamur: from mara al-shay yamuru mawran: it moves, comes and goes, as a palm sways its branches.]]

⁕ Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words ﴿until, when Gog and Magog are let loose, and they swarm down from every mound﴾: This is the beginning of the Day of Resurrection.

As for His words ﴿they swarm down﴾, it means: they will come out walking, hastening in their gait like the swift running of the wolf, as the poet said:

Like the wolf's swift loping, when he drew near the water, the night cold upon him, and he hastened [[The verse is attributed to Labid or to al-Nabigha al-Ja'di (al-Lisan: 'sl and nsl). 'Asala al-dhi'b and al-tha'lab means he went off swiftly, moved violently in his running, and shook his head. Al-qarib is one who seeks water at night, going swiftly toward it. Nasala the walker: he hastened (of the type daraba and qatala) with nasl and nasalan. The original sense of nasalan is for the wolf, and then it was used for other things.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 21, verse 97:

The explanation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Then the true promise will draw near, and behold, the eyes of those who disbelieved will stare fixedly. "Woe to us! We were heedless of this; nay, we were wrongdoers."﴾

His saying, exalted is His remembrance: Until, when Yajuj and Majuj are let loose, the true promise draws near, and that is Allah's promise which He made to His servants, that He will resurrect them from their graves for recompense, reward and punishment, and it is undoubtedly true, as His majesty and praise have said.

And those of the exegetes (ahl al-ta'wil) said the same as what we have said concerning this.

Mention of those who said that: Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: al-Hakam ibn Bashir related to us, saying: 'Amr, meaning Ibn Qays, related to us, saying: Hudhayfah related to us: "If a man were to mount a colt after the emergence of Yajuj and Majuj, he would not ride it until the Hour arrives."

⁕ Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His saying ﴿and the true promise draws near﴾: "It draws near to them on the Day of Resurrection." The "wa" in His saying ﴿and the true promise draws near﴾ is superfluous (muqhamah), and the meaning of the speech is: Until, when Yajuj and Majuj are let loose, the true promise draws near. This is similar to His saying ﴿So when they had both submitted, and he had flung him down upon his forehead, and We called out to him﴾, meaning: "We called out," without a "wa," as the poet Imru' al-Qays said:

"So when we crossed the courtyard of the tribe, and he (the steed) veered with us into the belly of a level tract, with winding sand-dunes and tangled hillocks."

[[The verse is from the Mu'allaqa of Imru' al-Qays ibn Hujr al-Kindi (Mukhtar al-Shi'r al-Jahili, with the commentary of Mustafa al-Saqa, Mustafa al-Babi al-Halabi edition, p. 27). He said: "ajaznā" means "we crossed." "Sāḥa" means the open space before the dwellings. "Khabt" is a level, low-lying land. "Ḥaqf" of sand is a bent dune, its plural being ḥiqāf; it is also narrated as "rukām," meaning piled one upon another. "ʿAqanqal" means tangled, one part entangled in another. The verse is evidence that the "wa" in His saying "wa-intaḥā" is superfluous; he means: "when we crossed the courtyard of the tribe, he veered." It is similar to the "wa" in His saying, exalted is He: (Until, when Yajuj and Majuj are let loose, and they come swarming down from every hill, and the true promise draws near). The "wa" in "wa-iqtaraba" is superfluous, and the verb is the response of the conditional "ḥattā idhā futiḥat." Al-Farra' said in Ma'ani al-Qur'an (folio 306 of the University microfilm no. 24059): "His saying (wa-iqtaraba al-waʿd al-ḥaqq) means, and Allah knows best: until, when they are let loose, it draws near. The entry of the 'wa' into the response after 'ḥattā idhā' is in the position of His saying: 'until, when they came to it and its gates were opened.' In the reading of ʿAbd Allah: 'So when he equipped them with their equipment, and placed the drinking-cup'; and in our reading, without 'wa'. Similar is in the attributes: 'So when they had both submitted, and he had flung him to the forehead, and We called to him,' meaning: 'We called to him.' Imru' al-Qays said: 'So when we crossed... the verse,' meaning: he veered."]]

That is: "When we crossed the courtyard of the tribe, he veered with us."

* *

As for His saying ﴿and behold, the eyes of those who disbelieved will stare fixedly﴾:

Concerning the "hiya" in His saying "fa-idhā hiya" there are two possibilities. The first is that it refers back to the eyes, and that the apparent "al-abṣār" that follows explains it, as the poet said:

"By the life of her father, my wife does not say: 'Get away from me, Malik ibn Abi Ka'b!'"

[[The verse is one of the witnesses of al-Farra' in Ma'ani al-Qur'an (folio 307 of the University microfilm), at His saying, exalted is He: (fa-idhā hiya shākhiṣatun abṣār alladhīna kafarū). He said: "It may be an 'imad (a dummy pronoun) that is suitable in its place, so that it is like His saying 'innahu anā Allāh al-ʿazīz.' Similar is His saying: 'fa-innahā lā taʿmā al-abṣār,' where the feminine comes because al-abṣār is feminine, and the masculine is for the 'imad... And if you wish, make 'hiya' refer to al-abṣār, having referred to it by pronoun, then manifest al-abṣār to explain it, as the poet said: 'By the life of her father... the verse.'" End of quotation.

According to al-Farra's statement, the pronoun in "abīhā" is explained by "ẓaʿīnatī." Similarly, the pronoun "hiya" in the verse "fa-idhā hiya" is explained by "abṣār." Abu al-Baqa' al-ʿUkbari said in I'rab al-Qur'an, and it is like the first of the two possibilities mentioned by al-Farra': "idhā" is for surprise (mufajaʾah), and it is a place-adverb; its governing element is "shākhiṣah." "Hiya" is a pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-qiṣṣah). "Abṣār alladhīna" is the subject (mubtada'), and "shākhiṣah" is its predicate. Al-Shawkani said in Fath al-Qadir (3: 413), presenting both possibilities: The pronoun in "fa-idhā hiya" refers to the matter, or is an ambiguous pronoun explained by what follows; and "idhā" is for surprise.]] He thus referred to the wife by pronoun in "li-ʿamri abīhā," then made her explicit, so the meaning of the speech then is: "then behold, the eyes are staring, the eyes of those who disbelieved."

The second: that it is an 'imad, as His majesty said: ﴿For indeed it is not the eyes that are blinded﴾, and as the poet said:

"Is it then raised up by what is here, a head?"

[[This is a half-line from three verses that appeared in the first volume of this commentary, p. 401, at His saying: "wa-huwa muḥarramun ʿalaykum ikhrājuhum." There it was shown that the pronoun "huwa" has two interpretations, as was said at His saying: "fa-idhā hiya shākhiṣatun abṣār alladhīna kafarū." And like the poet's words: "So inform Abu Yahya, when you meet him, upon the camels, on whose flanks is dried sweat: that the sulami who is in Dariyya, the amir of the protected land, has sold my right, Banu ʿAbs, for a garment, a dinar, a sheep and a dirham. Is then its head raised by what is here, a head?" The verses are among the witnesses of al-Farra' at the verse of al-Baqarah, and only the second half of the third verse is cited here.]]

* *

As for His saying ﴿"Woe to us! We were heedless of this"﴾:

His saying, exalted is His remembrance: "Then the eyes of those who disbelieved have stared fixedly at the coming of the true promise with its terrors and the establishment of the Hour in its realities, and they say: 'Woe to us! We were, before this time in the world, heedless of this which we see and witness, and which has descended upon us of great affliction.'" In the speech there is an omitted element, left unmentioned because of what is indicated by what was mentioned; it is: they say, from His saying "fa-idhā hiya shākhiṣatun abṣār alladhīna kafarū," they say "yā waylanā." As for His saying ﴿"Nay, we were wrongdoers"﴾, it reports the speech of those who disbelieved in Allah on that day: "We did not work for this day in a way that would save us from its severities; rather we were wrongdoers, by disobeying our Lord and obeying Iblis and his hosts in worshipping other than Allah, mighty and majestic is He."

Commentary on the interpretation of His words, Exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, you and what you worship besides Allah are the fuel of Hell; you will be going down into it﴾ [21:98]

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Indeed you, O polytheists who associate others with Allah, who worship besides Him idols and images, and what you worship besides Allah of gods.

As for this, it is related:

* I was told on the authority of al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd informed us, who said: I heard al-Dahhak say, concerning His words ﴿Indeed, you and what you worship besides Allah﴾, that it means the gods and those who worship them; ﴿the fuel of Hell﴾. As for "the fuel of Hell" (haṣab jahannam), some of them said: its meaning is the kindling and the trees of Hell.

Mention of those who said this: I was told by 'Ali, who said: 'Abd Allah related to us, who said: Mu'awiyah related to me, on the authority of 'Ali, on the authority of Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words ﴿the fuel of Hell﴾: the trees of Hell.

* Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, who said: my father related to me, who said: my paternal uncle related to me, who said: my father related to me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words ﴿Indeed, you and what you worship besides Allah, the fuel of Hell﴾, he said: its kindling.

Others said: rather, its meaning is the firewood of Hell.

Mention of those who said this: Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, who said: Abu 'Asim related to us, who said: 'Isa related to us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Najih, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the saying of Allah ﴿the fuel of Hell﴾, he said: its firewood.

* al-Qasim related to us, who said: al-Husayn related to us, who said: Hajjaj related to me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, the same, and he added to it: and in some readings it is ﴿haṭab jahannam﴾ (the firewood of Hell), meaning in the reading of 'A'ishah.

* Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, who said: Muhammad ibn Thawr related to us, on the authority of Ma'mar, on the authority of Qatadah, ﴿the fuel of Hell﴾, he said: the firewood of Hell, into which they will be cast.

* Ibn Bashshar related to us, who said: 'Abd al-Rahman related to us, who said: Sufyan related to us, on the authority of Ibn al-Hurr, on the authority of 'Ikrimah, regarding His words ﴿the fuel of Hell﴾, he said: the firewood of Hell.

Others said: rather, the meaning of that is that they will be thrown into Hell.

Mention of those who said this: I was told on the authority of al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd related to us, who said: I heard al-Dahhak say, concerning His words ﴿the fuel of Hell﴾, he said: Hell is only kindled by them, and haṣb (هو الرمي) means throwing; he says: they will be thrown into it.

The reading of this word differed. The reciters of the major cities read ﴿haṣab jahannam﴾ with the ṣad, and this is the reading we hold, due to the consensus of the authorities upon it.

It is related from 'Ali and 'A'ishah that they used to read it ﴿haṭab jahannam﴾ with the ṭa'.

It is related from Ibn 'Abbas that he read it ﴿haḍab﴾ with the ḍad.

* Ahmad ibn Yusuf related this to us, who said: al-Qasim related to us, who said: Ibrahim ibn Muhammad related to us, on the authority of 'Uthman ibn 'Abd Allah, on the authority of 'Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn 'Abbas, that he read it thus.

If Ibn 'Abbas did read it thus, he meant that they are those by whom Hell is kindled and by whom the fire is set ablaze within it, for everything with which fire is stoked and set alight is, in the Arabic usage, a ḥaḍab (fuel) for it. Since the correct reading, as we have mentioned, is that, and since the known meaning of haṣb in Arabic is throwing, from their saying "ḥaṣabtu al-rajul" (I pelted the man) when I threw at him, as He, may His majesty be exalted, said ﴿Indeed, We sent upon them a hāṣiban (a violent wind bearing pebbles)﴾, the more appropriate interpretation is the view of those who said that its meaning is that Hell will hurl them and they will be thrown into it. It has been mentioned that haṣb in the dialect of the people of Yemen means firewood; if that is so, it is also a sound interpretation. As for what we have said, that its meaning is throwing, that is the usage of the people of Najd. As for His words ﴿you will be going down into it﴾, its meaning is: you, O people, will be upon it or will come down to it, that is, will enter it. The meaning of wurud (coming down/entering) has already been explained earlier, sufficiently so that it need not be repeated here.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 21, verse 99:

The interpretation of His saying, ﴿Had these been gods, they would not have entered it, and all of them will abide therein.﴾

He, may He be exalted, says to these polytheists whose attribute He has described, that no reminder comes to them from their Lord, newly revealed, but they listen to it while they play, namely the polytheists of Quraysh: "You, O polytheists, and what you worship besides God, are fuel for Hell." Had what you worship besides God been gods, they would not have entered it. Rather, they would have prevented whoever wished to bring you into it, since you used to worship them in the world. But since they have no power to benefit themselves and no power to ward off harm from themselves, they are even further from having that power over others. Whoever is like this is clearly excluded from divinity, and the god is the one who has power over whatever He wills, and nothing has power over Him. As for one who is subject to power, it is impermissible for him to be a god.

* *

And His saying, ﴿and all of them will abide therein﴾

means: the gods and those who worshipped them will remain in the Fire forever, without end. The meaning of the statement is: all of you will abide therein.

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said something similar to what we have said about this.

Mention of those who said that: Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying, ﴿Had these been gods, they would not have entered it, and all of them will abide therein﴾: "The gods that the people worshipped." He said: "The worshipper and the worshipped."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 21, verses 100–101:

The interpretation of His saying, ﴿For them therein is a roaring, and they therein will not hear﴾ [21:100] ﴿Indeed, those for whom the best (al-husna) has preceded from Us – those will be kept far from it﴾ [21:101].

He, exalted is He, means by His saying ﴿For them﴾ the polytheists and their gods. The pronoun "them" in His saying ﴿For them﴾ refers back to "all" in His saying ﴿and all therein will abide forever﴾. He, exalted is He, says: For all of them in Hell is a roaring, ﴿and they therein will not hear﴾, meaning: and they, in the Fire, will not hear.

Ibn Mas'ud used to interpret His saying ﴿and they therein will not hear﴾ as follows:

* Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from al-Mas'udi, from Yunus ibn Khabbab, who said: Ibn Mas'ud recited this verse, ﴿For them therein is a roaring, and they therein will not hear﴾, and said: When those who are to abide forever are cast into the Fire, they are placed in coffins of fire; then those coffins are placed inside other coffins, then those coffins inside other coffins, in which there are nails of fire, so that none of them sees that anyone in the Fire is being punished other than himself. Then he recited, ﴿For them therein is a roaring, and they therein will not hear﴾.

As for His saying ﴿Indeed, those for whom the best (al-husna) has preceded from Us – those will be kept far from it﴾, the people of interpretation differed concerning who is meant by it. Some of them said: It means everyone for whom God has preceded happiness among His creatures, that he is kept far from the Fire.

Those who said that:

* Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Abu Bishr, from Yusuf ibn Sa'd (not the son of Mahak), from Muhammad ibn Hatib, who said: I heard Ali giving a sermon, and he recited this verse, ﴿Indeed, those for whom the best has preceded from Us – those will be kept far from it﴾, and said: ʿUthman (may Allah be pleased with him) is among them.

Others said: Rather, it means: whoever was worshipped besides Allah while he was obedient to Allah, and the worship of those who worship him was disliked by him.

Those who said that:

* Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, saying: ʿIsa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all of them, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿those will be kept far from it﴾, he said: ʿIsa, ʿUzayr, and the angels.

* Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, similarly.

Ibn Juraij said: His saying ﴿Indeed you and what you worship besides Allah﴾, then He made an exception, saying ﴿Indeed, those for whom the best has preceded from Us﴾.

* Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Wadih narrated to us, from al-Husayn, from Yazid, from ʿIkrimah, and al-Hasan al-Basri, both said: He said in Surat al-Anbiya': ﴿Indeed you and what you worship besides Allah are the fuel of Hell; you will be its certain arrivals. Had these been gods, they would not have arrived there; and all therein will abide forever. For them therein is a roaring, and they therein will not hear﴾, then He made an exception, saying ﴿Indeed, those for whom the best has preceded from Us – those will be kept far from it﴾. Thus the angels were worshipped besides Allah, and ʿUzayr and ʿIsa were worshipped besides Allah.

* Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Yaman narrated to us, from Ashʿath, from Jaʿfar, from Saʿid, regarding ﴿those will be kept far from it﴾, he said: ʿIsa.

* Ismaʿil ibn Sayf narrated to me, saying: ʿAli ibn Mushir narrated to us, saying: Ismaʿil ibn Abi Khalid narrated to us, from Abu Salih, regarding His saying ﴿Indeed, those for whom the best has preceded from Us﴾, he said: ʿIsa and his mother, ʿUzayr, and the angels.

* Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sat, as has reached me, one day with al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah. Then al-Nadr ibn al-Harith came and sat with them, and in the gathering were more than one of the men of Quraysh. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) spoke, and al-Nadr ibn al-Harith opposed him, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) argued with him until he silenced him. Then he recited to him and to them, ﴿Indeed you and what you worship besides Allah are the fuel of Hell; you will be its certain arrivals. Had these been gods, they would not have arrived there; and all therein will abide forever﴾ . . . up to His saying ﴿and they therein will not hear﴾. Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) stood up, and ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Zaba'ra ibn Qays ibn ʿAdi al-Sahmi came and sat down. Al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah said to ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Zaba'ra: By Allah, al-Nadr ibn al-Harith did not stand up for the son of ʿAbd al-Muttalib just now, nor did he sit, and he claimed that we and what we worship of our gods are the fuel of Hell. ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Zaba'ra said: By Allah, if I had found him, I would have defeated him. Ask Muhammad: Is everyone who is worshipped besides Allah in Hell along with those who worshipped him? We worship the angels, the Jews worship ʿUzayr, and the Christians worship the Messiah ʿIsa son of Maryam. Al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah and those in the gathering were amazed at the words of ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Zaba'ra, and they saw that he had argued and disputed. This was mentioned to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), the words of Ibn al-Zaba'ra, and he said: "Yes, everyone who wishes to be worshipped besides Allah is with those who worship him; they only worship the devils and those who command them to be worshipped." So Allah revealed to him ﴿Indeed, those for whom the best has preceded from Us – those will be kept far from it﴾ . . . to ﴿abide forever﴾. That is: ʿIsa son of Maryam, ʿUzayr, and those among the rabbis and monks who were worshipped, who died in obedience to Allah, and those who came after them of the people of misguidance took them as lords besides Allah. Allah then revealed concerning what they claimed, that they worship the angels and that they are daughters of Allah: ﴿And they say, "The Most Merciful has taken a son." Glory be to Him! Rather, they are honored servants﴾ . . . to His saying ﴿We recompense the wrongdoers﴾.

* I was told on the authority of al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Muʿadh say: ʿUbayd informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say: Some people say, ﴿Indeed, those for whom the best has preceded from Us – those will be kept far from it﴾, meaning from all of mankind. That is not so; rather it means those who were worshipped as gods while being obedient to Allah, such as ʿIsa and his mother, ʿUzayr, and the angels. Allah made an exception for these worshipped gods, while those who worship them are in the Fire.

* Ibn Sinan al-Qazzaz narrated to us, saying: al-Hasan ibn al-Husayn al-Ashqar narrated to us, saying: Abu Kudaynah narrated to us, from ʿAta' ibn al-Sa'ib, from Saʿid ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: When there was revealed ﴿Indeed you and what you worship besides Allah are the fuel of Hell; you will be its certain arrivals﴾, the polytheists said: Then ʿIsa is worshipped, and ʿUzayr, and the sun and the moon are worshipped. So Allah revealed ﴿Indeed, those for whom the best has preceded from Us – those will be kept far from it﴾, concerning ʿIsa and others.

The most correct of the opinions in the interpretation of this is the view of the one who said: What is meant by His saying ﴿Indeed, those for whom the best has preceded from Us – those will be kept far from it﴾ is whatever was worshipped, which the polytheists worshipped, while the one worshipped was obedient to Allah, and those who worship it by their worship of it are disbelievers. This is because His saying, exalted is He, ﴿Indeed, those for whom the best has preceded from Us﴾ is an initial statement confirming a matter that a people denied, in the manner we mentioned in the report from Ibn ʿAbbas. It is as if the polytheists said to the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ), when he said to them ﴿Indeed you and what you worship besides Allah are the fuel of Hell﴾: The matter is not as you say, for we worship the angels, and others worship the Messiah and ʿUzayr. So He, mighty and majestic, responded to their statement: Rather, it is so, and those for whom the best has preceded from Us are not those kept far from it, because they are not included in our saying ﴿Indeed you and what you worship besides Allah are the fuel of Hell﴾. As for the statement of those who said that as an exception from ﴿Indeed you and what you worship besides Allah are the fuel of Hell﴾, it is a statement without meaning, because an exception is only the removal of the excepted from that from which it is excepted. There is no doubt that those for whom the best has preceded from Us are either angels, or humans, or jinn, and when the Arabs mention all of these, they mostly mention them with "man" (من), not "what" (ما). Allah, exalted is He, mentioned the worshipped ones, of whom He informed that they are the fuel of Hell, with "what" (ما), saying ﴿Indeed you and what you worship besides Allah are the fuel of Hell﴾; it is intended by it what they worshipped of idols and gods made of stone and wood, not those among the angels and humans. If that is so, as we have described, then His saying ﴿Indeed, those for whom the best has preceded from Us﴾ is an answer from Allah to the polytheists who made the statement we mentioned, as a new beginning. As for "the best" (al-husna), it is the superlative form of "good" (al-husn), and what is meant by it is the happiness that Allah has preceded for them.

As:

* Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿Indeed, those for whom the best has preceded from Us﴾: "The best" is happiness; happiness preceded for its people from Allah, and wretchedness preceded for its people from Allah.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 21, verses 100–101:

The interpretation of His saying, ﴿For them therein is a roaring, and they therein will not hear﴾ [21:100] ﴿Indeed, those for whom the best (al-husna) has preceded from Us – those will be kept far from it﴾ [21:101].

He, exalted is He, means by His saying ﴿For them﴾ the polytheists and their gods. The pronoun "them" in His saying ﴿For them﴾ refers back to "all" in His saying ﴿and all therein will abide forever﴾. He, exalted is He, says: For all of them in Hell is a roaring, ﴿and they therein will not hear﴾, meaning: and they, in the Fire, will not hear.

Ibn Mas'ud used to interpret His saying ﴿and they therein will not hear﴾ as follows:

* Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from al-Mas'udi, from Yunus ibn Khabbab, who said: Ibn Mas'ud recited this verse, ﴿For them therein is a roaring, and they therein will not hear﴾, and said: When those who are to abide forever are cast into the Fire, they are placed in coffins of fire; then those coffins are placed inside other coffins, then those coffins inside other coffins, in which there are nails of fire, so that none of them sees that anyone in the Fire is being punished other than himself. Then he recited, ﴿For them therein is a roaring, and they therein will not hear﴾.

As for His saying ﴿Indeed, those for whom the best (al-husna) has preceded from Us – those will be kept far from it﴾, the people of interpretation differed concerning who is meant by it. Some of them said: It means everyone for whom God has preceded happiness among His creatures, that he is kept far from the Fire.

Those who said that:

* Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Abu Bishr, from Yusuf ibn Sa'd (not the son of Mahak), from Muhammad ibn Hatib, who said: I heard Ali giving a sermon, and he recited this verse, ﴿Indeed, those for whom the best has preceded from Us – those will be kept far from it﴾, and said: ʿUthman (may Allah be pleased with him) is among them.

Others said: Rather, it means: whoever was worshipped besides Allah while he was obedient to Allah, and the worship of those who worship him was disliked by him.

Those who said that:

* Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, saying: ʿIsa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all of them, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿those will be kept far from it﴾, he said: ʿIsa, ʿUzayr, and the angels.

* Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, similarly.

Ibn Juraij said: His saying ﴿Indeed you and what you worship besides Allah﴾, then He made an exception, saying ﴿Indeed, those for whom the best has preceded from Us﴾.

* Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Wadih narrated to us, from al-Husayn, from Yazid, from ʿIkrimah, and al-Hasan al-Basri, both said: He said in Surat al-Anbiya': ﴿Indeed you and what you worship besides Allah are the fuel of Hell; you will be its certain arrivals. Had these been gods, they would not have arrived there; and all therein will abide forever. For them therein is a roaring, and they therein will not hear﴾, then He made an exception, saying ﴿Indeed, those for whom the best has preceded from Us – those will be kept far from it﴾. Thus the angels were worshipped besides Allah, and ʿUzayr and ʿIsa were worshipped besides Allah.

* Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Yaman narrated to us, from Ashʿath, from Jaʿfar, from Saʿid, regarding ﴿those will be kept far from it﴾, he said: ʿIsa.

* Ismaʿil ibn Sayf narrated to me, saying: ʿAli ibn Mushir narrated to us, saying: Ismaʿil ibn Abi Khalid narrated to us, from Abu Salih, regarding His saying ﴿Indeed, those for whom the best has preceded from Us﴾, he said: ʿIsa and his mother, ʿUzayr, and the angels.

* Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sat, as has reached me, one day with al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah. Then al-Nadr ibn al-Harith came and sat with them, and in the gathering were more than one of the men of Quraysh. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) spoke, and al-Nadr ibn al-Harith opposed him, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) argued with him until he silenced him. Then he recited to him and to them, ﴿Indeed you and what you worship besides Allah are the fuel of Hell; you will be its certain arrivals. Had these been gods, they would not have arrived there; and all therein will abide forever﴾ . . . up to His saying ﴿and they therein will not hear﴾. Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) stood up, and ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Zaba'ra ibn Qays ibn ʿAdi al-Sahmi came and sat down. Al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah said to ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Zaba'ra: By Allah, al-Nadr ibn al-Harith did not stand up for the son of ʿAbd al-Muttalib just now, nor did he sit, and he claimed that we and what we worship of our gods are the fuel of Hell. ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Zaba'ra said: By Allah, if I had found him, I would have defeated him. Ask Muhammad: Is everyone who is worshipped besides Allah in Hell along with those who worshipped him? We worship the angels, the Jews worship ʿUzayr, and the Christians worship the Messiah ʿIsa son of Maryam. Al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah and those in the gathering were amazed at the words of ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Zaba'ra, and they saw that he had argued and disputed. This was mentioned to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), the words of Ibn al-Zaba'ra, and he said: "Yes, everyone who wishes to be worshipped besides Allah is with those who worship him; they only worship the devils and those who command them to be worshipped." So Allah revealed to him ﴿Indeed, those for whom the best has preceded from Us – those will be kept far from it﴾ . . . to ﴿abide forever﴾. That is: ʿIsa son of Maryam, ʿUzayr, and those among the rabbis and monks who were worshipped, who died in obedience to Allah, and those who came after them of the people of misguidance took them as lords besides Allah. Allah then revealed concerning what they claimed, that they worship the angels and that they are daughters of Allah: ﴿And they say, "The Most Merciful has taken a son." Glory be to Him! Rather, they are honored servants﴾ . . . to His saying ﴿We recompense the wrongdoers﴾.

* I was told on the authority of al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Muʿadh say: ʿUbayd informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say: Some people say, ﴿Indeed, those for whom the best has preceded from Us – those will be kept far from it﴾, meaning from all of mankind. That is not so; rather it means those who were worshipped as gods while being obedient to Allah, such as ʿIsa and his mother, ʿUzayr, and the angels. Allah made an exception for these worshipped gods, while those who worship them are in the Fire.

* Ibn Sinan al-Qazzaz narrated to us, saying: al-Hasan ibn al-Husayn al-Ashqar narrated to us, saying: Abu Kudaynah narrated to us, from ʿAta' ibn al-Sa'ib, from Saʿid ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: When there was revealed ﴿Indeed you and what you worship besides Allah are the fuel of Hell; you will be its certain arrivals﴾, the polytheists said: Then ʿIsa is worshipped, and ʿUzayr, and the sun and the moon are worshipped. So Allah revealed ﴿Indeed, those for whom the best has preceded from Us – those will be kept far from it﴾, concerning ʿIsa and others.

The most correct of the opinions in the interpretation of this is the view of the one who said: What is meant by His saying ﴿Indeed, those for whom the best has preceded from Us – those will be kept far from it﴾ is whatever was worshipped, which the polytheists worshipped, while the one worshipped was obedient to Allah, and those who worship it by their worship of it are disbelievers. This is because His saying, exalted is He, ﴿Indeed, those for whom the best has preceded from Us﴾ is an initial statement confirming a matter that a people denied, in the manner we mentioned in the report from Ibn ʿAbbas. It is as if the polytheists said to the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ), when he said to them ﴿Indeed you and what you worship besides Allah are the fuel of Hell﴾: The matter is not as you say, for we worship the angels, and others worship the Messiah and ʿUzayr. So He, mighty and majestic, responded to their statement: Rather, it is so, and those for whom the best has preceded from Us are not those kept far from it, because they are not included in our saying ﴿Indeed you and what you worship besides Allah are the fuel of Hell﴾. As for the statement of those who said that as an exception from ﴿Indeed you and what you worship besides Allah are the fuel of Hell﴾, it is a statement without meaning, because an exception is only the removal of the excepted from that from which it is excepted. There is no doubt that those for whom the best has preceded from Us are either angels, or humans, or jinn, and when the Arabs mention all of these, they mostly mention them with "man" (من), not "what" (ما). Allah, exalted is He, mentioned the worshipped ones, of whom He informed that they are the fuel of Hell, with "what" (ما), saying ﴿Indeed you and what you worship besides Allah are the fuel of Hell﴾; it is intended by it what they worshipped of idols and gods made of stone and wood, not those among the angels and humans. If that is so, as we have described, then His saying ﴿Indeed, those for whom the best has preceded from Us﴾ is an answer from Allah to the polytheists who made the statement we mentioned, as a new beginning. As for "the best" (al-husna), it is the superlative form of "good" (al-husn), and what is meant by it is the happiness that Allah has preceded for them.

As:

* Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿Indeed, those for whom the best has preceded from Us﴾: "The best" is happiness; happiness preceded for its people from Allah, and wretchedness preceded for its people from Allah.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 21, verses 102–103:

The interpretation of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿They will not hear the slightest sound of it, and they will abide forever in that which their souls desire﴾ (21:102)

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: those for whom the best reward has preceded from Us will not hear the faintest sound (ḥasīs) of the Fire. By ḥasīs He means the sound and the stir.

If someone says: how can they not hear its sound, when you know what has been reported, that Hell will be brought forth on the Day of Resurrection and will let out a roar such that no angel brought near and no prophet sent will remain except that he falls to his knees out of fear of it? It is said: the state in which they do not hear its sound is not that state; rather it is the state which Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my paternal uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿They will not hear the slightest sound of it, and they will abide forever in that which their souls desire﴾: he said: the people of Paradise will not hear the sound of the Fire when they have descended to their station in Paradise.

* *

And His saying ﴿and they will abide forever in that which their souls desire﴾

He says: they will remain in what their souls desire of its bounties and pleasures, not fearing any removal from it or any transfer away from it.

* *

The interpretation of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿The great terror will not grieve them, and the angels will receive them, saying: This is your day which you were promised﴾ (21:103)

The interpreters differed regarding "the great terror": which terror is it? Some of them said: it is the Fire when it closes over its people.

Those who said this: Abu Hisham related to us, saying: Yahya ibn Yaman related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, from 'Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, regarding ﴿The great terror will not grieve them﴾: he said: the Fire when it closes over its people.

Al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, saying: Ibn Jurayj said, regarding His saying ﴿The great terror will not grieve them﴾: he said: when it (Hell) closes over, and he said: when death is slaughtered.

Others said: rather, it is the Last Trumpet blast.

Those who said this: Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my paternal uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿The great terror will not grieve them﴾: he means the Last Trumpet blast.

Others said: rather, it is when the servant is commanded to be taken to the Fire.

Those who said this: Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Hakkam related to us, from 'Anbasa, from a man, from al-Hasan, regarding ﴿The great terror will not grieve them﴾: he said: the departure of the servant when he is commanded to go to the Fire.

The most correct of these opinions, in our view, is the saying of the one who said: it is at the Last Trumpet blast. This is because whoever is not grieved by that great terror and is secure from it, is more deserving that he will not be frightened by what follows it; and whoever is frightened by that, the fear of what follows it is not ruled out for him.

* *

And His saying ﴿and the angels will receive them﴾

He says: the angels will meet them, congratulating them, saying ﴿This is your day which you were promised﴾, wherein is honor from God, gift and abundant reward for what you toiled for in the world in obedience to God.

Ibn Zayd said something similar to what we have said regarding this.

Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿This is your day which you were promised﴾: he said: this is before they enter Paradise.
