The commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 21, verse 104:

On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿On the Day We roll up the heaven like the rolling of a scroll for writings. As We originated the first creation, We will repeat it, a promise binding upon Us. Indeed, We are ever doing [it]﴾ (21:104).

His words, exalted is His remembrance: "The greatest terror will not grieve them, on the Day We roll up the heavens." Here "the Day" is connected to the subject of "those whom it grieves."

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) differed concerning the meaning of "al-sijill" (the scroll) mentioned by God in this passage. Some of them said: it is the name of an angel among the angels.

Those who said this include: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Yamān narrated to us, saying: Abu al-Wafa' al-Ash'ari narrated to us, from his father, from Ibn 'Umar, concerning His words ﴿On the Day We roll up the heaven like the rolling of a scroll for writings﴾, he said: "The sijill is an angel; when he ascends with the seeking of forgiveness, he says: 'Write it as light.'"

Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Mu'ammal narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, saying: he heard al-Suddi say, concerning His words ﴿On the Day We roll up the heaven like the rolling of a scroll﴾: "The sijill: an angel."

Others said: the sijill is a man who used to write for the Messenger of God (ﷺ).

Those who said this include: Nasr ibn 'Ali narrated to us, saying: Nuh ibn Qays narrated to us, saying: 'Amr ibn Malik narrated to us, from Abu al-Jawza', from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning this verse ﴿On the Day We roll up the heaven like the rolling of a scroll for writings﴾, he said: Ibn 'Abbas used to say: "It is the man."

He said: Nuh ibn Qays narrated to us, saying: Yazid ibn Ka'b narrated to us, from 'Amr ibn Malik, from Abu al-Jawza', from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "The sijill: a scribe who used to write for the Messenger of God (ﷺ)."

Others said: rather, it is the sheet in which one writes.

Those who said this include: 'Ali narrated to me, saying: 'Abd Allah narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His words ﴿like the rolling of a scroll for writings﴾, he said: "Like the folding of the sheet over the writing."

Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to us, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His words ﴿On the Day We roll up the heaven like the rolling of a scroll for writings﴾, he said: "Like the folding of the pages."

Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all of them, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, who said: "The sijill: the sheet."

al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij, from Mujahid, concerning His words ﴿On the Day We roll up the heaven like the rolling of a scroll for writings﴾, he said: "The sijill: the sheet."

The most correct of these sayings, in our view, is the saying of the one who said: the sijill in this place is the sheet, because that is the known meaning in the speech of the Arabs; and no scribe of our Prophet (ﷺ) is known whose name was al-Sijill, nor is there an angel among the angels bearing that name.

If someone says: "How can the sheet be rolled up with the writing, if the sijill is a sheet?" It is said: the meaning is not so. Rather, its meaning is: "On the Day We roll up the heaven like the rolling of the scroll over what is in it of writing." Then the verbal noun (masdar) was used for "natwi" (We roll up), so it was said ﴿like the rolling of the scroll for writings﴾. The lam in His words "for writings" is in the sense of "over" (ʿalā).

The readers (al-qurra') differed in their recitation of this. The majority of the readers of the regional centres (al-amsar) recited ﴿On the Day We roll up the heaven﴾ with the nun, except Abu Ja'far the reader, who recited ﴿On the Day the heaven is rolled up﴾ with the ta' and with a damma, in the form where the agent is not named (al-fi'l ma lam yusamma fa'iluh).

The correct recitation in this is what the readers of the regional centres have, with the nun, because of the consensus of the authoritative readers upon it and the anomaly of what opposes it. As for "al-sijill," in the recitation of all of them it has the lam doubled (tashdid). As for "al-kitab" (the writing), the readers of Medina and some of the people of Kufa and Basra recited it in the singular: "like the rolling of the scroll for the writing." And the majority of the readers of Kufa recited "li-l-kutub" (for the writings) in the plural.

The more correct of the two readings in our view is the reading of the one who recited it in the singular, "li-l-kitab," for what we have mentioned of its meaning, since its intended meaning is: "like the rolling of the scroll over what is written in it." So, since that is its meaning for all the writings, there is no way except a way we follow from the known speech of the Arabs. At His words ﴿like the rolling of the scroll﴾ the statement about the connection of His words ﴿The greatest terror will not grieve them﴾ ends. Then He began a statement about what God will do with His creation on that day, so He, exalted is His remembrance, said: ﴿As We originated the first creation, We will repeat it﴾.

The kaf in His words ﴿kama﴾ ("as") is connected to "nu'idu" (We will repeat), which came before it. The meaning of the speech is: "We will repeat the creation barefoot, naked, and uncircumcised (ghurlan) on the Day of Resurrection, as We originated them the first time, in the state in which We created them in their mothers' wombs," with a difference among the people of interpretation concerning the explanation of this.

It is by what we have said in this that a group of the people of interpretation spoke, and there is a report from the Messenger of God (ﷺ) concerning it, so for that reason I chose to hold it over others.

Those who said this and the report that came concerning it: Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us, and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all of them, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning ﴿the first creation, We will repeat it﴾, he said: "Barefoot, naked, uncircumcised (ghurlan)."

al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij, from Mujahid, concerning His words ﴿the first creation, We will repeat it﴾, he said: "Barefoot, uncircumcised (ghulfan)." Ibn Juraij said: Ibrahim ibn Maysara informed me that he heard Mujahid say: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said to one of his wives: "They will come to Him barefoot, naked, uncircumcised." So she drew her shirt-sleeve over herself and said: "Alas, my shame!" Ibn Juraij said: I was informed that she was 'A'isha, who said: "O Prophet of God, do people not feel shy of one another?" He said: "For every person on that Day there is a matter that occupies him."

Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Sa'id narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, saying: al-Mughira ibn al-Nu'man narrated to me, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "People will be gathered barefoot, naked, uncircumcised (ghurlan). The first to be clothed will be Ibrahim." Then he recited ﴿As We originated the first creation, We will repeat it, a promise binding upon Us. Indeed, We are ever doing [it]﴾.

Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Ishaq ibn Yusuf narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from al-Mughira ibn al-Nu'man, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "The Messenger of God (ﷺ) stood among us to give an admonition, and he mentioned it in a similar manner."

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, saying: Shu'ba narrated to us, from al-Mughira ibn al-Nu'man al-Nakha'i, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "The Messenger of God (ﷺ) stood among us, and he mentioned it in a similar manner."

Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, from Shu'ba, who said: al-Mughira ibn al-Nu'man al-Nakha'i narrated to us, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, in a similar manner.

'Isa ibn Yusuf ibn al-Tabba' Abu Yahya narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from 'Amr ibn Dinar, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "I heard the Prophet (ﷺ) delivering a sermon, and he said: 'Verily you will meet God barefoot and uncircumcised (ghurlan).'"

Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Idris narrated to us, from Layth, from Mujahid, from 'A'isha, who said: "The Messenger of God (ﷺ) entered upon me while with me was an old woman from the Banu 'Amir. He said: 'Who is this old woman, O 'A'isha?' I said: 'One of my maternal aunts.' She said: 'Ask God to make me enter Paradise.' He said: 'Indeed, Paradise will not be entered by the infirm (al-'ajazah).' She was seized by what seized her. He said: 'Indeed God will bring them into being as a creation other than their creation.' Then he said: 'They will be gathered barefoot, naked, uncircumcised (ghulfan).' She said: 'Far be it from God!' The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: 'Yes indeed, God said: ﴿As We originated the first creation, We will repeat it, a promise binding upon Us﴾ ... to the end of the verse. The first to be clothed will be Ibrahim, the friend of God.'"

Muhammad ibn 'Umara al-Asadi narrated to me, saying: 'Ubayd Allah narrated to us, saying: Isra'il narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from 'Ata', from 'Uqba ibn 'Amir al-Juhani, who said: "People will be gathered in one plain, the sight will penetrate them, and the caller will make them hear, barefoot and naked, as they were created on the first day."

al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: 'Abbad ibn al-'Awwam narrated to me, from Hilal ibn Hibban, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, from the Messenger of God (ﷺ), who said: "People will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection barefoot, naked, walking, uncircumcised (ghurlan). I said: 'O Abu 'Abd Allah, what is al-ghurl?' He said: 'The uncircumcised (al-ghulf).' One of his wives said: 'O Messenger of God, will some of us look at others at their private parts?' He said: 'For every person on that Day there is what will occupy him from looking at the nakedness of his brother.'" Hilal said: Sa'id ibn Jubayr said concerning ﴿And you have come to Us alone, as We created you the first time﴾: "As on the day his mother bore him. Everything that was diminished from him will be returned to him, like the day he was born."

Others said: rather, the meaning of that is: "As We were, and there was nothing other than Us before We created anything, so likewise We will destroy things and then repeat them perishing, until there is nothing but Us."

Those who said this include: Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning ﴿As We originated the first creation, We will repeat it﴾ ... the verse, he said: "We will destroy every thing as it was the first time."

* *

As for His words ﴿a promise binding upon Us﴾:

He says: We have promised you that as a binding promise upon Us, that We will fulfil what We promised, "Indeed, We are ever doing what We promised you of that, O people," because it has already preceded in Our judgment and decree that We will do it, with certainty that it will happen. So prepare yourselves and get ready.

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We had written in the Psalms, after the Reminder, that the earth shall be inherited by My righteous servants﴾

The scholars of ta'wil (interpretation) differed about what is meant by the Zabur (Psalms) and the Dhikr (Reminder) in this place. Some of them said: By the Zabur is meant all the scriptures of the prophets that God sent down to them, and by the Dhikr is meant the Umm al-Kitab (Mother of the Book) which is with Him in heaven.

Mention of those who said this: Isa ibn Uthman ibn Isa al-Ramli narrated to me, saying: Yahya ibn Isa narrated to us, from al-A'mash, who said: I asked Sa'id about the words of God, ﴿And We had written in the Psalms after the Reminder﴾, and he said: The Dhikr is that which is in heaven.

* al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Isa ibn Yunus narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, concerning His words ﴿And We had written in the Psalms﴾. He said: al-A'mash recited it as ﴿al-Zubur﴾ (the plural). He said: The Zabur, the Torah, the Gospel and the Qur'an. ﴿After the Reminder﴾: He said: The Reminder that is in heaven.

* Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa narrated to us, all together, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿al-Zabur﴾, he said: The Book. ﴿After the Reminder﴾, he said: The Mother of the Book with God.

al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿al-Zabur﴾, he said: The Book. ﴿After the Reminder﴾, he said: The Mother of the Book with God.

* Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His words ﴿And We had written in the Psalms﴾: The Zabur is the books that were sent down upon the prophets, and the Dhikr is the Umm al-Kitab, in which things are written before that.

* Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Mansur, from Sa'id, concerning His words ﴿And We had written in the Psalms after the Reminder﴾, he said: We wrote in the Qur'an after the Torah.

Others said: Rather, by the Zabur is meant the books that God sent down to those prophets who came after Musa (Moses), and by the Dhikr is meant the Torah.

Mention of those who said this: Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, concerning His words ﴿And We had written in the Psalms after the Reminder﴾ ... the verse, he said: The Dhikr is the Torah, and the Zabur is the books.

* al-Husayn narrated to us, from him, saying: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say, concerning His words ﴿And We had written in the Psalms after the Reminder﴾ ... the verse, he said: The Dhikr is the Torah, and by the Zabur after the Torah is meant the books.

Others said: Rather, by the Zabur is meant the Zabur of Dawud (David), and by the Dhikr is meant the Torah of Musa, may God's blessings be upon them both.

Mention of those who said this: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Wahhab narrated to us, saying: Dawud narrated to us, from Amir, that he said concerning this verse ﴿And We had written in the Psalms after the Reminder﴾: The Zabur of Dawud; after the Reminder is the Reminder of Musa, the Torah.

* Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi Adi narrated to us, from Dawud, from al-Sha'bi, that he said concerning this verse ﴿And We had written in the Psalms after the Reminder﴾: In the Zabur of Dawud, after the Reminder of Musa.

The most correct of these sayings in my view, regarding this matter, is what Sa'id ibn Jubayr and Mujahid said, and whoever speaks in agreement with them, that its meaning is: And We had written in the books, after the Umm al-Kitab in which God wrote everything that exists before the creation of the heavens and the earth. This is because the Zabur is the Book; it is said from this: "zabartu al-kitab" (I wrote the book) when I write it; and every book that God sent down to one of His prophets is a Dhikr. Since this is so, the use of the definite article with "al-Dhikr" is clear evidence that it refers to a specific, known Reminder, known to those addressed by the verse. Had it been other than the Umm al-Kitab that we mentioned, the Torah would not be more deserving than the scrolls of Ibrahim (Abraham) to be the one meant by it, since the Zabur of Dawud came after them.

The interpretation of the statement therefore, given that it is as we have described: And We have decreed, and We have confirmed Our decree in the books after the Umm al-Kitab, that the earth shall be inherited by My righteous servants. What is meant is: the land of Paradise shall be inherited by My servants who act in obedience to Him and who abide by His commands and prohibitions, not those among them who act in disobedience and prefer the obedience of Satan to His obedience.

Mention of those who said this: Muhammad ibn Abd Allah al-Hilali narrated to us, saying: Ubayd Allah ibn Musa narrated to us, saying: Israil narrated to us, from Abu Yahya al-Qattat, from Mujahid, from Ibn Abbas, concerning His words ﴿that the earth shall be inherited by My righteous servants﴾, he said: The land of Paradise.

* Ali narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, concerning His words ﴿And We had written in the Psalms after the Reminder that the earth shall be inherited by My righteous servants﴾, he said: He, glory be to Him, informed in the Torah, the Zabur, and His prior knowledge before the heavens and the earth existed, that He would make the community of Muhammad (ﷺ) inherit the earth and admit them to Paradise, and they are the righteous.

* Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Mansur, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, concerning ﴿And We had written in the Psalms after the Reminder that the earth shall be inherited by My righteous servants﴾, he said: We wrote in the Qur'an after the Torah, and the earth is the land of Paradise.

* Ali ibn Sahl narrated to me, saying: Hajjaj narrated to us, from Abu Ja'far, from al-Rabi' ibn Anas, from Abu al-Aliya, ﴿that the earth shall be inherited by My righteous servants﴾, he said: The earth is Paradise.

* Isa ibn Uthman ibn Isa al-Ramli narrated to me, saying: Yahya ibn Isa narrated to us, from al-A'mash, who said: I asked Sa'id about the words of God ﴿that the earth shall be inherited by My righteous servants﴾, and he said: The land of Paradise.

* Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa narrated to us, all together, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning the words of God ﴿that the earth﴾, he said: Paradise; ﴿shall be inherited by My righteous servants﴾.

* al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, the same.

* Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His words ﴿that the earth shall be inherited by My righteous servants﴾, he said: Paradise. And he recited the saying of God, mighty is His praise: ﴿And they will say, "Praise be to God who has fulfilled His promise to us and made us inherit the earth, that we may dwell in Paradise wherever we will. How excellent is the reward of the workers."﴾ He said: The beginning of Paradise is in the earth, then its degrees go upward, and the beginning of Hell is in the earth, and between them is a barrier, a wall, and no one knows what that wall is. He recited ﴿A gate whose inner part holds mercy, and whose outer part is toward the torment﴾. He said: And its stairway goes downward in the earth, while the stairways of Paradise go upward in the heavens.

* Muhammad ibn Awf narrated to us, saying: Abu al-Mughira narrated to us, saying: Safwan narrated to us: I asked Amir ibn Abd Allah Abu al-Yaman: Is there a gathering place for the souls of the believers? He said: Indeed, the earth which God speaks of, ﴿And We had written in the Psalms after the Reminder that the earth shall be inherited by My righteous servants﴾, is the earth to which the spirits of the believers gather until the Resurrection.

Others said: It is the earth which God will give the believers to inherit in this world.

Others said: What is meant by this is the Children of Israel, because God promised them this and fulfilled it for them.

They cited for their saying the words of God: ﴿And We made the people who had been oppressed inherit the eastern and western parts of the earth, which We had blessed﴾. We have already mentioned the view of those who said that ﴿that the earth shall be inherited by My righteous servants﴾ refers to the land of the disbelieving nations, which the community of Muhammad (ﷺ) will inherit, and this is the saying of Ibn Abbas which Ali ibn Abi Talha reported from him.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 21, verse 106–107:

The interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, in this is a message for a people who worship [Allah]﴾ [106] ﴿And We have not sent you, [O Muhammad], except as a mercy to the worlds﴾ [107].

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: Indeed, in this Qur'an which We sent down to Our Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) is a message (balagh) for whoever worships Allah, by means of what it contains of the obligations (fara'id) which Allah has imposed, leading to His good pleasure, and attaining what is sought with Him. And in accordance with what we have said on this, the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have spoken.

Mention of those who said this: Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim related to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah related to us, from al-Jurayri, from Abu al-Ward ibn Thumamah, from Abu Muhammad al-Hadrami, who said: Ka'b related to us in this mosque, saying: By Him in whose hand is Ka'b's soul, indeed in this is a message for a people who worship; they are the people of, or the companions of, the five prayers; Allah named them "worshippers."

⁕ al-Husayn ibn Yazid al-Tahhan related to us, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah related to us, from Sa'id ibn Iyas al-Jurayri, from Abu al-Ward, from Ka'b, regarding His words ﴿Indeed, in this is a message for a people who worship﴾, he said: The fasting of the month of Ramadan and the five prayers. He said: It is a handful of the hands and the sea of worship.

⁕ al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn related to us, from al-Jurayri, who said: Ka'b al-Ahbar said ﴿Indeed, in this is a message for a people who worship﴾: [it is] for the community of Muhammad.

⁕ 'Ali related to me, saying: 'Abd Allah related to us, saying: Mu'awiyah related to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words ﴿Indeed, in this is a message for a people who worship﴾, he said: means "working" (ʿamilin).

⁕ al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Juraij, regarding His words ﴿Indeed, in this is a message for a people who worship﴾, he said: They say in this surah "balaghan" (a message).

Others say: In the Qur'an is a revelation of the obligations of the five daily prayers; whoever performs them, it is a message for a people who worship, meaning "working" (ʿamilin).

⁕ Yunus related to us, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words ﴿Indeed, in this is a message for a people who worship﴾: Indeed, in this is benefit and knowledge for a people who worship; that is the message.

* *

As for His words ﴿And We have not sent you except as a mercy to the worlds﴾:

He, exalted is His remembrance, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): And We have not sent you, O Muhammad, to Our creation except as a mercy to those among My creation to whom We sent you.

Then the people of interpretation differed concerning the meaning of this verse: Is it intended to encompass all the world to whom Muhammad was sent, both their believers and their disbelievers? Or is it intended only for the people of faith, to the exclusion of the people of disbelief? Some of them said: It refers to all the world, believers and disbelievers alike.

Mention of those who said this: Ishaq ibn Shahin related to me, saying: Ishaq ibn Yusuf al-Azraq related to us, from al-Mas'udi, from a man called Sa'id, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding the words of Allah in His Book ﴿And We have not sent you except as a mercy to the worlds﴾, he said: Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, mercy is written for him in this world and the Hereafter; and whoever does not believe in Allah and His Messenger is spared what befell the nations of punishment by sinking and by stones.

⁕ al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: 'Isa ibn Yunus related to us, from al-Mas'udi, from Abu Sa'id, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words ﴿And We have not sent you except as a mercy to the worlds﴾, he said: The mercy is complete for whoever believes in him, in this world and the Hereafter; and whoever does not believe in him is spared what befell the nations before.

Others said: Rather, it is intended only for the people of faith, to the exclusion of the people of disbelief.

Mention of those who said this: Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words ﴿And We have not sent you except as a mercy to the worlds﴾: "The worlds" are those who believed in him and affirmed him. He said ﴿And I do not know, perhaps it is a trial for you and enjoyment for a time﴾. He said: It is a trial for those and a mercy for these. The matter has come in general terms, "a mercy to the worlds," and "the worlds" here means those who believed in him, affirmed him, and obeyed him.

The more correct of the two opinions on this matter is the view related from Ibn 'Abbas: that Allah sent His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) as a mercy to the entire world, both its believers and its disbelievers. As for the believers, Allah guided them through him and admitted them into Paradise by their faith in him and their acting upon what came from Allah. As for the disbelievers, He averted from them through him the immediate punishment that would have descended upon the nations that denied their messengers before him.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 21, verse 108:

The exposition of His words, exalted is He: ﴿Say: "It is only revealed to me that your God is one God. Will you then submit?"﴾

He, exalted is His mention, says to His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ: Say, O Muhammad: "What is revealed to me by my Lord is only that there is no god for you that may be worshipped except one God; worship is fitting for none but Him, and it is not proper for it to be directed to anyone else."

He says: "Will you then submit to Him, O polytheists who worship idols and images, bowing humbly to that, and disavowing the worship of whatever else you take as gods?"

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 21, verse 109–111:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So if they turn away, say, "I have informed you equally, and I do not know whether what you are promised is near or far."﴾ (109)

His saying, exalted is He, means: If these polytheists, O Muhammad, turn their backs on acknowledging faith, that there is no god for them except one God, and they turn away from it and refuse to respond to it, then say to them: ﴿I have informed you equally﴾, meaning: inform them that you and they are on equal knowledge that some of you are at war with others, with no truce or peace between you.

What is meant by this is the people of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ from Quraysh.

As related:

* Al-Qasim told us, he said: al-Husayn told us, he said: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, regarding His saying, ﴿So if they turn away, say, "I have informed you equally"﴾: "So if they turn away" means Quraysh.

* * *

And His saying, ﴿and I do not know whether what you are promised is near or far﴾.

His saying, exalted is He, to His Prophet means: Say, "I do not know when the time will come upon you of the punishment of Allah which He has promised you, whereby He will take vengeance on you from you, whether its descent upon you is near or far."

The people of interpretation have said similarly to what we have said regarding this.

Mention of those who said that: Al-Qasim told us, he said: al-Husayn told us, he said: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, regarding ﴿and I do not know whether what you are promised is near or far﴾, he said: "The term (al-ajal)."

* * *

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, He knows what is spoken aloud and He knows what you conceal. (110) And I do not know; perhaps it is a trial for you and enjoyment for a time.﴾ (111)

His saying, exalted is He, to His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ means: Say to these polytheists, "Indeed Allah knows the loud speech that you utter, and He knows what you conceal and do not utter aloud. Both what is hidden and what is apparent, both secret and public, are equal to Him; nothing of it is hidden from Him. So if He delays His punishment for you on account of what you conceal of associating others with Him or what you utter aloud, then I do not know what the reason is for which He delays that from you. Perhaps His delaying it from you, along with His promise to you, is a trial He intends for you, and so that you may enjoy your lives until a term He has appointed for you, which you will reach, whereupon His vengeance will then descend upon you."

The people of interpretation have said similarly to what we have said regarding this.

Mention of those who said that: Al-Qasim told us, he said: al-Husayn told us, he said: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Ata al-Khurasani, from Ibn Abbas, regarding ﴿And I do not know; perhaps it is a trial for you and enjoyment for a time﴾, he said: "Perhaps what I have brought near to you of the punishment and the Hour is delayed for you until your appointed time, and enjoyment for a time, so that my saying that becomes a trial for you."

Mention of those who said that: Al-Qasim told us, he said: al-Husayn told us, he said: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, regarding ﴿and I do not know whether what you are promised is near or far﴾, he said: "The term (al-ajal)."

* * *

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, He knows what is spoken aloud and He knows what you conceal. (110) And I do not know; perhaps it is a trial for you and enjoyment for a time.﴾ (111)

His saying, exalted is He, to His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ means: Say to these polytheists, "Indeed Allah knows the loud speech that you utter, and He knows what you conceal and do not utter aloud. Both what is hidden and what is apparent, both secret and public, are equal to Him; nothing of it is hidden from Him. So if He delays His punishment for you on account of what you conceal of associating others with Him or what you utter aloud, then I do not know what the reason is for which He delays that from you. Perhaps His delaying it from you, along with His promise to you, is a trial He intends for you, and so that you may enjoy your lives until a term He has appointed for you, which you will reach, whereupon His vengeance will then descend upon you."

The people of interpretation have said similarly to what we have said regarding this.

Mention of those who said that: Al-Qasim told us, he said: al-Husayn told us, he said: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Ata al-Khurasani, from Ibn Abbas, regarding ﴿And I do not know; perhaps it is a trial for you and enjoyment for a time﴾, he said: "Perhaps what I have brought near to you of the punishment and the Hour is delayed for you until your appointed time, and enjoyment for a time, so that my saying that becomes a trial for you."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 21, verse 112:

The explanation of His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿He said, "My Lord, judge with truth. And our Lord is the Most Merciful, the one sought for help against what you describe."﴾

His, the Exalted's, saying means: Say, O Muhammad: "O Lord, decide between me and those among my people who disbelieved me, who associated others with You and worshipped other than You, by sending down Your punishment and vengeance upon them." This is the truth that God, the Exalted, commanded His Prophet to ask his Lord to judge by. It is similar to His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿Our Lord, decide between us and our people with truth, and You are the best of deciders.﴾

Those who interpret the Qur'an have said what we have said on this matter.

Mention of those who said that:

⁕ Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj told me, from Ibn Juraj, who said: Ibn Abbas said regarding ﴿He said, "My Lord, judge with truth"﴾: "None judges with truth except God. But he only sought haste in this matter in the world, asking his Lord concerning his people."

⁕ Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah: that the Prophet ﷺ, whenever he witnessed fighting, would say: ﴿Lord, judge with truth.﴾

The reciters differed in the reading of this. The majority of the reciters of the major cities read ﴿Qul rabbi uhkum﴾ with a kasra on the ba' of rabb and a connected alif of uhkum, in the manner of supplication and request, except Abu Ja'far, who read the ba' of rabb with a damma, in the manner of addressing a singular noun (vocative), and except al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim, from whom it is narrated that he would read it: ﴿Rabbi ahkamu﴾, in the manner of an announcement that God is more judicious with truth than every judge, so he affirmed the yaʾ in rabb, hamzed the alif of ahkamu, and made ahkamu nominative as a predicate of "Rabb" (may He be blessed and exalted).

Our view on the correct reading in this matter is: connecting the ba' of rabb with a kasra and uhkum without hamzat al-qat' (cutting alif) of uhkum, as the reciters of the major cities read it, due to the consensus of the authoritative reciters upon it and the anomaly of whatever opposes it. As for al-Dahhak, the reading attributed to him includes an extra letter beyond the script of the mushafs, and that should not be added to it, while the meaning of the reading is sound without that addition. Some have claimed that the meaning of His saying ﴿Rabb, judge with truth﴾ is: "Say: My Lord, judge with Your true judgment," then the noun "judgment" which "the truth" qualifies was omitted, and "the truth" was put in its place. There is a justification for this, but what we have said is clearer and more consistent with what the people of interpretation have said, so we have chosen it.

* *

As for His saying ﴿And our Lord is the Most Merciful, the one sought for help against what you describe﴾:

His, the Exalted's, saying means: Say, O Muhammad: "Our Lord is the One who shows mercy to His servants and encompasses them with His blessing, the One whom I seek help from against you regarding what you say and describe of your words to me concerning what I have brought to you from God: ﴿This is none but a human being like you. Will you then submit to magic while you see?﴾ and your saying ﴿Rather, he has invented it; rather, he is a poet﴾, and regarding your lying against God, the Exalted, and your saying ﴿The Most Merciful has taken a son﴾. For He is able to change that easily, and to decide between me and you by hastening punishment upon you for what you describe of that."

End of the commentary on Surah al-Anbiya', peace be upon them.
